title.zh: 卷十七下 本紀第十七下: 文宗下
title.raw: 卷十七下 本紀第十七下: 文宗下 Volume 17 Annals 17: Wenzong 2

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 武宗至道昭肅孝皇帝諱炎，穆宗第五子，母曰宣懿皇后韋氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, posthumous title Zhidao Zhaosu Xiaoxiao, taboo name Yan, was Muzong's fifth son; his mother was Empress Xuanyi, née Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong—taboo Yan—was Muzong's fifth son, born of Empress Xuanyi Wei.

sentences.zh: 六月十二日生於東宮。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the sixth month he was born in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the Eastern Palace on the twelfth of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 三月，封潁王，本名瀍。

translations.literal: In the third month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ying; his original name was Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he became Prince of Ying, born Zhan.

sentences.zh: 開成中加開府儀同三司、檢校吏部尚書，依百官例，逐月給俸料。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era he was made Acting Grand Preceptor, Acting Minister of Personnel, and per the officials' precedent received monthly salary allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaicheng he held acting grand preceptor and personnel posts with monthly stipends.

sentences.zh: 初，文宗追悔莊恪太子殂不由道，乃以敬宗子陳王成美為皇太子，冬十月宣制，未遑冊禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenzong regretted that Crown Prince Zhuangke had died by improper means; he therefore made Jingzong's son Prince of Chen, Chengmei, crown prince. In the tenth month of winter the edict was proclaimed, but investiture rites were not yet performed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, repenting Zhuangke's death, named Chen Wang Chengmei heir in winter without full rites.

sentences.zh: 開成五年五年正月二日，文宗暴疾，宰相李玨、知樞密劉弘逸奉密旨，以皇太子監國。

translations.literal: On the second day of the first month of Kaicheng 5—year 5 duplicated in the source—Wenzong fell suddenly ill. Chief ministers Li Jue and Director of Palace Secrets Liu Hongyi received secret orders to have the crown prince supervise the state.
translations.idiomatic: On Kaicheng 5's first-month second day Wenzong fell gravely ill; Li Jue and Liu Hongyi set the crown prince to regency.

sentences.zh: 兩軍中尉仇士良、魚弘志矯詔迎潁王於十六宅，曰：「朕自嬰疾疹，有加無瘳，懼不能躬總萬機，日厘庶政。

translations.literal: The two armies' commandants Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi forged an edict to welcome the Prince of Ying from the Sixteen Mansions, saying: "Since I first fell ill with rash, it has worsened without recovery; I fear I cannot personally oversee the myriad affairs or daily order the multitude of policies.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi forged an edict fetching Prince of Ying Zhan: "Since my illness worsens I cannot rule in person—

sentences.zh: 稽於謨訓，謀及大臣，用建親賢，以貳神器。

translations.literal: In accord with counsels and instructions, consulting the great ministers, I establish a close worthy to share the sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: —so by counsel of ministers I set a kinsman to share the throne."

sentences.zh: 親弟潁王瀍昔在藩邸，與朕常同師訓，動成儀矩，性稟寬仁。

translations.literal: My younger brother Prince of Ying Zhan, formerly in his princely residence, often studied with me under the same tutors; his conduct always matched ritual measure, his nature endowed with generous kindness.
translations.idiomatic: "My brother Zhan studied with me, measured in ritual, generous by nature."

sentences.zh: 俾奉昌圖，必諧人欲。

translations.literal: Let him uphold the flourishing design—he will surely harmonize with human desire.
translations.idiomatic: "He will uphold the realm and win the people's assent."

sentences.zh: 可立為皇太弟，應軍國政事，便令權勾當。

translations.literal: He may be established as Younger Brother Heir; for military and state affairs let him provisionally manage them.
translations.idiomatic: "Make him Younger Brother Heir to manage state and army affairs."

sentences.zh: 百辟卿士，中外庶臣，宜竭乃心，輔成予志。

translations.literal: All hundred officials and ministers, inner and outer subjects, should exhaust your hearts to help fulfill my intent.
translations.idiomatic: "Let all officials exhaust themselves to fulfill my will."

sentences.zh: 陳王成美先立為皇太子，以其年尚沖幼，未漸師資，比日重難，不遑冊命，迴踐朱邸，式協至公，可復封陳王。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Chengmei was first established as crown prince; because his years were still tender and he had not yet advanced under tutors, and recent days were grave, there was no leisure for investiture—return to his crimson residence in accord with supreme fairness; he may again be enfeoffed Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: "Chen Wang Chengmei, too young for rites, returns to prince rank for fairness."

sentences.zh: 」是夜，士良統兵士于十六宅迎太弟赴少陽院，百官謁見於東宮思賢殿。

translations.literal: " That night Shiliang led soldiers at the Sixteen Mansions to welcome the Younger Brother Heir to Shaoyang Court; the hundred officials paid homage at the Eastern Palace's Suxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That night Qiu Shiliang installed the Younger Brother Heir at Shaoyang; officials bowed at Suxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 三日，仇士良收捕仙韶院副使尉遲璋殺之，屠其家。

translations.literal: On the third day Qiu Shiliang arrested and killed Xianzhao Court deputy Yuchi Zhang and slaughtered his household.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day Qiu Shiliang killed Yuchi Zhang of Xianzhao Court and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 四日，文宗崩，宣遺詔：皇太弟宜於柩前即皇帝位，宰相楊嗣復攝冢宰。

translations.literal: On the fourth day Wenzong died; the testamentary edict was proclaimed: the Younger Brother Heir should take the throne before the coffin; Chief Minister Yang Sifu was to act as chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth Wenzong died; the testament named the Younger Brother Heir and Yang Sifu chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 十四日，受冊于正殿，時年二十七。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day he received investiture in the main hall; he was twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth he was enthroned in the main hall at twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 陳王成美、安王溶殂于邸第。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Chengmei and Prince of An Rong died at their residences.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wang Chengmei and An Wang Rong died in their mansions.

sentences.zh: 初，楊賢妃有寵於文宗，而莊恪太子母王妃失寵怨望，為楊妃所譖，王妃死，太子廢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Consort Yang Xian had favor with Wenzong, while Zhuangke Crown Prince's mother the princess consort, losing favor, harbored resentment and was slandered by Consort Yang; the princess consort died and the crown prince was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang had turned Wenzong against Zhuangke's mother; the consort died and the heir fell.

sentences.zh: 及開成末年，帝多疾無嗣，賢妃請以安王溶嗣，帝謀于宰臣李玨，玨非之，乃立陳王。

translations.literal: By the late Kaicheng years the Emperor was often ill and without heirs; the worthy consort asked that Prince of An Rong succeed; the Emperor consulted Chief Minister Li Jue, who opposed it, and Chen Wang was established.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaicheng, childless, Wenzong favored An Wang until Li Jue blocked it for Chen Wang.

sentences.zh: 至是，仇士良立武宗，欲歸功於己，乃發安王舊事，故二王與賢妃皆死。

translations.literal: At this time Qiu Shiliang enthroned Wuzong and wished to claim the merit; he therefore exposed Prince of An's old affairs, so the two princes and the worthy consort all died.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang, enthroning Wuzong, exposed An Wang's past and killed both princes and Consort Yang.

sentences.zh: 二月，制穆宗妃韋氏追諡宣懿皇太后，帝之母也。

translations.literal: Second month: an order posthumously ennobled Muzong's consort Wei as Empress Dowager Xuanyi—the Emperor's mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Muzong's consort Wei became posthumous Empress Dowager Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 上御正殿，降德音，以開府、右軍中尉仇士良封楚國公，左軍中尉魚弘志為韓國公，太常卿崔鄲、戶部尚書判度支崔珙並本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The Emperor attended the main hall and issued a grace edict: Acting Grand Preceptor and Right Army Commandant Qiu Shiliang was enfeoffed Duke of Chu; Left Army Commandant Yu Hongzhi Duke of Han; Minister of Rites Cui Ye and Minister of Revenue overseeing finances Cui Gong all kept their posts and became Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: From the main hall Wuzong enfeoffed Qiu Shiliang Duke of Chu, Yu Hongzhi Duke of Han, and made Cui Ye and Cui Gong councillors.

sentences.zh: 敕二月十五日玄元皇帝降生日宜為降聖節，休假一日。

translations.literal: An order: the fifteenth day of the second month, the Descent Day of the Primordial Lord, should be the Descent-of-Sage Festival with one day of leave.
translations.idiomatic: The second month's fifteenth became the Descent-of-Sage holiday with one day off.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔宮人劉氏、王氏並為妃。

translations.literal: Third month: an edict made palace women Liu and Wang consorts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month palace women Liu and Wang were made consorts.

sentences.zh: 敕朔望入閣對刑法官，是日非便，宜停。

translations.literal: An order: on new and full moon days entering the hall to face penal officials—when inconvenient that day, stop.
translations.idiomatic: New- and full-moon audiences with penal officials were suspended when inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 五月，中書奏：六月十二日，皇帝載誕之辰，請以其日為慶陽節。

translations.literal: Fifth month: the Secretariat memorialized: the twelfth day of the sixth month is the day the Emperor was born; request that day as the Qingyang Festival.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Secretariat asked the sixth month's twelfth as Qingyang Festival.

sentences.zh: 祔宣懿太后于太廟。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanyi was enshrined in the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanyi entered the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 初，武宗欲啟穆宗陵祔葬，中書門下奏曰：「園陵已安，神道貴靜。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wuzong wished to open Muzong's tomb for joint burial; the Secretariat memorialized: "The park tomb is already settled; the spirit way values stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong wished to open Muzong's tomb for joint burial; the Secretariat objected:

sentences.zh: 光陵二十餘載，福陵則近又修崇。

translations.literal: Guang Mausoleum has stood more than twenty years; Fu Mausoleum was recently repaired and honored.
translations.idiomatic: "Guang Mausoleum has stood twenty years; Fu Mausoleum was just restored."

sentences.zh: 竊惟孝思，足彰嚴奉。

translations.literal: We consider that filial thought alone suffices to show solemn service.
translations.idiomatic: "Filial duty already shows solemn care."

sentences.zh: 今若再因合祔，須啟二陵，或慮聖靈不安，未合先旨。

translations.literal: If we now again undertake joint burial, we must open two tombs; we fear the sage spirit would be unsettled and it would not accord with the prior intent.
translations.idiomatic: "Reopening both tombs might disturb the spirits and breach prior intent."

sentences.zh: 又以陰陽避忌，亦有所疑。

translations.literal: Also yin-yang taboos give some doubt.
translations.idiomatic: "Yin-yang taboos also counsel caution."

sentences.zh: 不移福陵，實協典禮。

translations.literal: Not moving Fu Mausoleum truly accords with canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: "Leaving Fu Mausoleum untouched accords with rites."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " It stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the memorial; the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 就舊墳增築，名曰福陵。

translations.literal: On the old mound they added construction and named it Fu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: They enlarged the old mound and named it Fu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「准今年二月八日赦文，應京諸司勒留官，令本處剋留手力雜給與攝官者。

translations.literal: They also memorialized: "Per this year's second-month eighth-day amnesty text, retained officials of capital offices should have hand labor and miscellaneous allotments from their home offices deducted and given to acting officials.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that retained capital officials share hand labor pay with acting substitutes per the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 臣等檢詳，諸道正官料錢絕少，雜給手力即多，今正官勒留，亦管公事，料錢少於雜給，刻下事未得中。

translations.literal: We have examined in detail: regular officials' salary funds in the circuits are extremely few while miscellaneous hand labor is great; now regular officials are retained and also manage public affairs, yet salary is less than miscellaneous pay—the matter below is not balanced.
translations.idiomatic: "Regular salaries are thin while hand-pay is heavy—retained officers cannot balance both."

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，其正官料錢雜給等錢，望每貫割留二百文與攝官，餘並如舊。

translations.literal: We have discussed: for regular officials' salary and miscellaneous funds, we request two hundred cash per string be cut and given to acting officials; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: "Let two hundred cash per string of salary go to acting officers; the rest unchanged."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，制檢校禮部尚書、華州刺史陳夷行復為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Acting Minister of Rites and Huazhou prefect Chen Yixing was restored as Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chen Yixing returned as secretariat councillor.

sentences.zh: 八月十七日，葬文宗皇帝于章陵。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the eighth month Emperor Wenzong was buried at Zhang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth month's seventeenth Wenzong was buried at Zhang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 知樞密劉弘逸、薛季稜率禁軍護靈駕至陵所，二人素為文宗獎遇，仇士良惡之，心不自安，因是掌兵，欲倒戈誅士良、弘志。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Secrets Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling led the forbidden armies escorting the spirit carriage to the tomb; the two had long been favored by Wenzong; Qiu Shiliang hated them and was ill at ease; because they held troops they wished to turn swords and execute Shiliang and Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling, Wenzong's favorites escorting the bier, plotted to kill Qiu Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿使兵部尚書王起、山陵使崔稜覺其謀，先諭鹵簿諸軍。

translations.literal: Procession master Minister of War Wang Qi and tomb commissioner Cui Ling detected the plot and first instructed the procession troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi and Cui Ling uncovered the plot and warned the escort troops.

sentences.zh: 是日弘逸、季稜伏誅。

translations.literal: That day Hongyi and Jiling were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That day Liu Hongyi and Xue Jiling were executed.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事楊嗣復檢校吏部尚書、潭州刺史，充湖南都團練觀察使；

translations.literal: Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor Yang Sifu was made Acting Minister of Personnel and Tanzhou prefect, Hunan defense commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu was banished to Hunan as acting personnel minister;

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事李玨檢校兵部尚書、桂州刺史，充桂管防禦觀察等使；

translations.literal: Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor Li Jue Acting Minister of War and Guizhou prefect, Gui circuit defense commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue to Guizhou as acting war minister;

sentences.zh: 御史中丞裴夷直為杭州刺史：皆坐弘逸、季稜黨也。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pei Yizhi made Hangzhou prefect—all for the Hongyi and Jiling faction.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yizhi to Hangzhou—all punished as Hongyi's party.

sentences.zh: 易定軍亂，逐節度使陳君賞。

translations.literal: Yiding army mutinied and expelled military commissioner Chen Junshang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yiding army expelled Chen Junshang.

sentences.zh: 君賞鳩合豪傑數百人，復入城，盡誅謀亂兵士，軍城復安。

translations.literal: Junshang gathered several hundred stalwarts, re-entered the city, and executed all mutinous soldiers; the garrison city was again secure.
translations.idiomatic: Junshang rallied hundreds, retook the city, and slaughtered the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 九月，以淮南節度使、檢校尚書左僕射李德裕為吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事，尋兼門下侍郎；

translations.literal: September: Huainan military commissioner Acting Minister of the Left Li Deyu was made Minister of Personnel and Grand Councillor, soon also Secretariat Vice Director;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Li Deyu left Huainan for the Grand Council and soon the secretariat;

sentences.zh: 以宣武軍節度使、檢校吏部尚書、汴州刺史李紳代德裕鎮淮南。

translations.literal: Xuanwu military commissioner Acting Minister of Personnel and Bianzhou prefect Li Shen replaced Deyu in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen replaced him at Huainan.

sentences.zh: 帝在藩時，頗好道術修攝之事，是秋，召道士趙歸真等八十一人入禁中，於三殿修金籙道場。

translations.literal: While in his princely residence the Emperor had greatly favored Daoist cultivation; that autumn he summoned eighty-one Daoists including Zhao Guizhen into the inner palace and in the Three Halls established a Golden Register ritual arena.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wuzong summoned eighty-one Daoists including Zhao Guizhen for Golden Register rites in the Three Halls.

sentences.zh: 帝幸三殿，於九天壇親受法籙。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited the Three Halls and at the Nine Heavens altar personally received the ritual registers.
translations.idiomatic: He received ritual registers at the Nine Heavens altar.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺王哲上疏，言王業之初，不宜崇信過當，疏奏不省。

translations.literal: Right Reminder Wang Zhe memorialized that at the founding of the royal enterprise one should not believe excessively; the memorial was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhe warned against excessive faith in Daoism; the court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，鹽鐵轉運使奏江淮已南請復稅茶，從之。

translations.literal: November: the Salt and Transport commissioner memorialized that south of the Yangzi and Huai tea tax should be restored; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the tea tax south of the Yangzi and Huai was restored.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使何進滔卒，三軍推其子重霸知留後事。

translations.literal: Weibo military commissioner He Jintao died; the three armies made his son Chongba provisional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He Jintao died; the Weibo armies backed his son Chongba.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年會昌元年正月壬寅朔。

translations.literal: Huichang 1, first month, renyin new moon—year Huichang 1 duplicated in the source.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang 1 opened on renyin.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，有事於郊廟，禮畢，御丹鳳樓，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On gengxu he performed suburban and ancestral rites; when the rites ended he ascended Danfeng Tower, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu suburban rites ended with universal amnesty and the new era from Danfeng Tower.

sentences.zh: 二月壬寅，以淮南節度使、檢校吏部尚書李紳為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Second month, renyin: Huainan military commissioner Acting Minister of Personnel Li Shen was made Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Shen joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 中書奏：「南宮六曹皆有職分，各責官業，即事不因循。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "The Six Boards of the Southern Palace each have duties and should answer for their offices without dragging affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat urged the Six Boards to stop passing army petitions to idle clerks:

sentences.zh: 近者戶部度支，多是諸軍奏請，本司郎吏束手閑居。

translations.literal: Recently Revenue and Expenditure were mostly army petitions; this ministry's clerks sat idle with hands bound.
translations.idiomatic: "Revenue and Expenditure had become a mailbox for army requests while clerks sat idle."

sentences.zh: 今後請祗令本行分判，委中書門下簡擇公幹才器相當者轉授。

translations.literal: Hereafter let only this line divide cases; the Secretariat and Chancellery should select men of public talent and capacity to transfer appointments."
translations.idiomatic: "Let each board judge its own docket with councillors picking capable men." Thus ended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸昆明池。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited Kunming Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited Kunming Pool.

sentences.zh: 賜仇士良紀功碑，詔右僕射李程為其文。

translations.literal: A merit stele was granted Qiu Shiliang; an order had Right Vice Director Li Cheng compose the text.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang received a merit stele composed by Li Cheng.

sentences.zh: 三月，貶湖南觀察使楊嗣復潮州司馬，桂管觀察使李玨端州司馬，杭州刺史裴夷直驩州司戶。

translations.literal: Third month: Hunan observation commissioner Yang Sifu was demoted Chaozhou vice prefect; Gui observation commissioner Li Jue Duanzhou vice prefect; Hangzhou prefect Pei Yizhi Huanzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yang Sifu, Li Jue, and Pei Yizhi were driven deeper into exile.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李德裕進位司空。

translations.literal: Chief minister Li Deyu was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三月壬申，宰相李德裕、陳夷行、崔珙、李紳等奏：「憲宗皇帝有恢復中興之功，請為百代不遷之廟。

translations.literal: Third month, renshen: Grand councillors Li Deyu, Chen Yixing, Cui Gong, Li Shen, and others memorialized: "Emperor Xianzong had the merit of restoring the central revival; request a temple that would never be moved for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the councillors asked an eternal temple for Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「所論至當。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The discussion is entirely apt."
translations.idiomatic: "Entirely apt," said the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」續議之，事竟不行。

translations.literal: " Discussion continued, but in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Debate continued, but the proposal failed.

sentences.zh: 贈故中書令、晉國公裴度太師。

translations.literal: The late Chief Councillor and Duke of Jin Pei Du was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 山南東道蝗害稼。

translations.literal: Shannan East circuit locusts harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 造靈符應聖院於龍首池。

translations.literal: The Spirit Talisman Responsive Sage Cloister was built at Dragon Head Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Head Pool gained the Spirit Talisman Responsive Sage Cloister.

sentences.zh: 四月辛丑，敕：「《憲宗實錄》舊本未備，宜令史官重修進內。

translations.literal: Fourth month, xinchou: an order: "The old Veritable Records of Xianzong are incomplete; historians should revise and submit within."
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Xianzong's Veritable Records were ordered revised.

sentences.zh: 其舊本不得注破，候新撰成同進。

translations.literal: The old text may not be annotated as void; wait until the new compilation is finished and submit together."
translations.idiomatic: "Submit the new text with the old, unmarked void."

sentences.zh: 」時李德裕先請不遷憲宗廟，為議者沮之，復恐或書其父不善之事，故復請改撰實錄，朝野非之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Deyu had first asked that Xianzong's temple not be moved; debaters blocked it; he again feared they might record his father's faults, so he again asked to rewrite the Veritable Records—the court and country disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, blocked on Xianzong's temple, sought to rewrite the records to shield his father—drawing public scorn.

sentences.zh: 五月辛未，中書門下奏：「據《六典》，隋置諫議大夫七人，從四品上。

translations.literal: Fifth month, xinwei: the Secretariat memorialized: "Per the Six Offices Canon, Sui established seven Remonstrance officials at Vice Fourth Rank upper.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Secretariat asked to restore remonstrance ranks per the Six Offices Canon:

sentences.zh: 大曆二年，升門下侍郎為正三品，兩省遂闕四品。

translations.literal: In Dali 2 the Secretariat Vice Director was raised to Regular Third Rank; the two departments then lacked Fourth Rank posts.
translations.idiomatic: "Since Dali 2 vice directors rose to third rank, both departments lack fourth-rank posts."

sentences.zh: 建官之道，有所未周。

translations.literal: The way of establishing offices is somewhat incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: "Office structure remains incomplete."

sentences.zh: 詩云『袞職有闕，仲山甫補之』。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "The king's duties have gaps—Zhong Shanfu mends them."
translations.idiomatic: "As the Odes say, royal gaps need ministers to mend them."

sentences.zh: 周、漢大臣，願入禁闥，補過拾遺。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han great ministers wished to enter the forbidden inner gates to remedy faults and gather remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou and Han ministers entered the inner gates to remonstrate."

sentences.zh: 張衡為侍郎，常居帷幄，從容諷諫。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng as Vice Director often dwelt within the curtains and remonstrated at ease.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang Heng remonstrated from within the curtains."

sentences.zh: 此皆大臣之任，故其秩峻，其任重，則敬其言而行其道。

translations.literal: These are all great ministers' tasks; therefore their rank is lofty and their burden heavy—then respect their words and walk their way.
translations.idiomatic: "Great ministers need lofty rank to make their words weighty."

sentences.zh: 況蹇諤之地，宜老成之人，秩未優崇，則難用耆德。

translations.literal: Moreover the place of blunt speech should have seasoned men; if rank is not honored, it is hard to use elders of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: "Blunt remonstrance requires honored elders."

sentences.zh: 其諫議大夫望依隋氏舊制，升為從四品，分為左右，以備兩省四品之闕。

translations.literal: The Remonstrance officials should follow Sui's old system, be raised to Vice Fourth Rank, divided left and right, to fill the two departments' Fourth Rank gap.
translations.idiomatic: "Restore remonstrance to vice fourth rank, left and right."

sentences.zh: 向後與丞郎出入迭用，以重其選。

translations.literal: Hereafter rotate with directors and vice directors in and out to weight the selection.
translations.idiomatic: "Rotate remonstrance with director posts to weight selection."

sentences.zh: 又御史中丞為大夫之貳，緣大夫秩崇，官不常置，中丞為憲臺之長。

translations.literal: Also the Censor Vice Director is second to the Chief Censor; because the Chief Censor's rank is lofty the post is not always filled—the Vice Director is head of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: "The censor vice director should match other second-in-command fourth ranks."

sentences.zh: 今寺監、少卿、少監、司業、少尹並為寺署之貳，皆為四品。

translations.literal: Now directorates, vice directors, vice ministers, vice supervisors, academicians, and vice magistrates are all seconds in their offices, all Fourth Rank.
translations.idiomatic: "Temple and directorate seconds are fourth rank."

sentences.zh: 中丞官名至重，見秩未崇，望升為從四品。

translations.literal: The Vice Director's title is weighty yet its seen rank is not honored; we request it be raised to Vice Fourth Rank."
translations.idiomatic: "Raise the censor vice director to vice fourth rank." Thus ended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 六月，有禿鶖鳥集於禁苑。

translations.literal: Sixth month: bald vultures gathered in the forbidden park.
translations.idiomatic: Bald vultures gathered in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 庚子夜五更，小流星五十餘旁午流散。

translations.literal: On gengzi night at the fifth watch more than fifty small meteors crisscrossed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi night fifty small meteors crisscrossed the sky.

sentences.zh: 制以魏博兵馬留後何重霸檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史，充天雄軍節度使，仍賜名重順。

translations.literal: An order made Weibo army provisional commander He Chongba Acting Minister of Works and Wezhou grand protector, full Tianxiong military commissioner, and still granted the name Chongshun.
translations.idiomatic: He Chongba became Tianxiong commander and was renamed Chongshun.

sentences.zh: 中書奏請依姚璹故事，宰相每月修時政記送史館，從之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat requested that per Yao Shuan's precedent grand councillors monthly compile a record of current policy and send it to the History Office; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councillors were ordered to send monthly policy records to the History Office.

sentences.zh: 以衡山道士劉玄靖為銀青光祿大夫，充崇玄館學士，賜號廣成先生，令與道士趙歸真於禁中修法籙。

translations.literal: Hengshan Daoist Liu Xuanjing was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master, Chongxuan Hall academician, granted the style Lord of Broad Completion, and ordered with Zhao Guizhen to perform ritual registers in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanjing joined Zhao Guizhen performing registers in the palace.

sentences.zh: 左補闕劉彥謨上疏切諫，貶彥謨為河南府戶曹。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Liu Yanmo memorialized sharply in remonstrance; Yanmo was demoted Henan prefecture registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanmo's sharp remonstrance earned a Henan registrar post.

sentences.zh: 敕：「自前中外上封論事，有所糾舉，則請留中。

translations.literal: An order: "Formerly when inner and outer persons memorialized on affairs with impeachments, they asked to retain at court.
translations.idiomatic: An order ended "retain at court" petitions:

sentences.zh: 今後並云『請付御史臺』，不得云『留中不下』。

translations.literal: Hereafter all shall say "Please deliver to the Censorate" and may not say "Retain at court without release."
translations.idiomatic: "Say deliver to the Censorate, not retain at court."

sentences.zh: 如事關軍國，理須宥密，不在此限。

translations.literal: If the matter concerns military and state affairs and reason requires secrecy, it is not within this limit.
translations.idiomatic: "State secrets remain excepted."

sentences.zh: 如臺司勘當後，若得事實，必獎奉公。

translations.literal: After the Censorate investigates, if facts are found, public service must be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: "Proven charges merit reward for public service."

sentences.zh: 苟涉加誣，必當反問。

translations.literal: If it involves false accusation, there must be counter-inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: "False accusation brings counter-inquiry."

sentences.zh: 告示中外，明知此意。

translations.literal: Proclaim to inner and outer so all clearly know this intent."
translations.idiomatic: "Let all know this rule." Thus ended the edict.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 七月己巳，北方有流星，經天良久。

translations.literal: Seventh month, jisi: in the north a meteor crossed the sky for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi a meteor crossed the northern sky for a long while.

sentences.zh: 關東大蝗傷稼。

translations.literal: East of the Pass great locusts harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged the eastern plain.

sentences.zh: 襄、郢、江左大水。

translations.literal: Xiang, Ying, and the lands east of the river suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Floods struck Xiang, Ying, and the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 彗復出室壁之間。

translations.literal: The comet again appeared between Room and Wall.
translations.idiomatic: The comet returned between Room and Wall.

sentences.zh: 八月，回鶻烏介可汗遣使告難，言本國為黠戛斯所攻，故可汗死，今部人推為可汗。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the Uighur Wujie qaghan sent envoys reporting distress, saying his state was attacked by the Kirghiz, the former qaghan died, and the tribes now made him qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Uighur Wujie reported Kirghiz attacks and his election as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 緣本國破散，今奉太和公主南投大國。

translations.literal: Because the state was broken and scattered, he now escorts Princess Taihe south to the great state.
translations.idiomatic: Broken and scattered, he escorted Princess Taihe south to Tang.

sentences.zh: 時烏介至塞上，大首領嗢沒斯與赤心宰相相攻，殺赤心，率其部下數千帳近西城。

translations.literal: At the time Wujie reached the frontier; great chief Wamosi and the Red-Heart chancellor fought, killing Red-Heart and leading several thousand tents near the western city.
translations.idiomatic: At the frontier Wamosi killed the Red-Heart chancellor and led thousands of tents westward.

sentences.zh: 天德防禦使田牟以聞。

translations.literal: Tiande defense commissioner Tian Mou reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Mou of Tiande reported it.

sentences.zh: 烏介又令其相頡干迦斯上表，借天德城以安公主，仍乞糧儲牛羊供給。

translations.literal: Wujie also had his chancellor Qiegan Jiasi memorialize, borrowing Tiande city to settle the princess, still begging grain stores and cattle and sheep for supply.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie asked to borrow Tiande for the princess and begged grain and herds.

sentences.zh: 詔金吾大將軍王會、宗正少卿李師偃往其牙宣慰，令放公主入朝，賑粟二萬石。

translations.literal: An edict sent Gold Crow general Wang Hui and Court of Imperial Clan vice director Li Shiyan to his camp to console, ordering release of the princess to court, and relief grain twenty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui and Li Shiyan were sent to console Wujie, free the princess, and grant twenty thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 九月，幽州軍亂，逐其帥史元忠，推牙將陳行泰為留後。

translations.literal: September: Youzhou army mutinied, expelled its commander Shi Yuanzhong, and made barracks general Chen Xingtai provisional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Youzhou expelled Shi Yuanzhong for Chen Xingtai.

sentences.zh: 三軍上章請符節，朝旨未許。

translations.literal: The three armies submitted a memorial requesting credentials; court orders were not yet granted.
translations.idiomatic: The armies petitioned for credentials; the court withheld them.

sentences.zh: 十月，幽州雄武軍使張絳遣軍吏吳仲舒入朝，言行泰慘虐，不可處將帥之任，請以鎮軍加討，許之。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Youzhou Xiongwu commissioner Zhang Jiang sent army clerk Wu Zhongshu to court, saying Xingtai was cruel and could not hold a commander's post, requesting the garrison army be added for punishment; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhang Jiang denounced Xingtai's cruelty and won permission to attack.

sentences.zh: 十月，誅行泰，遂以絳知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Xingtai was executed; Jiang was then made provisional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xingtai was executed; Zhang Jiang took command.

sentences.zh: 車駕校獵咸陽。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage hunted at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hunted at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁酉朔。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, dingyou new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh month opened on dingyou.

sentences.zh: 壬寅夜，大星東北流，其光燭地，有聲如雷，山崩石隕。

translations.literal: On renyin night a great star flowed northeast; its light lit the ground; there was sound like thunder; mountains collapsed and stones fell.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin night a great fire-star lit the northeast with thunder; mountains collapsed.

sentences.zh: 其彗起於室，凡五十六日而滅。

translations.literal: The comet arose in Room; in all fifty-six days it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The comet in Room lasted fifty-six days.

sentences.zh: 太和公主遣使入朝，言烏介自稱可汗，乞行策命，緣初至漠南，乞降使宣慰，從之。

translations.literal: Princess Taihe sent envoys to court saying Wujie styled himself qaghan and begged investiture patent; because he had first reached south of the desert he begged envoys to console—approved.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taihe asked patents for Wujie; envoys were sent to console him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，中書門下奏修實錄體例：「舊錄有載禁中之言。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: the Secretariat memorialized rules for revising the Veritable Records: "The old record carries words from within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Secretariat tightened Veritable Records rules:

sentences.zh: 伏以君上與宰臣、公卿言事，皆須眾所聞見，方可書於史冊。

translations.literal: We consider that when the sovereign speaks with councillors and ministers, all must hear before it may be written in the historical book.
translations.idiomatic: "Only words heard by many may enter the history."

sentences.zh: 且禁中之語，在外何知，或得之傳聞，多涉於浮妄，便形史筆，實累鴻猷。

translations.literal: Moreover words within the forbidden—how would the outer know? If obtained by rumor they often involve the floating and false; to shape them in the history pen truly burdens great design.
translations.idiomatic: "Inner words known only by rumor must be cut."

sentences.zh: 今後實錄中如有此色，並請刊削。

translations.literal: Hereafter if the Veritable Records has such color, all request excision.
translations.idiomatic: "Cut such passages hereafter."

sentences.zh: 又宰臣與公卿論事，行與不行，須有明據。

translations.literal: Also when councillors and ministers debate affairs, whether carried out or not there must be clear evidence.
translations.idiomatic: "Debates need public proof of outcome."

sentences.zh: 或奏請允愜，必見褒稱；

translations.literal: If a memorial is approved and pleasing, praise must appear;
translations.idiomatic: "Approved plans must show praise;"

sentences.zh: 或所論乖僻，因有懲責。

translations.literal: if what is discussed is perverse, there will be punishment.
translations.idiomatic: "perverse ones punishment."

sentences.zh: 在藩鎮上表，必有批答，居要官啟事者，自有著明，並須昭然在人耳目。

translations.literal: In frontier commands memorials must have written replies; key officials presenting affairs have their own clarity—all must shine in human eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: "Frontier memorials need written replies visible to all."

sentences.zh: 或取捨存於堂案，或與奪形於詔敕，前代史書所載奏義，罔不由此。

translations.literal: Whether keep or discard rests in hall records, or grant and seize appears in edicts—former dynasties' histories record memorials and meaning without exception thus.
translations.idiomatic: "Hall records and edicts must show decisions openly."

sentences.zh: 近見實錄多載密疏，言不彰於朝聽，事不顯於當時，得自其家，未足為信。

translations.literal: Recently the Veritable Records often carry secret memorials—words not proclaimed in court hearing, affairs not shown at the time, obtained from their families, insufficient for trust.
translations.idiomatic: "Secret memorials from families must not be recorded."

sentences.zh: 今後實錄所載章奏，並須朝廷共知者，方得紀述，密疏並請不載。

translations.literal: Hereafter Veritable Records may record memorials only if the court jointly knew them; secret memorials all request not to be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: "Record only what the court jointly knew."

sentences.zh: 如此則理必可法，人皆向公，愛憎之志不行，褒貶之言必信。

translations.literal: Thus principle can be law, all turn to fairness, love and hate cannot run, praise and blame words will be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus history stays fair and trusted." Thus ended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 李德裕奏改修《憲宗實錄》所載吉甫不善之迹，鄭亞希旨削之。

translations.literal: Li Deyu memorialized to revise the Veritable Records' record of Jifu's faults; Zheng Ya to please the intent cut them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had Zheng Ya cut Jifu's faults from Xianzong's records.

sentences.zh: 德裕更此條奏，以掩其迹。

translations.literal: Deyu changed this memorial clause to cover his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu rewrote the rule to hide his hand.

sentences.zh: 搢紳謗議，武宗頗知之。

translations.literal: Gentry slandered; Wuzong knew it fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry murmured; Wuzong knew.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年二年春正月丙申朔，以撫王紘為開府儀同三司、幽州大都督府長史，充幽州盧龍節度大使。

translations.literal: Huichang 2, spring, first month, bingchen new moon—year Huichang 2 duplicated—Prince of Fu Hong was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Youzhou grand protector, full Youzhou Lulong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang 2 opened with Prince of Fu Hong made Lulong commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以雄武軍使張絳檢校左散騎常侍，兼幽州左司馬，知兩使留後，仍賜名仲武。

translations.literal: Xiongwu commissioner Zhang Jiang was made Acting Left Cavalier and concurrent Youzhou left marshal, provisional commander of both commissions, still granted the name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiang became Zhongwu, provisional Lulong commander.

sentences.zh: 中書奏百官議九宮壇本大祠，請降為中祠。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized officials' debate: the Nine Palaces altar was originally a great sacrifice; request lowering it to middle sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Palaces altar was lowered from great to middle sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔珙、陳夷行奏定左右僕射上事儀注。

translations.literal: Grand councillors Cui Gong and Chen Yixing memorialized fixing the protocol for left and right vice directors presenting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong and Chen Yixing fixed vice-director audience protocol.

sentences.zh: 二月丙寅，中書奏：「准元和七年敕，河東、鳳翔、鄜坊、邠寧等道州縣官，令戶部加給課料錢歲六萬二千五百貫。

translations.literal: Second month, bingyin: the Secretariat memorialized: "Per the Yuanhe 7 order, Hedong, Fengxiang, Bin-Fang, and Bin-Ning circuit prefects were to receive supplemental salary funds of sixty-two thousand five hundred strings yearly from Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Secretariat asked steady supplemental pay for frontier prefects:

sentences.zh: 吏部出得平留官數百員，時以為當。

translations.literal: Personnel released several hundred balanced retention posts; at the time it was thought fitting.
translations.idiomatic: "Personnel once released hundreds of balanced posts when pay was steady."

sentences.zh: 自後戶部支給零碎不時，觀察使乃別將破用，徒有加給，不及官人，所以選人憚遠，不樂注受。

translations.literal: Since then Revenue paid in fragments not on time; observation commissioners then diverted broken funds—empty addition without reaching officials, so candidates feared distance and would not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: "Now fragmented pay never reaches appointees, deterring frontier service."

sentences.zh: 伏望令部都與實物，及時支遣。

translations.literal: We request the ministry deliver in kind and pay on time.
translations.idiomatic: "Deliver supplemental pay in kind on time."

sentences.zh: 諸道委觀察判官知給受，專判此案，隨月支給，年終計帳申戶部。

translations.literal: Let circuits' observation vice commissioners manage distribution, solely judge this case, pay monthly, year-end account to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: "Observation vice commissioners should pay monthly and account yearly."

sentences.zh: 又赴選官人多京債，到任填還，致其貪求，罔不由此。

translations.literal: Also appointees often owe capital debts; on reaching post they repay, so their greed—none is not from this.
translations.idiomatic: "Capital debts drive frontier greed."

sentences.zh: 今年三銓，於前件州府得官者，許連狀相保，戶部各借兩月加給料錢，至支時折下。

translations.literal: This year's three selections—for those gaining posts in the aforesaid prefectures, permit joint bonds; Revenue lends two months supplemental salary, deducted at payout.
translations.idiomatic: "Lend two months supplemental pay to new frontier appointees."

sentences.zh: 所冀初官到任，不帶息債，衣食稍足，可責清廉。

translations.literal: We hope new officials reaching post carry no interest debt, food and clothing somewhat sufficient, and may be charged with integrity."
translations.idiomatic: "So new appointees arrive debt-free and able to serve cleanly." Thus ended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 太子太師致仕蕭俛卒。

translations.literal: Retired Grand Preceptor Xiao Fang died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fang, retired grand preceptor, died.

sentences.zh: 牂柯、南詔蠻遣使入朝。

translations.literal: Zangke and Nanzhao barbarians sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zangke and Nanzhao sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣使冊迴紇烏介可汗。

translations.literal: Third month: envoys were sent to invest the Uighur Wujie qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month envoys invested Wujie qaghan.

sentences.zh: 以振武麟勝節度使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射、單于大都護、兼御史大夫、彭城郡開國公、食邑二千戶劉沔可檢校右僕射，兼太原尹、北京留守，充河東節度、管內觀察處置等使，代苻澈。

translations.literal: Zhenwu Lin-Sheng military commissioner Liu Mian was made Acting Right Vice Director, concurrent Taiyuan prefect, Beijing regent, full Hedong military commissioner and circuit observation commissioner, replacing Fu Che.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian replaced Fu Che at Hedong with a massive commission.

sentences.zh: 時迴紇在天德，命沔以太原之師討之。

translations.literal: At the time the Uighur were at Tiande; Mian was ordered to take Taiyuan troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was ordered to strike the Uighur at Tiande with Taiyuan troops.

sentences.zh: 四月乙丑朔，光祿大夫、守司空、兼門下侍郎、平章事李德裕，銀青光祿大夫、守右僕射、門下侍郎、平章事崔珙，銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、同平章事李紳，金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、兼太子太保牛僧孺等上章，請加尊號曰仁聖文武至神大孝皇帝。

translations.literal: Fourth month, yichou new moon: Acting Minister of Works and Secretariat Vice Director Li Deyu, Acting Right Vice Director and Secretariat Vice Director Cui Gong, Secretariat Vice Director Li Shen, Acting Minister of Education Niu Sengru, and others submitted a memorial requesting the honorific title Benevolent Sagely Martial Civil Ultimate Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the councillors sought the honorific Benevolent Sagely Martial Civil Ultimate Filial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，御宣政殿受冊。

translations.literal: On wuyin he received the patent at Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Wuzong received the honorific at Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 是月九日雨，至十四日轉甚，乃改用二十三日。

translations.literal: That month rain from the ninth to the fourteenth grew worse, so they changed to the twenty-third.
translations.idiomatic: Rain forced the rites from the ninth to the twenty-third.

sentences.zh: 時有纖人告中尉仇士良，言宰相作赦書，欲減削禁軍衣糧馬草料。

translations.literal: At the time a petty man informed Commandant Qiu Shiliang that the councillors were drafting an amnesty to cut forbidden-army clothing, grain, and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: A informer told Qiu Shiliang the amnesty would cut army rations.

sentences.zh: 士良怒曰：「必若有此，軍人須至樓前作鬧。

translations.literal: Shiliang angrily said: "If truly so, the soldiers must riot before the tower."
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang threatened a tower-front mutiny.

sentences.zh: 」宰相李德裕等知之，請開延英訴其事。

translations.literal: Grand councillor Li Deyu and others learned it and requested Extended Ying to plead the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu pleaded the case in Extended Ying.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「奸人之詞也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The words of a villain."
translations.idiomatic: "Villain's talk," said the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」召兩軍中尉諭之曰：「赦書出自朕意，不由宰相，況未施行，公等安得此言？

translations.literal: He summoned both army commandants and instructed: "The amnesty comes from my intent, not the councillors; moreover it is not yet implemented—how can you say this?"
translations.idiomatic: He told the commandants the amnesty was his own and unreleased.

sentences.zh: 」士良惶恐謝之。

translations.literal: Shiliang fearfully apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang apologized in fear.

sentences.zh: 是日晴霽。

translations.literal: That day cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The sky cleared that day.

sentences.zh: 中書奏：「元日御含元殿，百官就列，唯宰相及兩省官皆未開扇前立於欄檻之內，及扇開，便侍立於御前。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "On New Year's day at Hanyuan Hall the hundred officials take formation; only councillors and both-department officials stand inside the railing before the fans open; when fans open they attend before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat asked councillors to bow with the hundred officials at New Year:

sentences.zh: 三朝大慶，萬邦稱賀，唯宰相侍臣同介胄武夫，竟不拜至尊而退，酌於禮意，事未得中。

translations.literal: Three great morning felicitations, ten thousand states congratulate—only councillors and attending ministers stand like armored warriors, finally not bowing to the supreme before withdrawing—compared to ritual intent, the matter is not balanced.
translations.idiomatic: "Councillors alone stood like guards without bowing—against ritual."

sentences.zh: 臣等請御殿日昧爽，宰相、兩省官鬥班於香案前，俟扇開，通事贊兩省官再拜，拜訖，升殿侍立。

translations.literal: We request on audience days at dawn councillors and both-department officials queue before the incense table; when fans open, the usher praises both-department officials to bow again; after bowing ascend and attend."
translations.idiomatic: "Let councillors queue and bow before ascending." Thus ended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 天德奏，迴紇族帳侵擾部內。

translations.literal: Tiande reported Uighur tribal tents harassing within the command.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande reported Uighur harassment.

sentences.zh: 敕：「勸課種桑，比有敕命，如能增數，每歲申聞。

translations.literal: An order: "Encouraging mulberry planting—there have been orders; if numbers increase, report yearly.
translations.idiomatic: An order forbade felling mulberry for fuel:

sentences.zh: 比知並無遵行，恣加翦伐，列於鄽市，賣作薪蒸。

translations.literal: We know none obey; they recklessly cut, display in markets, and sell as firewood.
translations.idiomatic: "Officials had ignored mulberry orders, selling trees as firewood."

sentences.zh: 自今州縣所由，切宜禁斷。

translations.literal: From now prefectural agents must strictly forbid."
translations.idiomatic: "Strictly forbid it hereafter." Thus ended the edict.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 五月，敕慶陽節百官率醵外，別賜錢三百貫，以備素食合宴，仍令京兆府供帳，不用追集坊市樂人。

translations.literal: Fifth month: an order for Qingyang Festival besides officials' pooled gifts additionally granted three hundred strings for vegetarian joint banquet, still ordering Jingzhao to supply tents without pressing market musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyang Festival gained three hundred strings for banquets without pressed musicians.

sentences.zh: 天德軍使田牟奏：迴紇大將嗢沒斯與多覽將軍將吏二千六百人請降，遣中人齎詔慰勞之。

translations.literal: Tiande commissioner Tian Mou memorialized: Uighur great general Wamosi and Duolan general and officers twenty-six hundred requested surrender; the court sent envoys with edicts to console.
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi and twenty-six hundred Uighur officers sought surrender.

sentences.zh: 宰相李德裕兼守司徒。

translations.literal: Grand councillor Li Deyu concurrently Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu also became acting minister of education.

sentences.zh: 太子太師致仕鄭覃卒。

translations.literal: Retired Grand Preceptor Zheng Qin died.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qin, retired grand preceptor, died.

sentences.zh: 六月甲子朔，火星犯木。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jiazi new moon: Mars transgressed Wood.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth month opened with Mars transgressing Wood.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，太白犯東井。

translations.literal: On bingyin Venus transgressed the eastern well.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Venus crossed the eastern well.

sentences.zh: 迴紇降將嗢沒斯將吏二千六百餘人至京師。

translations.literal: Uighur surrendering general Wamosi and officers more than twenty-six hundred reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi and twenty-six hundred Uighur reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 制以嗢沒斯檢校工部尚書，充歸義軍使，封懷化郡王，仍賜姓名曰李思忠；

translations.literal: An order made Wamosi Acting Minister of Works, full Return-to-Righteousness commissioner, enfeoffed Duke of Huaihua, still granted the surname Li and name Sizhong;
translations.idiomatic: Wamosi became Li Sizhong, Duke of Huaihua, Return-to-Righteousness commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以迴紇宰相受耶勿為歸義軍副使、檢校右散騎常侍，賜姓名曰李弘順。

translations.literal: the Uighur chancellor Shouyewu was made Return-to-Righteousness vice commissioner, Acting Right Cavalier, granted the surname Li and name Hongshun.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyewu became Li Hongshun, his vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七月，嵐州人田滿川據郡叛，劉沔誅之。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Lanzhou man Tian Manchuan rebelled holding the prefecture; Liu Mian executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian crushed Tian Manchuan's Lanzhou revolt.

sentences.zh: 八月，迴紇烏介可汗過天德，至杷頭烽北，俘掠雲、朔北川，詔劉沔出師守雁門諸關。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Uighur Wujie qaghan passed Tiande to north of Batou beacon, plundering Yun and Shuo north of the river; Liu Mian was ordered to march guarding Yanmen passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie raided north of the river; Liu Mian guarded Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 迴紇首領屈武降幽州，授左武衛將軍同正。

translations.literal: Uighur chief Quwu surrendered to Youzhou and was made Left Martial Guard general on probation.
translations.idiomatic: Quwu surrendered at Youzhou and became a probationary general.

sentences.zh: 詔以迴紇犯邊，漸浸內地，或攻或守，於理何安？

translations.literal: An edict: because the Uighur violated the border and gradually soaked the inner lands, whether attack or defense—by principle what is secure?
translations.idiomatic: The court asked whether to attack or merely defend the Uighur.

sentences.zh: 令少師牛僧孺、陳夷行與公卿集議可否以聞。

translations.literal: Order Junior Preceptor Niu Sengru and Chen Yixing with public ministers to gather debate on feasibility and report.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru and Chen Yixing were told to debate policy.

sentences.zh: 僧孺曰：「今百僚議狀，以固守關防，伺其可擊則用兵。

translations.literal: Sengru said: "Now the hundred officials' memorials debate holding firm pass defenses and striking when possible with troops."
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru favored holding passes and striking when possible.

sentences.zh: 」宰相李德裕議：「以迴紇所恃者嗢沒、赤心耳，今已離叛，其強弱之勢可見。

translations.literal: Grand councillor Li Deyu debated: "What the Uighur rely on are only Wamosi and Red-Heart; now they have split—their strong and weak situation is visible.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu argued the Uighur had lost Wamosi and Red-Heart and could be crushed.

sentences.zh: 戎人獷悍，不顧成敗，以失二將，乘忿入侵，出師急擊，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Barbarians are fierce and heed not success or failure; having lost two generals they invade in rage—urgent strike and breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: "Strike now while they rage without their generals."

sentences.zh: 守險示弱，虜無由退。

translations.literal: Holding peril and showing weakness—the barbarians have no reason to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: "Defensive weakness only emboldens them."

sentences.zh: 擊之為便。

translations.literal: Striking is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: "Attack is the advantage."

sentences.zh: 」天子以為然。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃徵發許、蔡、汴、滑等六鎮之師，以太原節度使劉沔為迴紇南面招討使；

translations.literal: Then Xu, Cai, Bian, and Hua six commands' troops were mobilized; Taiyuan commissioner Liu Mian was Uighur southern campaign commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Six commands mobilized; Liu Mian led the southern campaign;

sentences.zh: 以張仲武為幽州盧龍節度使、檢校工部尚書，封蘭陵郡王，充迴紇東面招討使；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu was Youzhou Lulong commissioner, Acting Minister of Works, enfeoffed Duke of Lanling, full Uighur eastern campaign commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu led the eastern campaign;

sentences.zh: 以李思忠為河西党項都將，迴紇西南面招討使：皆會軍於太原。

translations.literal: Li Sizhong was Hexi Tangut commander, Uighur southwestern campaign commissioner—all assembling at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhong led the southwest—all converging at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 制以皇子峴為益王，岐為兗王，皇長女為昌樂公主，第二女為壽春公主，第三女永寧公主。

translations.literal: An order made the princes Xian Prince of Yi, Qi Prince of Yan; the eldest imperial daughter Princess of Changle, second daughter Princess of Shouchun, third daughter Princess of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Xian and Qi and three princesses were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 上御麟德殿，見室韋首領督熱論等十五人。

translations.literal: The Emperor attended Lindde Hall and received fifteen Shive chiefs including Dutirelun.
translations.idiomatic: At Lindde Hall Wuzong received fifteen Shive chiefs.

sentences.zh: 太原奏迴紇移帳近南四十里，索叛將嗢沒斯，昨至橫水俘虜，兼公主上表言食盡，乞賜牛羊事。

translations.literal: Taiyuan memorialized the Uighur moved their camp forty li nearer south, demanding the rebel general Wamosi; yesterday at Hengshui they captured and plundered; also the princess memorialized food exhausted, begging cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan reported Uighur camps nearer, demanding Wamosi and begging food for the princess.

sentences.zh: 賜烏介詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict to Wujie said:
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Wujie this edict:

sentences.zh: 「朕自臨寰區，為人父母，唯好生為德，不願黷武為名。

translations.literal: "I since facing the realm am parent to the people; I only take cherishing life as virtue and do not wish to make indiscriminate war a name.
translations.idiomatic: "As parent of the realm I cherish life, not glory in war."

sentences.zh: 故自彼國不幸為黠戛斯所破，來投邊境，已歷歲年，撫納之間，無所不至。

translations.literal: Therefore since your state's misfortune of Kirghiz destruction you came to the border—already years in receiving and soothing without limit.
translations.idiomatic: "Since your Kirghiz ruin we have fed and soothed you for years."

sentences.zh: 初則念其饑歉，給以糧儲；

translations.literal: At first remembering your hunger, grain stores were given;
translations.idiomatic: "We first gave grain for your hunger;"

sentences.zh: 旋則知其破傷，盡還馬價。

translations.literal: then knowing your wounds, horse prices were fully returned.
translations.idiomatic: "then returned your horse prices when you were broken."

sentences.zh: 前後遣使勞問，交馳道途。

translations.literal: Envoys were repeatedly sent to console; roads were crowded.
translations.idiomatic: "Envoys crowded the roads in consolation."

sentences.zh: 小小侵擾，亦盡不計。

translations.literal: Small harassments were all not counted.
translations.idiomatic: "Small raids we overlooked."

sentences.zh: 今可汗尚此近塞，未議還蕃。

translations.literal: Now the qaghan still nears the frontier and has not discussed returning to the steppe.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet you linger near the frontier without returning."

sentences.zh: 朝廷大臣，四方節鎮，皆懷疑忿，盡請興師，雖朕切務含弘，亦所未諭。

translations.literal: Court ministers and frontier commissioners all harbor suspicion and anger, all requesting troops; though I urgently practice forbearance, I also am not instructed.
translations.idiomatic: "Ministers demand war though I still forbear."

sentences.zh: 一昨數使迴來。

translations.literal: Yesterday several envoys returned.
translations.idiomatic: "Yesterday's envoys returned saying"

sentences.zh: 皆言可汗只待馬價，及令付之次，又聞所止屢遷，或侵掠雲、朔等州，或劫奪羌、渾諸部，未知此意，終欲如何？

translations.literal: all saying the qaghan only awaited horse price; when ordered paid, again heard his stops repeatedly shifted, sometimes raiding Yun and Shuo, sometimes seizing Qiang and Hun tribes—not knowing this intent, in the end what is intended?
translations.idiomatic: "you awaited horse price yet raided Yun, Shuo, Qiang, and Hun—what do you intend?"

sentences.zh: 若以未交馬價，須近塞垣，行止之間，亦宜先告邊將。

translations.literal: If because horse price is not yet paid you must near the wall, in movement you should first tell frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: "If you need the wall for horse price, tell our generals first."

sentences.zh: 豈有倏來忽往，遷徙不常。

translations.literal: How can you come suddenly and go suddenly, migrating without constancy?
translations.idiomatic: "Do not come and go without notice."

sentences.zh: 雖云隨逐水草，動皆逼近城柵。

translations.literal: Though you say following grass and water, every move nearly presses city ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: "Even following pasture you press our ramparts."

sentences.zh: 遙揣深意，似恃姻好之情；

translations.literal: From afar weighing deep intent, it seems to rely on marriage kinship;
translations.idiomatic: "You seem to rely on marriage yet"

sentences.zh: 每睹蹤由，實為弛突之計。

translations.literal: each sight of tracks is truly a plan of sudden raid.
translations.idiomatic: "your tracks show raid plans."

sentences.zh: 況到橫水柵下，殺戮至多。

translations.literal: Moreover reaching below Hengshui stockade, slaughter was very great.
translations.idiomatic: "You slaughtered greatly at Hengshui."

sentences.zh: 蕃、渾牛羊，豈吝馳掠；

translations.literal: Tribal and Hun cattle and sheep—would you spare driving plunder?
translations.idiomatic: "You plundered tribal herds;"

sentences.zh: 黎庶何罪，皆被傷夷。

translations.literal: what crime had common people—all were wounded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: "and killed common people without crime."

sentences.zh: 所以中朝大臣皆云：『迴紇近塞，已是違盟；

translations.literal: Therefore central ministers all say: "The Uighur near the frontier already violate the covenant;
translations.idiomatic: "Ministers say you violate the covenant"

sentences.zh: 更戮邊人，實背大義。

translations.literal: further killing frontier people truly betrays great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: "and betray righteousness by killing border people."

sentences.zh: 』咸願因此翦逐，以雪殂謝之冤。

translations.literal: " All wish to cut and drive because of this to avenge the wronged dead.
translations.idiomatic: "and wish to destroy you to avenge the dead."

sentences.zh: 然朕志在懷柔，情深屈己，寧可汗之負德，終未忍於幸災。

translations.literal: Yet my intent rests in gentle cherishing, feeling deep in bending myself—I cannot bear the qaghan's ingratitude and finally not indulge in opportunistic disaster.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet I still forbear though you are ungrateful."

sentences.zh: 石戒直久在京城，備知人實憤惋，發於誠懇，固請自行。

translations.literal: Shi Jiezhi long in the capital fully knows human hearts are indignant; arising from sincere earnestness he firmly requested to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: "Shi Jiezhi, knowing the court's wrath, begged to go."

sentences.zh: 嘉其深見事機，不能違阻。

translations.literal: I praise his deep seeing of affairs and could not refuse obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: "I could not refuse him."

sentences.zh: 可汗審自問遂，速擇良圖，無至不悛，以貽後悔。

translations.literal: Qaghan examine yourself and quickly choose a good plan—do not reach incorrigibility and bring later regret."
translations.idiomatic: "Choose wisely before regret comes." Thus ended the edict.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 詔太原起室韋沙陀三部落、吐渾諸部，委石雄為前鋒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Taiyuan to raise Shive, Shatuo three tribes, and Tuhun tribes; Shi Xiong was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan raised Shive, Shatuo, and Tuhun with Shi Xiong as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 易定兵千人守大同軍，契苾通、何清朝領沙陀、吐渾六千騎趨天德，李思忠率迴紇、党項之師屯保大柵。

translations.literal: Yiding thousand men guarded Datong Army; Qibi Tong and He Qingchao led Shatuo and Tuhun six thousand cavalry toward Tiande; Li Sizhong led Uighur and Tangut troops encamped at Baoda stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Allied columns marched on Tiande and Baoda.

sentences.zh: 十月，吐蕃贊普卒，遣使論普熱入朝告哀，詔將作少監李璟入蕃弔祭。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Tibetan qaghan died; envoys Lun Pire entered court announcing mourning; Director of Imperial Works Li Jing was ordered into Tibet to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan qaghan died; Li Jing was sent to mourn.

sentences.zh: 帝幸涇陽，校獵白鹿原。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Jingyang and hunted at White Deer Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong hunted at White Deer Plain near Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫高少逸、鄭朗等於閣內論：「陛下校獵太頻，出城稍遠，萬機廢馳，星出夜歸，方今用兵，且宜停止。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Gao Shaoyi and Zheng Lang debated within the hall: "Your Majesty hunts too often, leaves the city somewhat far, myriad affairs abandoned, stars out and night return—now using troops, for the time stop."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shaoyi and Zheng Lang urged an end to frequent hunts during war.

sentences.zh: 」上優勞之。

translations.literal: The Emperor graciously comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong graciously heard them.

sentences.zh: 諫官出，謂宰相曰：「諫官甚要，朕時聞其言，庶幾減過。

translations.literal: When remonstrance officials left they told the councillors: "Remonstrance officials are very important; I sometimes hear their words and may reduce faults."
translations.idiomatic: He told councillors remonstrance kept him from error.

sentences.zh: 」會昌三年三年春正月，以宿師於野，罷元會。

translations.literal: Huichang 3, spring, first month—year Huichang 3 duplicated—because troops were long in the field, the New Year audience was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang 3 canceled the New Year audience for troops in the field.

sentences.zh: 敕新授銀州刺史、本州押蕃落、銀川監牧使何清朝可檢校太子賓客、左龍武大將軍，令分領沙陀、吐渾、党項之眾赴振武，取劉沔處分。

translations.literal: An order: newly appointed Yinzhou prefect, tribal superintendent, Yin River supervisor He Qingchao was made Acting Crown Prince Guest of Honor and Left Dragon Martial great general, ordered to divide command of Shatuo, Tuhun, and Tangut masses to Zhenwu, taking Liu Mian's disposition.
translations.idiomatic: He Qingchao was sent to Zhenwu commanding tribal allies.

sentences.zh: 二月，先詔百官之家不得於京城置私廟者，其皇城南向六坊不得置，其閑僻坊曲即許依舊置。

translations.literal: Second month: the prior edict forbidding officials' households from private temples in the capital—the six wards south of the imperial city might not have them; secluded wards might keep old ones.
translations.idiomatic: Private temples were banned in the southern capital wards only.

sentences.zh: 太原劉沔奏：「昨率諸道之師至大同軍，遣石雄襲迴鶻牙帳，雄大敗迴鶻於殺胡山，烏介可汗被創而走。

translations.literal: Taiyuan Liu Mian memorialized: "Yesterday leading allied commands to Datong Army, sent Shi Xiong to raid the Uighur royal camp; Xiong greatly defeated the Uighur at Kill-Hu Mountain; Wujie qaghan was wounded and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian reported Shi Xiong's victory at Kill-Hu Mountain and Wujie wounded;

sentences.zh: 已迎得太和公主至雲州。

translations.literal: Princess Taihe has been welcomed to Yunzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taihe reached Yunzhou."

sentences.zh: 」是日，御宣政殿，百僚稱賀。

translations.literal: That day the Emperor attended Xuanzheng Hall; the hundred officials congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: That day the court congratulated at Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 制曰：

translations.literal: An order said:
translations.idiomatic: A victory edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 「夫天之所廢，難施繼絕之恩；

translations.literal: "What Heaven abandons, hard to apply continuing-the-lineage grace;
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's abandoned may not receive continuing-lineage grace;"

sentences.zh: 人之所棄，當用侮亡之道。

translations.literal: what men discard should use the way of insulting the perished."
translations.idiomatic: "what men discard should be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 朕每思前訓，豈忘格言。

translations.literal: I each think on former instruction—how can I forget the maxim?
translations.idiomatic: "I remember the maxim of destroying the perished."

sentences.zh: 迴鶻比者自恃兵強，久為桀驁，淩虐諸部，結怨近鄰。

translations.literal: The Uighur lately relied on military strength, long been fierce and arrogant, oppressing all tribes, knotting hate with near neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: "The Uighur grew arrogant and oppressed neighbors."

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯潛師彗掃，穹居瓦解，種族盡膏於原野，區落遂至於荊榛。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz sent troops like a comet sweep; the dome dwelling collapsed, clans all oiled the wilds, districts reached brambles.
translations.idiomatic: "Kirghiz swept them; clans perished in the wilds."

sentences.zh: 今可汗逃走失國，竊號自立，遠逾沙漠，寄命邊陲。

translations.literal: Now the qaghan fled losing the state, stealing title and standing alone, far crossing desert, trusting life to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: "Their qaghan fled and clung to our border."

sentences.zh: 朕念其衰殘，尋加賑恤。

translations.literal: I thought on their decline and soon added relief.
translations.idiomatic: "I pitied and fed them."

sentences.zh: 每陳章表，多詐諛之詞；

translations.literal: Each memorial often held many false flattery;
translations.idiomatic: "Their memorials flattered;"

sentences.zh: 接我使臣，如全盛之日。

translations.literal: receiving my envoys as in full flourishing days.
translations.idiomatic: "they treated envoys as if still mighty."

sentences.zh: 無傷禽哀鳴之意，有困獸猶鬥之心。

translations.literal: No wounded bird's mournful cry—there was a cornered beast still fighting mind.
translations.idiomatic: "They fought like cornered beasts."

sentences.zh: 去歲潛入朔川，大掠牛馬；

translations.literal: Last year they secretly entered Shuochuan, greatly plundering cattle and horses;
translations.idiomatic: "Last year they raided Shuochuan for herds;"

sentences.zh: 今春掩襲振武，逼近城池。

translations.literal: this spring they suddenly struck Zhenwu, nearing the walled city.
translations.idiomatic: "this spring they struck Zhenwu near the walls."

sentences.zh: 可汗皆自率兵，首為寇盜，不恥破敗，莫顧姻親。

translations.literal: The qaghan all personally led troops, first as robber chief, not ashamed of defeat, not caring for marriage kin.
translations.idiomatic: "The qaghan himself led raids without shame or kinship."

sentences.zh: 河東節度使劉沔料敵伐謀，乘機制勝，發胡貉之騎以為前鋒，搴翎侯之旗伐彼在穴。

translations.literal: Hedong commissioner Liu Mian gauged the enemy and plotted victory, seized opportunity for triumph, sent Hu and Mo cavalry as vanguard, plucked the feather-banner flag while they were in the burrow.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian sent Hu and Mo cavalry under Shi Xiong to strike their camp.

sentences.zh: 短兵鏖於帳下，元惡抶於彀中。

translations.literal: Short weapons battled below the tent; the chief villain was seized in the trap.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy chief was seized in the tent battle.

sentences.zh: 況乘匪六飛，眾纔一旅，儲備已竭，計日可擒。

translations.literal: Moreover riding not the six flying horses, masses barely one command, stores already exhausted—capture counted by days.
translations.idiomatic: Their few starving horses could be taken within days.

sentences.zh: 太和公主居處不同，情義久絕。

translations.literal: Princess Taihe's dwelling differed; affection long severed.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taihe had long been estranged.

sentences.zh: 懷土多思，亟聞黃鵠之歌；

translations.literal: Missing homeland she often heard the yellow crane's song;
translations.idiomatic: She longed for home like the yellow crane song;

sentences.zh: 失位自傷，寧免《綠衣》之歎。

translations.literal: losing position she grieved—how avoid the Green Clothes' lament.
translations.idiomatic: and grieved her lost station like the Green Clothes ode.

sentences.zh: 念其羈苦，常軫朕心。

translations.literal: Thinking on her bonds and hardship often pained my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Her suffering pained the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今已脫於豺狼，再見宮闕，上以攄宗廟之宿憤，次以慰太皇太后之深慈，永言歸寧，良用欣感。

translations.literal: Now freed from wolves and dogs, again seeing palace gates—above to vent the ancestral temple's old wrath, next to comfort the grand empress dowager's deep kindness; forever speaking return and peace, truly used joy and gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Freed, she returned to vent ancestral wrath and comfort the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 其迴紇既以破滅，義在翦除，宜令諸道兵馬使同進討。

translations.literal: The Uighur already broken and destroyed—righteousness lies in cutting them; all commands' troops should jointly advance to punish.
translations.idiomatic: Uighur destruction required joint pursuit.

sentences.zh: 河東立功將士已下，優厚賞給，續條疏處分。

translations.literal: Hedong merit troops and below—richly reward; continued memorials will dispose.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong victors would be richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 應在京外宅及東都修功德迴紇，並勒冠帶，各配諸道收管。

translations.literal: Those in capital outer residences and eastern capital performing merit Uighur—all forced caps and belts, each assigned to commands for custody.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Uighur were registered to commands.

sentences.zh: 其迴紇及摩尼寺莊宅、錢物等，並委功德使與御史臺及京兆府各差官點檢收抽，不得容諸色人影占。

translations.literal: Uighur and Manichean temple estates, money and goods—all entrusted to the Merit commissioner with Censorate and Jingzhao each sending officers to inspect and seize; no person of any sort might shadow-occupy.
translations.idiomatic: Uighur and Manichean property was seized by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 如犯者並處極法，錢物納官。

translations.literal: Violators all suffer extreme law; money and goods enter the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Violators faced death; goods went to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 摩尼寺僧委中書門下條疏聞奏。

translations.literal: Manichean monks were entrusted to the Secretariat to memorialize disposal."
translations.idiomatic: Manichean monks awaited secretariat disposal." Thus ended the edict.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 以麟州刺史、天德行營副使石雄為銀青光祿大夫、檢校左散騎常侍、豐州刺史、御史大夫，充豐州西城中城都防禦、本管押蕃落等使。

translations.literal: Linzhou prefect and Tiande campaign vice commissioner Shi Xiong was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master, Acting Left Cavalier, Fengzhou prefect, Censor-in-Chief, full Fengzhou western inner-city metropolitan defense and tribal superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong was richly rewarded for the Uighur victory.

sentences.zh: 劉沔檢校尚書左僕射，張仲武檢校尚書右僕射，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Liu Mian was made Acting Left Vice Director; Zhang Zhongwu Acting Right Vice Director—the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian and Zhang Zhongwu were promoted.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯使注吾合素入朝，獻名馬二匹，言可汗已破迴鶻，迎得太和公主歸國，差人送公主入朝，愁迴鶻殘眾奪之於路。

translations.literal: Kirghiz envoy Zhunwu Hesu entered court, presenting two famous horses, saying the qaghan had broken the Uighur and welcomed Princess Taihe home, sending men to escort the princess to court, fearing Uighur remnants would seize her on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Kirghiz envoys offered horses and asked Tang to escort the princess.

sentences.zh: 帝遂遣中使送注吾合素往太原迎公主。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent palace envoys with Zhunwu Hesu to Taiyuan to welcome the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys went to Taiyuan with the Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 時烏介可汗中箭，走投黑車子，詔黠戛斯出兵攻之。

translations.literal: At the time Wujie qaghan was shot; he fled seeking the Black Cart; an edict ordered Kirghiz troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie, wounded, fled to the Black Cart; Kirghiz were ordered to pursue.

sentences.zh: 三月，太和公主至京師，百官班于章敬寺迎謁，仍令所司告憲宗、穆宗二室。

translations.literal: Third month: Princess Taihe reached the capital; officials lined at Zhangjing Temple to welcome; still ordered the offices to announce to Xianzong and Muzong's shrines.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Princess Taihe returned amid state rites.

sentences.zh: 四月，昭義節度使劉從諫卒，三軍以從諫侄稹為兵馬留後，上表請授節鉞。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Zhaoyi commissioner Liu Congjian died; the three armies made his nephew Zhen provisional commander and memorialized for credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian died; his nephew Zhen seized Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使齎詔潞府，令稹護從諫之喪歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon envoys were sent with edicts to Luzhou ordering Zhen to escort Congjian's bier to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts ordered Zhen to send the bier to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 稹拒朝旨。

translations.literal: Zhen refused court orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen refused.

sentences.zh: 詔中書門下兩省尚書御史臺四品已上、武官三品已上，會議劉稹可誅可宥之狀以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Secretariat, Chancellery, both departments, Censorate fourth rank and above, martial officials third rank and above, to meet debating whether Liu Zhen might be executed or pardoned and report.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated executing Liu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 五月，敕諸道節度使置隨身不得過六十人，觀察使不得過四十人，經略、都護不得過三十人。

translations.literal: Fifth month: an order for all military commissioners' personal guards not to exceed sixty, observation commissioners forty, frontier commissioners thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Personal guards of commissioners were capped.

sentences.zh: 築望仙觀於禁中。

translations.literal: Wangxian Observatory was built in the forbidden inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wangxian Observatory rose in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 宰臣百僚進議狀：「以昆戎未殄，塞上用兵，不宜中原生事，潞府請以親王遙領，令稹權知兵馬事，以俟邊上罷兵。

translations.literal: Councillors and hundred officials submitted debate memorials: "Because the western barbarians are not destroyed and the frontier uses troops, the central plain should not raise affairs—the Luzhou request is to have an imperial prince hold title remotely and let Zhen provisionally command troops until frontier war ends."
translations.idiomatic: Most councillors urged a remote prince and temporary Zhen command until frontier war ended.

sentences.zh: 」獨李德裕以為澤潞內地，前時從諫許襲，已是失斷，自後跋扈難制，規脅朝廷。

translations.literal: Only Li Deyu held that Ze-Lu was inner land; when Congjian was permitted succession it was already a lost judgment; afterward overbearing hard to control, scheming to coerce the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu alone said Zhen must be destroyed lest Ze-Lu coerce the court again.

sentences.zh: 以稹豎子，不可復踐前車，討之必殄。

translations.literal: Because Zhen is a stripling, one cannot repeat the prior cart—strike and he will be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhen is young; strike and he falls."

sentences.zh: 武宗性雄俊，曰：「吾與德裕同之，保無後悔。

translations.literal: Wuzong's nature was heroic; he said: "I agree with Deyu—surely no later regret."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong sided with Deyu: "No regret."

sentences.zh: 」自是諫官上疏言不可用兵相繼。

translations.literal: From this remonstrance officials' memorials saying troops must not be used followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators then flooded in against war.

sentences.zh: 六月，西內神龍寺災。

translations.literal: Sixth month: the western inner Divine Dragon Temple burned.
translations.idiomatic: The inner Divine Dragon Temple burned.

sentences.zh: 左軍中尉楚國公仇士良卒。

translations.literal: Left Army Commandant Duke of Chu Qiu Shiliang died.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang died.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊子，宰相奏：「秋色已至，將議進軍，幽州須早平迴鶻，鎮、魏須速誅劉稹，各須遣使諭旨，兼偵三鎮軍情。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, wuzi: councillors memorialized: "Autumn color has arrived; we will discuss advancing troops; Youzhou must early pacify the Uighur, Zhen and Wei must quickly execute Liu Zhen—each must send envoys proclaiming intent and spy the three commands' army mood."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month councillors planned envoys to three commands.

sentences.zh: 今日延英面奉聖旨，欲遣張賈充使。

translations.literal: Today in Extended Ying we received the sacred face wishing to send Zhang Jia as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor first named Zhang Jia envoy.

sentences.zh: 臣等續更商量，張賈幹濟有才，甚諳軍中體勢，然性剛負氣，慮不安和，不如且命李回。

translations.literal: We continued discussion: Zhang Jia is capable and knows army situation well, but his nature is hard and proud—we fear no peace—better for now order Li Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Councillors preferred Li Hui over the proud Zhang Jia.

sentences.zh: 若以臺綱闕人，即兵部侍郎鄭涯久為征鎮判官，情甚精敏，雖無詞辯，言事分明，官重事閑，最似相稱。

translations.literal: If the censorate lacks men, War Vice Minister Zheng Ya long served as frontier commissioner's aide, very keen though without eloquence, affairs clear, rank heavy duty light—most fitting."
translations.idiomatic: They also named Zheng Ya as an alternative.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「不如令李回去。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Better order Li Hui return."
translations.idiomatic: "Send Li Hui," said the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」即遣回奉使三鎮。

translations.literal: Immediately Li Hui was sent as envoy to the three commands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui was dispatched to the three commands.

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，火星自七月蒼赤色，動搖井中，至是月十六日犯輿鬼。

translations.literal: Eighth month, renxu: Mars since the seventh month was pale red, shaking in the well; by this month's sixteenth it transgressed Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Mars transgressed Ghost after shaking in the well.

sentences.zh: 萬年縣東市火。

translations.literal: Wannian county eastern market burned.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian's east market burned.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯使諦德伊斯難珠入朝。

translations.literal: Kirghiz envoy Didesi Nanzhu entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Another Kirghiz envoy arrived.

sentences.zh: 以右僕射、平章事陳夷行檢校司空，兼河中尹、御史大夫，充河中節度、晉絳慈隰觀察等使。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director and Grand Councillor Chen Yixing was made Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Hezhong prefect and Censor-in-Chief, full Hezhong military commissioner and Jin- Jiang- Ci- Li observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing took Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 九月，制：

translations.literal: Ninth month, an order:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an order declared war on Liu Zhen:

sentences.zh: 「定天下者，致風俗於大同；

translations.literal: "To settle the realm is to bring custom to great unity;
translations.idiomatic: "To settle the realm unifies custom;

sentences.zh: 安生人者，齊法度於畫一。

translations.literal: to pacify the living is to align law on one measure."
translations.idiomatic: "to pacify the living aligns law on one measure."

sentences.zh: 雖晉之欒、趙，家有舊勳；

translations.literal: Though Jin's Luan and Zhao families had old merit;
translations.idiomatic: "Though Jin's Luan and Zhao had old merit,

sentences.zh: 漢之韓、黥，身為佐命。

translations.literal: Han's Han and Ying, bodies as assistants to mandate—
translations.idiomatic: Han's Han Xin and Ying Bu aided the mandate—

sentences.zh: 至於干亂紀律，罔不梟夷，禁暴除殘，古今大義。

translations.literal: as for disturbing discipline, none were not displayed and killed; forbidding violence and removing the cruel is ancient and modern great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: rebels who disturbed discipline were executed—ancient righteousness."

sentences.zh: 故昭義節度劉悟，頃居海岱，嘗列爪牙。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhaoyi commissioner Liu Wu formerly dwelt on the eastern sea, once ranked among claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Wu once served the throne from the eastern sea."
