sentences.zh: 屬師道阻兵，王師問罪，三面開網，一境離心，乘此危機，遂能歸命。

translations.literal: When Shidao obstructed troops the royal army questioned guilt; three faces opened nets, one territory lost heart—seizing this crisis he could return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: "When Shidao rebelled Wu turned to allegiance."

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉其誠款，授以南燕；

translations.literal: Xianzong praised his sincere pledge and gave southern Yan;
translations.idiomatic: "Xianzong gave him Zhaoyi."

sentences.zh: 穆宗待以腹心，委之上黨。

translations.literal: Muzong treated him as trusted belly and heart, entrusted upper Dang.
translations.idiomatic: "Muzong entrusted upper Dang to him."

sentences.zh: 招致死士，固護一方，迨於未年，已虧臣節。

translations.literal: He recruited dead warriors, firmly guarding one region—by his last years he already lacked a minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: "He grew overmighty until his minister's integrity failed."

sentences.zh: 劉從諫生稟戾氣，幼習亂風。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian bore perverse qi from birth, from youth practiced chaotic wind.
translations.idiomatic: "Congjian was perverse from youth."

sentences.zh: 因跋扈之資，以專封壤；

translations.literal: By overbearing capital he monopolized his fief;
translations.idiomatic: "He monopolized his fief by arrogance;"

sentences.zh: 恃紀綱之力，以襲兵符。

translations.literal: by discipline's power he seized military tallies.
translations.idiomatic: "and seized military tallies by force."

sentences.zh: 暫展執珪之儀，終無上綬之請。

translations.literal: Briefly he showed holding jade scepter ritual—finally no request for upper investiture.
translations.idiomatic: "He played loyal without seeking investiture."

sentences.zh: 隙駒為喻，魏豹姑務于絕河；

translations.literal: Gap-horse as metaphor—Wei Bao for a time worked to cut the river;
translations.idiomatic: "Like a gap horse or Wei Bao at the river,

sentences.zh: 井蛙自居，孫述頗聞於恃險。

translations.literal: well-frog dwelling alone—Sun Shu was heard to trust peril.
translations.idiomatic: or a well frog like Sun Shu trusting his peril."

sentences.zh: 誘受戶命，妄作妖言，中罔朝廷，潛圖左道。

translations.literal: He lured and received household mandates, recklessly made demon words, deceived the court within, secretly plotted left-hand ways.
translations.idiomatic: "He deceived the court with omens and left-hand plots."

sentences.zh: 接壤戎帥，屢奏陰謀，顧髫齔之所矜，豈淵魚之是察。

translations.literal: Bordering Rong commanders repeatedly memorialized secret plots—pitying infants he cherished—how could deep fish be observed?
translations.idiomatic: "Border commanders reported his plots though the court indulged him."

sentences.zh: 洎乎沈痼，曾靡哀鳴，猶駐將盡之魂，恣行邪僻之志，罔或奮拔，自樹狡童。

translations.literal: When his illness deepened he never mourned; still stationed his dying soul, wantonly walked perverse intent, none could wrest him up—he himself set a crafty boy.
translations.idiomatic: "Dying, he left power to the crafty boy Zhen."

sentences.zh: 中使授醫，莫睹其朝服；

translations.literal: Palace envoys gave medicine—none saw his court dress;
translations.idiomatic: "Envoys could not enter his gates;"

sentences.zh: 近臣銜命，不入於壘門。

translations.literal: near ministers bore orders—not entering the rampart gate.
translations.idiomatic: "and near ministers were barred."

sentences.zh: 逆節甚明，人神共棄。

translations.literal: Rebellion was very clear; men and spirits together abandoned him.
translations.idiomatic: "His rebellion was plain to men and spirits."

sentences.zh: 其贈官及先所授官爵、並劉稹在身官爵，宜並削奪。

translations.literal: His posthumous offices and prior granted offices and titles and Liu Zhen's personal offices and titles should all be stripped."
translations.idiomatic: "Strip all titles of Congjian and Zhen."

sentences.zh: 成德軍節度使王元逵、魏博節度使何弘敬，或姻連王室，或任重藩維，懇陳一至之誠，願揚九伐之命。

translations.literal: Chengde commissioner Wang Yuankui and Weibo commissioner He Hongjing—some kin-linked to the royal house, some weighty in frontier pillars—all earnestly stated one-minded sincerity, wishing to raise the nine punishments' mandate.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Yuankui and He Hongjing begged to campaign."

sentences.zh: 吳漢任職，受詔而初無辦嚴；

translations.literal: Wu Han took office, received edict yet at first made no preparation;
translations.idiomatic: "Like Wu Han receiving orders without delay,

sentences.zh: 卜式朴忠，未戰而義形於色。

translations.literal: Bu Shi's plain loyalty showed righteousness before battle."
translations.idiomatic: or Bu Shi showing loyalty before battle."

sentences.zh: 況成德軍嘗以梟騎橫陣，首破朱滔。

translations.literal: Moreover Chengde army once with owl cavalry arrayed across, first broke Zhu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: "Chengde once broke Zhu Tao;"

sentences.zh: 戰氣方酣，再迴魯陽之日；

translations.literal: Battle spirit just fierce, again turned Luyang's sun;
translations.idiomatic: "its spirit turned Luyang's sun;"

sentences.zh: 鼓音不息，三周不注之山。

translations.literal: drums unceasing, three circuits around Bu Zhu mountain.
translations.idiomatic: "its drums circled Bu Zhu mountain thrice."

sentences.zh: 魏博軍頃以大旆涉河，竟殲師道。

translations.literal: Weibo army lately with great banners crossed the river, finally destroyed Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: "Weibo destroyed Shidao across the river."

sentences.zh: 建十二郡之旗鼓，以列降人；

translations.literal: Raised twelve prefectures' flags and drums to array surrendering men;
translations.idiomatic: "It raised twelve prefectures' banners for surrender;"

sentences.zh: 削六十年之厲階，盡歸皇化。

translations.literal: cut sixty years' harsh steps—all returned to imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: "and ended sixty years of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 士傳餘勇，軍有雄名，必能稟酇侯之指縱，成葛亮之心伐。

translations.literal: Soldiers transmit surplus courage, armies have heroic names—surely they can follow Xiao He's direction and accomplish Zhuge Liang's heart in campaigning."
translations.idiomatic: "Their courage can follow great captains of old."

sentences.zh: 咨爾二帥，朕所注懷，元逵可本官充北面招討澤潞使，弘敬充東面招討澤潞使。

translations.literal: Consult you two commanders, my entrusted care—Yuankui may keep his post as northern Ze-Lu campaign commissioner; Hongjing eastern Ze-Lu campaign commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: "Yuankui leads north, Hongjing east against Zhen."

sentences.zh: 曩者列祖在藩，先天啟聖。

translations.literal: Formerly the former emperors were in frontier posts; Heaven first opened sagely fortune.
translations.idiomatic: "Our ancestors in Ze-Lu bore omens of sage rule;"

sentences.zh: 符瑞昭晰，彩繪煥於泗亭；

translations.literal: Portents clear, painted brilliance flashed at Si Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: "portents shone at Si Pavilion;"

sentences.zh: 鑾輅巡遊，金石刻于代邸。

translations.literal: imperial chariot toured, metal and stone carved at Dai Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: "imperial tours carved Dai Lodge."

sentences.zh: 實謂可封之俗，久為仁壽之鄉。

translations.literal: Truly called a fiefable folk, long a benevolent longevity village.
translations.idiomatic: "Ze-Lu was long a loyal land."

sentences.zh: 寇難以來，頗著誠節，必非同惡，咸許自新。

translations.literal: Since bandits came, quite showing sincere loyalty—surely not the same evil; all permitted to renew.
translations.idiomatic: "Its people showed loyalty amid trouble and may renew."

sentences.zh: 其昭義舊將士及百姓等，如保初心，並赦而不問。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi old soldiers and common people—if they keep the first heart, all pardon without question.
translations.idiomatic: "Old soldiers who keep faith are pardoned."

sentences.zh: 如能捨逆效順，以州郡兵眾歸降者，必厚加封賞。

translations.literal: If they abandon rebellion and show obedience, surrendering prefectural troops and masses—richly enfeoff.
translations.idiomatic: "Surrendering troops will be richly rewarded."

sentences.zh: 如能擒送劉稹者，別授土地，以報勳庸。

translations.literal: If they capture and deliver Liu Zhen—separately grant land to repay merit.
translations.idiomatic: "Capturing Zhen wins separate fiefs."

sentences.zh: 頃隨劉悟鄆州舊將校子孫，既有義心，宜思改悔。

translations.literal: Formerly following Liu Wu's Yanzhou old officers' descendants—already having righteous hearts—should think to repent.
translations.idiomatic: "Yanzhou old officers should repent and turn."

sentences.zh: 如能感喻劉稹，束身歸朝，必當待之如初，特與洗雪。

translations.literal: If they can move Liu Zhen to bind himself and return to court—he will surely be treated as at first, especially washed clean.
translations.idiomatic: "Those who move Zhen to surrender will be washed clean."

sentences.zh: 爾等舊校，亦並酬勞。

translations.literal: Your old officers also will all be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: "Their officers will also be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 仍委夷行、劉沔、王茂元各進兵同力攻討。

translations.literal: Still entrust Yixing, Liu Mian, and Wang Maoyuan each to advance troops with united strength to attack."
translations.idiomatic: "Yixing, Liu Mian, and Wang Maoyuan will join the attack."

sentences.zh: 其諸道進軍，並不得焚燒廬舍，發掘墳墓，擒執百姓以為俘囚。

translations.literal: All commands advancing—none may burn huts, dig graves, seize and hold common people as captives.
translations.idiomatic: "Armies must not burn, dig graves, or seize civilians."

sentences.zh: 桑麻田苗，各許本戶為主。

translations.literal: Mulberry hemp and field seedlings—each permits the original household as master.
translations.idiomatic: "Fields return to their owners."

sentences.zh: 罪止元惡，務拯生靈。

translations.literal: Guilt stops at the chief villain; strive to save the living."
translations.idiomatic: "Punish only Zhen; spare the people."

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The edict sighed: Alas!

sentences.zh: 蕃維大臣，抗疏於外；

translations.literal: Frontier great ministers submitted blunt memorials without;
translations.idiomatic: "Frontier ministers remonstrated without;"

sentences.zh: 髦俊舊老，昌言於朝。

translations.literal: eminent old men spoke clearly in court.
translations.idiomatic: "court elders spoke clearly."

sentences.zh: 戒朕以祖宗之法，不可私一族；

translations.literal: They warned me with ancestral law—one clan may not be privately favored;
translations.idiomatic: "They warned me: ancestral law forbids favoring one clan;"

sentences.zh: 刑賞之柄，所以正萬邦。

translations.literal: the handle of punishment and reward is to correct ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: "punishment and reward correct the realm."

sentences.zh: 宜用甲兵，陳於原野。

translations.literal: Armor and troops should be arrayed on the wild plain."
translations.idiomatic: "Use arms on the plain."

sentences.zh: 雖朕以恩不聽，而群臣以義固爭，詢自僉謀，諒非獲已。

translations.literal: Though I by grace would not listen, yet ministers by righteousness firmly contended—inquiry from collective counsel, surely not obtained willingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Though I wished mercy, ministers by righteousness demanded war."

sentences.zh: 佈告中外，明體朕懷。

translations.literal: Proclaim inner and outer, clarifying my heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Let all know my reluctant heart." Thus ended the edict.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 仍以徐泗節度使李彥佐為澤潞西南面招討使。

translations.literal: Still made Xu-Si commissioner Li Yanzhuo Ze-Lu southwestern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzhuo became southwestern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使王茂元以本軍屯萬善。

translations.literal: Heyang commissioner Wang Maoyuan encamped his army at Wanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyuan encamped at Wanshan.

sentences.zh: 彥佐制下後逾月未出師，朝廷疑其持重，乃以天德軍石雄為彥佐之副。

translations.literal: After Yanzhuo's order more than a month passed without marching—the court suspected his caution—then made Tiande Shi Xiong Yanzhuo's vice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzhuo's delay made Shi Xiong his vice.

sentences.zh: 劉稹牙將李丕降，用為忻州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen's barracks general Li Pi surrendered and was used as Xinzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pi surrendered and became Xinzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 以陳許節度使王宰充澤潞南面招討使。

translations.literal: Chen-Xu commissioner Wang Zai was made Ze-Lu southern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai led the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使王茂元卒，贈司徒。

translations.literal: Heyang commissioner Wang Maoyuan died; posthumously made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyuan died and was posthumously honored.

sentences.zh: 王宰代茂元總萬善之師。

translations.literal: Wang Zai replaced Maoyuan commanding Wanshan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai took the Wanshan army.

sentences.zh: 十月，宰相監修國史李紳、兵部郎中史館修撰判館事鄭亞進重修《憲宗實錄》四十卷，頒賜有差。

translations.literal: Tenth month: supervising Veritable Records councillor Li Shen and War Bureau director and History Office compiler Zheng Ya submitted the revised forty volumes of Xianzong's Veritable Records, distributed with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen and Zheng Ya presented forty revised volumes of Xianzong's records.

sentences.zh: 晉絳行營副招討石雄奏收賊砦五。

translations.literal: Jin-Jiang campaign vice commissioner Shi Xiong memorialized capturing five rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong reported five stockades taken.

sentences.zh: 以河東節度使劉沔檢校司空，兼滑州刺史、御史大夫，充義成軍節度、鄭滑濮觀察等使。

translations.literal: Hedong commissioner Liu Mian was made Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Huazhou prefect and Censor-in-Chief, full Yicheng military commissioner and Zheng-Hua-Pu observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian took Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 以荊南節度使、檢校右僕射、同平章事李石可檢校司空、平章事，兼太原尹、北都留守，充河東節度、管內觀察等使。

translations.literal: Jingnan commissioner Acting Right Vice Director Li Shi was made Acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor, concurrent Taiyuan prefect, northern capital regent, full Hedong observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi took Hedong and the council.

sentences.zh: 十一月，敕：「中外官員，過為繁冗，量宜減省，以便軍民。

translations.literal: November: an order: "Inner and outer officials are excessively numerous—measure and reduce to benefit army and people.
translations.idiomatic: An order demanded Personnel report staff cuts:

sentences.zh: 宜令吏部條疏合減員數以聞。

translations.literal: Let Personnel memorialize the combined reduction count and report."
translations.idiomatic: "Let Personnel report combined reductions." Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，王宰奏收天井關。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Wang Zai memorialized capturing Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai took Tianjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 榆社行營都將王逢奏兵少，乞濟師，詔太原軍二千人赴之。

translations.literal: Yushe campaign commander Wang Feng memorialized few troops, begging reinforcements; an edict sent Taiyuan two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng received two thousand Taiyuan reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 初，劉沔破迴鶻，留三千人戍橫水，至是，李石以太原無兵，抽橫水戍卒一千五百人以赴王逢。

translations.literal: Earlier when Liu Mian broke the Uighur he left three thousand men garrisoning Hengshui; now Li Shi because Taiyuan had no troops drew fifteen hundred Hengshui garrison for Wang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi stripped Hengshui garrison for Wang Feng.

sentences.zh: 是月二十八日，橫水軍至太原，請出軍優給。

translations.literal: That month on the twenty-eighth Hengshui troops reached Taiyuan requesting to march with generous pay.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth Hengshui troops at Taiyuan demanded generous pay.

sentences.zh: 舊例每一軍絹二疋，時劉沔交代後，軍庫無絹。

translations.literal: Old precedent each army two bolts silk; at the time after Liu Mian's handover the army treasury had no silk.
translations.idiomatic: Each army expected two bolts silk, but the treasury was empty.

sentences.zh: 石以己絹益之。

translations.literal: Li Shi used his own silk to supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi supplied his own silk.

sentences.zh: 方可人給一疋，便催上路。

translations.literal: Only then one bolt per man, then hurried on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Each man got one bolt and was hurried out.

sentences.zh: 軍人以歲將除，欲候過歲，期既速，軍情不悅。

translations.literal: Soldiers because the year would end wished to wait past New Year—the term was urgent, army mood displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers wanted to pass New Year; the rush angered them.

sentences.zh: 都頭楊弁乘士卒流怨，激之為亂。

translations.literal: Command head Yang Bian seized soldiers' spreading resentment and incited rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bian incited mutiny from their anger.

sentences.zh: 會昌四年四年春正月乙酉朔，以澤潞用兵，罷元會。

translations.literal: Huichang 4, spring, first month, yiyou new moon—year Huichang 4 duplicated—because Ze-Lu used troops, the New Year audience was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang 4 canceled the New Year audience for the Ze-Lu war.

sentences.zh: 其日，楊弁逐太原節度使李石。

translations.literal: That day Yang Bian expelled Taiyuan commissioner Li Shi.
translations.idiomatic: That day Yang Bian expelled Li Shi from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 敕：「齋月斷屠，出於釋氏，國家創業，猶近梁、隋、卿相大臣，或沿茲弊。

translations.literal: An order: "Fast-month meat cutting comes from Buddhism; our state's founding still nears Liang and Sui—ministers and great officials sometimes follow this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: An order limited Buddhist slaughter bans:

sentences.zh: 鼓刀者既獲厚利，糾察者潛受請求。

translations.literal: Butchers gain thick profit; inspectors secretly receive requests.
translations.idiomatic: "Butchers and inspectors profited from the ban."

sentences.zh: 正月以萬物生植之初，宜斷三日。

translations.literal: The first month is when the myriad things first grow—should cut three days.
translations.idiomatic: "Cut three days in the first month;"

sentences.zh: 列聖忌斷一日。

translations.literal: The former emperors' memorial days cut one day.
translations.idiomatic: "one day on imperial memorial days;"

sentences.zh: 仍准開元二十二年敕，三元日各斷三日，餘月不禁。

translations.literal: Still per Kaiyuan 22 order, the three yuan days each cut three days; other months not forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: "three days on each yuan day; other months free." Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」壬子，河東監軍使呂義忠收復太原，生擒楊弁，盡斬其亂卒，百僚稱賀。

translations.literal: On renzi Hedong army supervisor Lü Yizhong recovered Taiyuan, captured Yang Bian alive, executed all mutinous soldiers; the hundred officials congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Lü Yizhong retook Taiyuan and executed the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 二月甲寅朔。

translations.literal: Second month, jiayin new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The second month opened on jiayin.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，制河中晉、絳、慈、隰等州節度觀察等使、中散大夫、檢校左散騎常侍、河中尹、御史大夫、上柱國、博陵縣開國男、食邑三百戶崔元式可檢校禮部尚書，兼太原尹、北都留守，充河東節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: On dingsi an order: Hezhong Jin-Jiang-Ci-Li observation commissioner Acting Left Cavalier Hezhong prefect Cui Yuanshi was made Acting Minister of Rites, concurrent Taiyuan prefect, northern capital regent, full Hedong observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Cui Yuanshi replaced Li Shi at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 戊午夜，太白犯鎮星。

translations.literal: On wuwu night Venus transgressed the Station Star.
translations.idiomatic: That wuwu night Venus crossed the Station Star.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，太原送楊弁與其同惡五十四人來獻，斬於狗脊嶺。

translations.literal: On xinyou Taiyuan sent Yang Bian and fifty-four fellow evildoers to be presented; executed at Gouji Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Yang Bian and fifty-four rebels were executed at Gouji Ridge.

sentences.zh: 三月，以晉絳副招討石雄為澤潞西面招討，以汾州刺史李丕為副。

translations.literal: Third month: Jin-Jiang vice campaign Shi Xiong was made Ze-Lu western campaign commissioner; Fenzhou prefect Li Pi vice.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong and Li Pi led the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 以道士趙歸真為左右街道門教授先生。

translations.literal: Daoist Zhao Guizhen was made Left-Right Street Gate professor master.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guizhen became street-gate professor master.

sentences.zh: 時帝志學神仙，師歸真。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor's intent studied immortals, taking Guizhen as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong studied immortality under Zhao Guizhen.

sentences.zh: 歸真乘寵，每對，排毀釋氏，言非中國之教，蠹耗生靈，盡宜除去，帝頗信之。

translations.literal: Guizhen riding favor each audience slandered Buddhism, saying it was not China's teaching, harrying and wasting the living—all should be removed; the Emperor quite believed.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhen urged destroying Buddhism as foreign and wasteful; Wuzong believed him.

sentences.zh: 四月，王宰進軍攻澤州。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Wang Zai advanced attacking Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai besieged Ze prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五月，以司農卿薛元賞為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Minister of Agriculture Xue Yuan Shang was made Jingzhao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan Shang became Jingzhao prefect.

sentences.zh: 六月，金紫光祿大夫、尚書右僕射、中書侍郎、同平事、判度支崔珙貶澧州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Gold-Purple Grand Master, Right Vice Director, Secretariat Vice Director, Grand Councillor overseeing finances Cui Gong was demoted Lizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Cui Gong was banished to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，敕：「諫官論事，所見不同，連狀署名，事同糾率。

translations.literal: On guichou an edict: "When remonstrance officials debate affairs and their views differ, joint petitions with signed names resemble coordinated accusation."
translations.idiomatic: On guichou an edict barred remonstrators from joint-signed petitions except on major policy.

sentences.zh: 此後凡論公事，各隨己見，不得連署姓名。

translations.literal: "Henceforth in all public debate each shall follow his own view and may not sign names together."
translations.idiomatic: "Each must state his own view; collective signatures were forbidden."

sentences.zh: 如有大政奏論，即可連署。

translations.literal: "When great policy is memorialized, joint signature is permitted."
translations.idiomatic: "Great-policy memorials could still be jointly signed."

sentences.zh: 」制追削故左軍中尉仇士良先授官及贈官，其家財並籍沒。

translations.literal: An edict also stripped posthumously from former Left Army Vice Commander Chou Shiliang his prior grants and mourning titles; his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The edict also posthumously stripped Chou Shiliang's ranks and confiscated his estate.

sentences.zh: 士良死後，中人於其家得兵仗數千件，兼發士良宿罪故也。

translations.literal: After Shiliang's death eunuchs found thousands of weapons at his home — also because old crimes were exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs found thousands of weapons in his house after his death, reopening old crimes.

sentences.zh: 敕責授官銀青光祿大夫、澧州刺史、上柱國、安平郡開國公、食邑二千戶崔珙再貶恩州司馬員外置，以珙領鹽鐵時欠宋滑院鹽鐵九十萬貫。

translations.literal: An edict demoted again Silver-Green Grandee, Lizhou prefect, Pillar of State, Duke of Anping with two thousand households Cui Gong to Enzhou acting staff member — Gong, while overseeing salt and iron, owed the Song-Hua office ninety million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong was banished to Enzhou for a ninety-million-string salt debt from his monopoly tenure.

sentences.zh: 帝令度支、鹽鐵、轉運合為一使。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Revenue, Salt and Iron, and Transport merged into one commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue, salt, and transport were consolidated under one commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七月，以淮南節度使、檢校司空杜悰守尚書右僕射、兼門下侍郎、同平章事，仍判度支，充鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Huainan military commissioner, acting Minister of Works Du Cong was made Right Vice Director, concurrent Secretariat Vice Director, Grand Councillor, still overseeing Revenue, and salt-and-transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Du Cong became right vice director and grand councillor with the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 又制銀青光祿大夫、守尚書右僕射、兼門下侍郎、同平章事、監修國史、上柱國、趙郡開國公、食邑二千戶李紳可檢校司空、平章事、揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度副大使、知節度事。

translations.literal: An edict: Silver-Green Grandee, Right Vice Director, concurrent Secretariat Vice Director, Grand Councillor, overseer of national history, Pillar of State, Duke of Zhao with two thousand households Li Shen was made acting Minister of Works, Grand Councillor, Yangzhou metropolitan governor, and Huainan deputy military commissioner in charge of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen took Huainan and the council seal as acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 吏部條奏中外合減官員一千一百一十四員。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel memorialized that central and local offices should cut one thousand one hundred fourteen posts.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel proposed cutting more than eleven hundred posts empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 王元逵奏邢州刺史裴問、別將高元武以城降。

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui memorialized that Xingzhou prefect Pei Wen and adjutant Gao Yuanwu surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui reported Xingzhou had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 洺州刺史王釗、磁州刺史安玉以城降何弘敬。

translations.literal: Luozhou prefect Wang Zhao and Cizhou prefect An Yu surrendered their cities to He Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou and Cizhou also surrendered to He Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 山東三州平。

translations.literal: The three eastern provinces were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The three Shandong prefectures were pacified.

sentences.zh: 潞州大將郭誼、張谷、陳揚廷遣人至王宰軍，請殺稹以自贖。

translations.literal: Lu prefecture generals Guo Yi, Zhang Gu, and Chen Yangting sent men to Wang Zai's army asking to kill Zhen to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Lu generals offered to kill Zhen if Wang Zai would spare them.

sentences.zh: 王宰以聞，乃詔石雄率軍七千入潞州，誼斬劉稹首以迎雄，澤、潞等五州平。

translations.literal: Wang Zai reported it; an edict ordered Shi Xiong to lead seven thousand troops into Lu; Yi beheaded Liu Zhen's head to welcome Xiong — Ze, Lu, and five other prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong entered Lu; Guo Yi sent Zhen's head and five prefectures fell.

sentences.zh: 八月戊戌，王宰傳稹首與大將郭誼等一百五十人，露布獻於京師，上御安福門受俘，百僚樓前稱賀。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuxu: Wang Zai forwarded Zhen's head with Guo Yi and one hundred fifty others; a victory bulletin was presented at the capital; the Emperor received captives at Anfu Gate; the hundred officials hailed him before the tower.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Wang Zai's victory train reached Chang'an; Wuzong received captives at Anfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 以魏博節度使、檢校尚書右僕射、同平章事何弘敬進封廬江郡開國公，食邑二千戶；

translations.literal: Weibo military commissioner, acting Right Vice Director, Grand Councillor He Hongjing was advanced to Duke of Lujiang with two thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing became Duke of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 以成德軍節度使王元逵檢校司空、兼太子太師、同平章事，進封太原郡開國公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Chengde military commissioner Wang Yuankui was made acting Minister of Works, concurrent Heir-apparent Junior Preceptor, Grand Councillor, advanced to Duke of Taiyuan with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui became duke of Taiyuan and entered the council.

sentences.zh: 宰相李德裕守太尉，進封衛國公，加食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Li Deyu was made Grand Preceptor, advanced to Duke of Weiguo, household increased one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu became grand preceptor and Duke of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎、翰林學士承旨崔鉉為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War, Hanlin academician-in-chief Cui Xuan was made Secretariat Vice Director and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan joined the Grand Council from the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使陳夷行卒。

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Chen Yixing died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing died at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 九月，以天德軍使、晉絳行營招討使石雄檢校兵部尚書、河中尹、兼御史大夫、河中晉絳慈隰等州節度使。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Tiande army commander, Jin-He campaign commissioner Shi Xiong was made acting Minister of War, Hezhong metropolitan governor, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Hezhong-Jin-He-Ci-Li military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong took Hezhong and the Jin-He command.

sentences.zh: 以前山南東道節度使盧鈞檢校尚書左僕射、潞州大都督府長史，充昭義軍節度使、澤潞邢洺觀察等使。

translations.literal: Former Shannan East military commissioner Lu Jun was made acting Left Vice Director, Lu metropolitan governor, Zhaoyi military commissioner, and Ze-Lu-Xing-Luo observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jun received Zhaoyi and the Lu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以忠武軍節度、陳許蔡等州觀察處置等使、河陽行營諸軍招討使、金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射、兼御史大夫、上柱國、太原郡開國公、食邑二千戶王宰檢校司空、太原尹、北都留守，充河東節度、管內觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Zhongwu military commissioner, Chen-Xu-Cai observation and disposition commissioner, Heyang campaign commissioner, Gold-Purple Grandee, acting Right Vice Director, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, Duke of Taiyuan with two thousand households Wang Zai was made acting Minister of Works, Taiyuan metropolitan governor, northern capital regent, and Hedong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai became Hedong regent and acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「逆賊郭誼等，狐鼠之妖，依丘穴而作固；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The rebel Guo Yi and others — fox-and-rat demons nesting in hill burrows;
translations.idiomatic: "Rebels like Guo Yi," the edict began, "were vermin in their dens;

sentences.zh: 牛羊之力，得水草而逾兇。

translations.literal: cattle and sheep that grow fiercer with grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: beasts that grew bold with pasture and stream."

sentences.zh: 久從叛臣，皆負逆氣。

translations.literal: Long following traitors, all bore rebellious air.
translations.idiomatic: They had long served traitors and breathed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 劉從諫背德反義，掩賊藏奸，積其怙亂之謀，無非親吏之計。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian turned his back on virtue and righteousness, hid villains and treachery, piled defiant plots — all the schemes of intimate clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian's defiance and hidden plots were the work of his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 劉公直、安全慶等各憑地險，屢抗王師，每肆悖言，罔懷革面。

translations.literal: Liu Gongzhi, An Qingqing, and others each relied on terrain and repeatedly resisted the royal army, always with reckless words, never thinking to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongzhi and An Qingqing held the passes and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 況郭誼、王協聞邢、洺歸款，懼義旅覆巢，賣孽童以圖全，據堅城而請命。

translations.literal: Moreover Guo Yi and Wang Xie, hearing Xing and Luo had submitted, feared righteous troops would overturn their nest, sold the wicked child to save themselves, and held the strong city begging mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi and Wang Xie sold Zhen's heir and begged mercy when Xing and Luo fell.

sentences.zh: 昔伍被詣吏，不免就誅；

translations.literal: In old times Wu Bei went to the magistrate and still could not escape execution;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bei surrendered and still died;

sentences.zh: 延岑出降，終亦夷族。

translations.literal: Yan Cen came out and submitted, yet his clan was also exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Cen's clan was wiped out despite his surrender.

sentences.zh: 致之大辟，無所愧懷。

translations.literal: To impose the great punishment leaves no room for shame.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was owed without remorse."

sentences.zh: 」郭誼、劉公直、王協、安全慶、李道德、李佐堯、劉稹、稹母阿裴、稹弟曹九、滿郎、君郎、妹四娘、五娘、從兄洪卿、漢卿、周卿、魯卿、匡堯、張谷男涯、解愁、陳揚廷弟宣、男醜奴、張溢男歡郎、三寶、門客甄戈、伎術人郭諗、蔣黨、李訓兄仲京、王涯侄孫羽、韓約男茂章、茂寶、王璠男珪等，並處斬于獨柳。

translations.literal: Guo Yi, Liu Gongzhi, Wang Xie, An Qingqing, Li Daode, Li Zuoyao, Liu Zhen, Zhen's mother A Pei, Zhen's younger brothers Cao Jiu, Manlang, Junlang, sisters Fourth Daughter and Fifth Daughter, cousins Hongqing, Hanqing, Zhouqing, Luqing, Kuangyao, Zhang Gu's son Ya, Jiechou, Chen Yangting's younger brother Xuan, son Chounu, Zhang Yi's son Huanlang, Sanbao, retainers Zhen Ge, wonder-workers Guo Shen, Jiang Dang, Li Xun's elder brother Zhongjing, Wang Ya's grandnephew Yu, Han Yue's sons Maozhang and Maobao, Wang Fan's son Gui, and others were all executed at Solitary Willow.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi, Liu Gongzhi, Wang Xie, the Zhen family, Zhang Gu, Chen Yangting, retainers, and accomplices were beheaded at Solitary Willow.

sentences.zh: 敕以河陽三城鎮遏使為孟州，割澤州隸焉，與懷、孟、澤為節度，號河陽。

translations.literal: An edict made the Heyang three-cities suppression commissioner into Mengzhou, detached Zezhou to it, with Huai, Meng, and Ze as a circuit named Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang circuit was reorganized with Mengzhou and Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 制以皇子愕為開府儀同三司、夏州刺史、朔方軍節度大使。

translations.literal: An edict made the imperial son E Prince with opening privileges, Xia prefect, and Shuofang military commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Prince E was sent to Xia and Shuofang with full honors.

sentences.zh: 時党項叛，命親王以制之。

translations.literal: At the time the Tangut rebelled; a prince was ordered to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: A Tangut revolt prompted a princely command on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十月，車駕幸鄠縣。

translations.literal: Tenth month: the carriage visited E county.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court visited E county.

sentences.zh: 十一月，幸雲陽。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: visited Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month it visited Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，敕：「郊禮日近，獄囚數多，案款已成，多有翻覆。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, edict: "The suburban sacrifice draws near; prisoners are many; cases concluded often overturn."
translations.idiomatic: A twelfth-month edict ordered swift closure of prisoners before the suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 其兩京、天下州府見繋囚，已結正及兩度翻案伏款者，並令先事結斷訖申。

translations.literal: All prisoners held in the two capitals and circuits whose cases were concluded or who had twice confessed after reversal were to be finally judged and reported first.
translations.idiomatic: Closed cases and double-confessed prisoners were to be sentenced at once.

sentences.zh: 」時左僕射王起頻年知貢舉，每貢院考試訖，上榜後，更呈宰相取可否。

translations.literal: At the time Left Vice Director Wang Qi had for years overseen the examinations; after each session ended and the list was posted, he again presented it to the chief ministers for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi still routed examination lists through the premiers for approval.

sentences.zh: 後人數不多，宰相延英論言：「主司試藝，不合取宰相與奪。

translations.literal: Later, with few candidates, the chief ministers discussed at Yanying: "The chief examiner tests arts; he should not let the chief ministers decide pass or fail.
translations.idiomatic: Premiers argued examiners, not councillors, should pass candidates.

sentences.zh: 比來貢舉艱難，放人絕少，恐非弘訪之道。

translations.literal: Recently examinations have been hard and few passed — this may not be the way to seek talent broadly."
translations.idiomatic: "Too few pass now — that is no way to find talent," they said.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「貢院不會我意。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The examination hall does not grasp my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong said the examiners missed his intent.

sentences.zh: 不放子弟，即太過，無論子弟、寒門，但取實藝耳。

translations.literal: If they do not pass my sons' protégés, that is excessive; whether sons of ministers or poor scholars, take only real talent."
translations.idiomatic: "Pass real talent, not just ministerial sons — but do not shut out my men entirely."

sentences.zh: 」李德裕對曰：「鄭肅、封敖有好子弟，不敢應舉。

translations.literal: Li Deyu replied: "Zheng Su and Feng Ao have worthy sons who dare not sit the examination."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu noted worthy sons of Zheng Su and Feng Ao feared to test.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我比聞楊虞卿兄弟朋比貴勢，妨平人道路。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I lately heard the Yang Yuqing brothers banded with the powerful and blocked commoners' paths.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong cited the Yang Yuqing clique's favoritism.

sentences.zh: 昨楊知至、鄭朴之徒，並令落下，抑其太甚耳。

translations.literal: Yesterday Yang Zhizhi, Zheng Pu, and the like were all struck from the list — only to curb them."
translations.idiomatic: "I struck Yang Zhizhi and Zheng Pu from the list to curb that excess."

sentences.zh: 」德裕曰：「臣無名第，不合言進士之非。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Your servant has no examination degree and ought not speak ill of jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu demurred: without a degree he should not judge jinshi.

sentences.zh: 然臣祖天寶末以仕進無他伎，勉強隨計，一舉登第。

translations.literal: Yet your servant's grandfather in the Tianbao era, with no other skill for office, forced himself into the quota and passed in one attempt.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had forced one Tianbao pass without other skill.

sentences.zh: 自後不於私家置《文選》，蓋惡其祖尚浮華，不根藝實。

translations.literal: Afterward he kept no Wenxuan in the household — he hated its ancestors' love of ornament without rooted craft.
translations.idiomatic: The family thereafter shunned the Wenxuan and its ornamental style.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷顯官，須是公卿子弟。

translations.literal: Yet court eminent officials must be sons of dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet high office still belongs to ministerial sons," he said.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 自小便習舉業，自熟朝廷間事，臺閣儀范，班行准則，不教而自成。

translations.literal: From childhood they practice the examination curriculum, naturally know court affairs, terrace etiquette, and row standards — formed without teaching.
translations.idiomatic: They grew up inside court ritual and examination drill.

sentences.zh: 寒士縱有出人之才，登第之後，始得一班一級，固不能熟習也。

translations.literal: Poor scholars with outstanding talent, after passing, only then reach one grade and one rank — they cannot be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Poor scholars learn rank only after they pass.

sentences.zh: 則子弟成名，不可輕矣。

translations.literal: Thus when sons of families achieve fame, it cannot be lightly regarded."
translations.idiomatic: "So ministerial sons who pass cannot be lightly dismissed."

sentences.zh: 」會昌五年五年春正月己酉朔，敕造望仙臺於南郊壇。

translations.literal: Huichang 5, first month, jiyou new moon: an edict built the Terrace of Gazing for Immortals at the southern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou of Huichang 5's first month work began on the Gazing-for-Immortals terrace.

sentences.zh: 時道士趙歸真特承恩禮，諫官上疏，論之延英。

translations.literal: At the time the Daoist Zhao Guizhen enjoyed special favor; remonstrance officials memorialized; discussion reached Yanying.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators attacked Zhao Guizhen's favor at Yanying.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰臣曰：「諫官論趙歸真，此意要卿等知。

translations.literal: The Emperor told the chief ministers: "When remonstrance officials discuss Zhao Guizhen, I want you to know my mind.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong told his premiers to understand his mind on Zhao Guizhen.

sentences.zh: 朕宮中無事，屏去聲技，但要此人道話耳。

translations.literal: In the palace I have nothing to do and have put away music — I only want this man to talk the Way."
translations.idiomatic: "I have banished music; I only want his conversation."

sentences.zh: 」李德裕對曰：「臣不敢言前代得失，只緣歸真於敬宗朝出入宮掖，以此人情不願陛下復親近之。

translations.literal: Li Deyu replied: "Your servant dare not speak of former dynasties' gains and losses — only because Guizhen in Jingzong's reign went in and out of the inner palaces, popular feeling does not wish Your Majesty to draw near him again."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu warned that Guizhen had haunted Jingzong's inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我爾時已識此道人，不知名歸真，只呼趙鍊師。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I already knew this Daoist then, not knowing the name Guizhen — I only called him Master Zhao the Refiner.
translations.idiomatic: "I knew him as Master Zhao the Refiner in Jingzong's day," Wuzong said.

sentences.zh: 在敬宗時亦無甚過。

translations.literal: In Jingzong's time he also had no great fault.
translations.idiomatic: "He did little harm then."

sentences.zh: 我與之言，滌煩爾。

translations.literal: When I speak with him, it washes vexation.
translations.idiomatic: "He eases my vexation."

sentences.zh: 至於軍國政事，唯卿等與次對官論，何須問道士。

translations.literal: As for military and state affairs, only you and the secondary audience officials debate — why ask a Daoist?
translations.idiomatic: "State affairs are yours — why ask a Daoist?"

sentences.zh: 非直一歸真，百歸真亦不能相惑。

translations.literal: Not only one Guizhen — a hundred Guizhens could not confuse me."
translations.idiomatic: "A hundred such men could not sway me."

sentences.zh: 」歸真自以涉物論，遂舉羅浮道士鄧元起有長年之術，帝遣中使迎之。

translations.literal: Guizhen, because he touched public debate, then presented the Luofu Daoist Deng Yuanqi, who had arts of long life; the Emperor sent a palace envoy to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhen offered Deng Yuanqi of Luofu; the court sent envoys to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 由是與衡山道士劉玄靖及歸真膠固，排毀釋氏，而拆寺之請行焉。

translations.literal: Hence he bonded with Hengshan Daoist Liu Xuanjing and Guizhen, slandered Buddhism, and the request to demolish temples went forward.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Xuanjing he pressed anti-Buddhist temple closures.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李德裕、杜悰、李讓夷、崔鉉、太常卿孫簡等率文武百僚上徽號曰仁聖文武章天成功神德明道皇帝。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Li Deyu, Du Cong, Li Rangyi, Cui Xuan, Minister of Rites Sun Jian, and others led the hundred civil and military officials in offering the honorific Benevolent Sagely Martial Literary Heavenly Successful Spirit Virtue Bright Way Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu, Du Cong, and the court offered the honorific Benevolent Sagely Martial Literary Heavenly Successful Spirit Virtue Bright Way Emperor.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，有事於郊廟，禮畢，御承天門，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On xinhai the suburban rites were performed; when ritual ended, he took Cheng Tian Gate and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the suburban rites ended with universal amnesty at Cheng Tian Gate.

sentences.zh: 庚申，義安太后崩，敬宗之母也。

translations.literal: On gengshen the Yi'an empress dowager died — Jingzong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Jingzong's mother, the Yi'an empress dowager, died.

sentences.zh: 遺令皇帝三日聽政，十三日小祥，二十五日大祥，二十七日釋服。

translations.literal: Her testament ordered the Emperor to hear government three days, small mourning on the thirteenth day, great mourning on the twenty-fifth, and release of mourning on the twenty-seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Her will set a twenty-seven-day mourning schedule.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書歸融奏：「事貴得中，禮從順變，配祔之禮，宜有等差。

translations.literal: Minister of War Gui Rong memorialized: "Affairs should hit the mean; ritual should follow change; the rites of spirit-tablet placement should have graded differences.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Rong urged a shortened mourning schedule.

sentences.zh: 請降服期，以日易月，十二日釋服。

translations.literal: I ask to reduce the mourning period, exchanging months for days — release mourning on the twelfth day.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed twelve days instead of months.

sentences.zh: 內外臣僚，亦請以其日釋服。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials also please release mourning on that day.
translations.idiomatic: Officials inside and out should mourn twelve days.

sentences.zh: 陵園制度，請無降殺。

translations.literal: Mausoleum regulations — please do not reduce.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb observances should not be cut.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 以前太原節度使、檢校司空李石以本官充東都留守。

translations.literal: Former Taiyuan military commissioner, acting Minister of Works Li Shi was made eastern capital regent in his present rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi became Luoyang regent.

sentences.zh: 二月戊寅朔，太白掩昴之北側。

translations.literal: Second month, wuyin new moon: Venus covered the north side of the Pleiades.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Venus veiled the Pleiades' northern horn.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫、權知禮部貢舉陳商選士三十七人中第，物論以為請托，令翰林學士白敏中覆試，落張瀆、李玗、薛忱、張覿、崔凜、王諶、劉伯芻等七人。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official acting Minister of Rites examiner Chen Shang chose thirty-seven candidates to pass; public opinion held it was patronage; the Emperor ordered Hanlin academician Bai Minzhong to re-examine and struck Zhang Du, Li Yu, Xue Chen, Zhang Di, Cui Lin, Wang Chen, Liu Bochu, and seven others.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong's re-exam struck seven of Chen Shang's thirty-seven passes as patronage.

sentences.zh: 三月，崔鉉罷知政事，出為陝虢觀察使。

translations.literal: Third month: Cui Xuan left the council and went out as Shan-Guo observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan left the council for Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞、兼兵部侍郎李回本官同平章事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief, concurrent Vice Minister of War Li Hui was made Grand Councillor in his original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui joined the council from the censorate.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，皇第四女封延慶公主，第五女封靖樂公主。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: the fourth imperial daughter was enfeoffed Princess of Yanqing; the fifth as Princess of Jingle.
translations.idiomatic: Two princesses were enfeoffed in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 敕祠部檢括天下寺及僧尼人數。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to tally temples and monks and nuns empire-wide.
translations.idiomatic: Rites was ordered to count every temple and cleric.

sentences.zh: 大凡寺四千六百，蘭若四萬，僧尼二十六萬五百。

translations.literal: In all, temples four thousand six hundred, hermitages forty thousand, monks and nuns two hundred sixty thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The tally found 4,600 temples, 40,000 hermitages, and 260,500 clerics.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜悰罷知政事。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Du Cong left the council.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong left the council.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎、判戶部崔元式同平章事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue, acting Revenue overseer Cui Yuanshi was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanshi joined the council from Revenue.

sentences.zh: 六月丙子，敕：「漢、魏已來，朝廷大政，必下公卿詳議，博求理道，以盡群情。

translations.literal: Sixth month, bingzi, edict: "From Han and Wei onward, great court policy had to go to the dukes and ministers for detailed debate, broadly seeking the Way, to exhaust popular feeling.
translations.idiomatic: A sixth-month edict revived Han-Wei consultation on law and ritual.

sentences.zh: 所以政必有經，人皆向道。

translations.literal: Thus government had constants and people faced the Way.
translations.idiomatic: "So policy had roots and the people had a path."

sentences.zh: 此後事關禮法，群情有疑者，令本司申尚書都省，下禮官參議。

translations.literal: Hereafter when ritual and law are involved and popular feeling is doubtful, let the originating office report to the Secretariat Directorate and send ritual officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful ritual cases must pass through the directorate and ritual officers.

sentences.zh: 如是刑獄，亦先令法官詳議，然後申刑部參覆。

translations.literal: If criminal cases, first let the judge deliberate in detail, then report to Punishments for review.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal cases must be judged before Punishments reviews them.

sentences.zh: 如郎官、御史有能駁難，或據經史故事，議論精當，即擢授遷改以獎之。

translations.literal: If a bureau official or censor can refute or cite classics and historical precedents with precise argument, promote and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Able refuters among censors and bureau men were to be promoted.

sentences.zh: 如言涉浮華，都無經據，不在申聞。

translations.literal: If words are ornamental and without canonical basis, do not report upward."
translations.idiomatic: "Ornamental argument without canon was not to reach the throne."

sentences.zh: 」神策奏修望仙樓及廊舍五百三十九間功畢。

translations.literal: The Divine Strategy army reported repair of the Terrace of Gazing for Immortals and five hundred thirty-nine corridor rooms completed.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Strategy army finished the Gazing-for-Immortals terrace and 539 rooms.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚子，敕併省天下佛寺。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, gengzi: an edict merged and cut temples empire-wide.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict ordered empire-wide temple mergers.

sentences.zh: 中書門下條疏聞奏：「據令式，諸上州國忌日官吏行香於寺，其上州望各留寺一所，有列聖尊容，便令移於寺內；

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "According to regulations, on the state mourning day of upper prefectures officials burn incense at temples; each upper prefecture and major command should keep one temple with imperial portraits moved inside;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat proposed keeping one portrait temple per upper prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其下州寺並廢。

translations.literal: lower-prefecture temples are all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Lower prefectures were to lose all temples.

sentences.zh: 其上都、東都兩街請留十寺，寺僧十人。

translations.literal: In the two capitals' upper and eastern wards ten temples are requested, ten monks each."
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals might keep ten temples with ten monks each."

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「上州合留寺，工作精妙者留之；

translations.literal: Edict: "Upper prefectures should keep temples whose craftsmanship is exquisite; if ruined, they should also be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong ordered fine upper-prefecture temples kept and ruined ones destroyed.

sentences.zh: 如破落，亦宜廢毀。

translations.literal: If ruined, they should also be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruined temples were to be demolished as well.

sentences.zh: 其合行香日，官吏宜於道觀。

translations.literal: On days for burning incense, officials should use Daoist abbeys.
translations.idiomatic: Incense rites were moved to Daoist halls.

sentences.zh: 其上都、下都每街留寺兩所，寺留僧三十人。

translations.literal: In the upper and lower capitals each street keeps two temples, thirty monks each.
translations.idiomatic: Each capital street would keep two temples and thirty monks.

sentences.zh: 上都左街留慈恩、薦福，右街留西明、莊嚴。

translations.literal: Upper capital left ward keeps Cien and Jianfu; right ward Ximing and Zhuangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an's left ward kept Cien and Jianfu; the right, Ximing and Zhuangyan.

sentences.zh: 」中書又奏：「天下廢寺，銅像、鐘磬委鹽鐵使鑄錢，其鐵像委本州鑄為農器，金、銀、鍮石等像銷付度支。

translations.literal: The Secretariat again memorialized: "Abolished temples empire-wide — bronze statues and bells and chimes are entrusted to the salt commissioner to cast coin; iron statues to the prefecture to cast farm tools; gold, silver, and brass images melted for Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished temples' metal was ordered cast into coin and farm tools.

sentences.zh: 衣冠士庶之家所有金、銀、銅、鐵之像，敕出後限一月納官，如違，委鹽鐵使依禁銅法處分。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, copper, and iron images in gentry households — within one month after the edict they must be surrendered; violators handled by the salt commissioner under the copper prohibition law.
translations.idiomatic: Private metal images had to be surrendered within a month.

sentences.zh: 其土、木、石等像合留寺內依舊。

translations.literal: Clay, wood, and stone images may remain in temples as before."
translations.idiomatic: Clay, wood, and stone images could remain in temples.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「僧尼不合隸祠部，請隸鴻臚寺。

translations.literal: Again memorialized: "Monks and nuns should not be under the Ministry of Rites; please place them under the Court of Imperial Entertainments."
translations.idiomatic: Clerics were transferred from Rites to the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 其大秦穆護等祠，釋教既已釐革，邪法不可獨存。

translations.literal: Da Qin, Muhu, and other shrines — since Buddhism is reformed, heterodox cults cannot stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: Da Qin and Muhu shrines were abolished with Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 其人並勒還俗，遞歸本貫，充稅戶。

translations.literal: Their people are all compelled to return to lay life, sent to native districts as tax households.
translations.idiomatic: Their adherents were forced to laicize and register as taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 如外國人，送還本處收管。

translations.literal: If foreigners, send back to native places for control."
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners were sent home for local control."

translations.literal: End of memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the memorial."

sentences.zh: 八月，制：

translations.literal: Eighth month, edict:
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wuzong proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 「朕聞三代已前，未嘗言佛，漢魏之後，像教寖興。

translations.literal: "I have heard that before the Three Dynasties Buddha was never spoken of; after Han and Wei the image-teaching gradually rose.
translations.idiomatic: "Before the Three Dynasties no one spoke of Buddha; under Han and Wei the image cult spread,"

sentences.zh: 是由季時，傳此異俗，因緣染習，蔓衍滋多。

translations.literal: It came from decadent seasons and spread this alien custom; through cause and condition and habit it grew more and more.
translations.idiomatic: "born of decadent times and grown by habit."

sentences.zh: 以至於蠹耗國風而漸不覺。

translations.literal: Until it harmed national custom and gradually went unnoticed.
translations.idiomatic: "until it ate the state without notice."

sentences.zh: 誘惑人意，而眾益迷。

translations.literal: It seduced human hearts and the masses grew more deluded.
translations.idiomatic: "It deluded hearts and deepened the crowd's trance."

sentences.zh: 洎于九州山原，兩京城闕，僧徒日廣，佛寺日崇。

translations.literal: Down to the nine provinces' mountains and plains, the two capitals' gates and wards — monks daily increased, temples daily rose.
translations.idiomatic: "Monks and temples multiplied through plain and capital alike."

sentences.zh: 勞人力於土木之功，奪人利於金寶之飾，遺君親於師資之際，違配偶于戒律之間。

translations.literal: Laboring men on earth-and-wood works, seizing people's profit in gold-and-jewel adornment, abandoning ruler and kin at the teacher's moment, violating spouses within precepts.
translations.idiomatic: "They wasted labor on timber and gold, forsook kin for teachers, broke marriage for precepts."

sentences.zh: 壞法害人，無逾此道。

translations.literal: Destroying law and harming people — nothing surpasses this path.
translations.idiomatic: "Nothing harmed law and people more."

sentences.zh: 且一夫不田，有受其飢者；

translations.literal: Moreover if one man does not plow, someone suffers hunger;
translations.idiomatic: "One man not plowing means another hungry;"

sentences.zh: 一婦不蠶，有受其寒者。

translations.literal: if one woman does not weave, someone suffers cold.
translations.idiomatic: "one woman not weaving means another cold."

sentences.zh: 今天下僧尼，不可勝數，皆待農而食，待蠶而衣。

translations.literal: Today monks and nuns are beyond counting — all wait on farming to eat, on silkworms to clothe.
translations.idiomatic: "Today's clerics beyond count all eat the farmer's grain and wear the weaver's silk."

sentences.zh: 寺宇招提，莫知紀極，皆雲構藻飾，僭擬宮居。

translations.literal: Temples and roadside shrines beyond reckoning — all cloud-built and painted, usurping and imitating palaces.
translations.idiomatic: "Temples beyond reckoning aped the palace in cloud and paint."

sentences.zh: 晉、宋、齊、梁，物力凋瘵，風俗澆詐，莫不由是而致也。

translations.literal: Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang — material strength withered, customs shallow and deceitful — all from this.
translations.idiomatic: "Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang withered from this very cause."

sentences.zh: 況我高祖、太宗，以武定禍亂，以文理華夏，執此二柄，足以經邦，豈可以區區西方之教，與我抗衡哉！

translations.literal: How much more our High Ancestor and Taizong, who with martial arts settled chaos and calamity, with culture adorned Huaxia — holding these two handles suffices to govern the realm; how can a petty western teaching vie with us!
translations.idiomatic: "Gaozu and Taizong ruled by sword and script — why yield to a western cult?"

sentences.zh: 貞觀、開元，亦嘗釐革，剗除不盡，流衍轉滋。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan and Kaiyuan there were also reforms and cuts, yet not fully removed; the stream spread and grew.
translations.idiomatic: "Even Zhenguan and Kaiyuan could not uproot it wholly."

sentences.zh: 朕博覽前言，旁求輿議，弊之可革，斷在不疑。

translations.literal: I broadly review former words and seek popular debate on all sides — what can be reformed, I cut without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: "What can be cut, I cut without doubt."

sentences.zh: 而中外誠臣，協予至意，條疏至當，宜在必行。

translations.literal: Inner and outer loyal ministers harmonize with my utmost intent; memorials are thoroughly apt and must be executed.
translations.idiomatic: "Loyal ministers' plans must be executed."

sentences.zh: 懲千古之蠹源，成百王之典法，濟人利眾，予何讓焉。

translations.literal: Punishing the thousand-year's vermin source, completing the hundred kings' canonical law, benefiting people and aiding the masses — what would I yield?
translations.idiomatic: "To punish a thousand-year pest and make law for a hundred kings — why should I yield?"

sentences.zh: 其天下所拆寺四千六百餘所，還俗僧尼二十六萬五百人，收充兩稅戶，拆招提、蘭若四萬餘所，收膏腴上田數千萬頃，收奴婢為兩稅戶十五萬人。

translations.literal: Temples demolished empire-wide four thousand six hundred and more, monks and nuns returned to lay life two hundred sixty thousand five hundred, enrolled as two-tax households; roadside shrines and hermitages forty thousand and more demolished, fertile upland fields several tens of millions of mu recovered, bond servants as two-tax households one hundred fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: 4,600 temples were razed, 260,500 clerics laicized, 40,000 shrines cleared, millions of mu and 150,000 bondsmen restored to tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 隸僧尼屬主客，顯明外國之教。

translations.literal: Monks and nuns placed under the Host of Guests — making foreign teaching explicit.
translations.idiomatic: Clerics were placed under the Host of Guests as foreign religion.

sentences.zh: 勒大秦、穆護、祆三千餘人還俗，不雜中華之風。

translations.literal: Compelled Da Qin, Muhu, and Zoroastrian three thousand and more to return to lay life, not mixing with Huaxia custom.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand Da Qin, Muhu, and Zoroastrian adherents were laicized.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The edict cried Alas!

sentences.zh: 前古未行，似將有待；

translations.literal: What antiquity had not done seemed to await its time;
translations.idiomatic: "What antiquity had not done seemed to await its hour;"

sentences.zh: 及今盡去，豈謂無時。

translations.literal: to remove it all today — can one say there is no season?
translations.idiomatic: "to remove it now — can one say the season is wrong?"

sentences.zh: 驅游惰不業之徒，已逾十萬；

translations.literal: Driving idle non-workers has already passed one hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: "More than a hundred thousand idlers were driven back to work;"

sentences.zh: 廢丹雘無用之室，何啻億千。

translations.literal: abandoning cinnabar-painted useless rooms — how few are not in the billions?
translations.idiomatic: "useless painted halls abandoned by the billion."

sentences.zh: 自此清淨訓人，慕無為之理；

translations.literal: Henceforth pure instruction trains people, admiring the principle of non-action;
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth pure teaching and wuwei shall train the people;"

sentences.zh: 簡易齊政，成一俗之功。

translations.literal: simple government aligns policy, completing one custom's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: "simple rule shall align the realm."

sentences.zh: 將使六合黔黎，同歸皇化。

translations.literal: It will make the six realms' black-haired people together return to imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: "All under heaven shall return to imperial transformation."

sentences.zh: 尚以革弊之始，日用不知，下制明廷，宜體予意。

translations.literal: Still, at the start of reform daily use is not yet known; issue edicts in the bright court — you should embody my intent.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet at reform's start the court must embody my intent."

translations.literal: Closing quote of edict."
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict."

sentences.zh: 制第六女封樂溫公主，第七女封長寧公主。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed the sixth daughter Princess of Lewen; the seventh as Princess of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth and seventh daughters became princesses of Lewen and Changning.

sentences.zh: 中書奏：「伏見公主上表稱『妾某者』，伏以臣妾之義，取其賤稱；

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "We see princesses' memorials say 'your concubine so-and-so' — the meaning of subject-concubine takes the humble title;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat asked princesses to drop the term "concubine" in memorials.

sentences.zh: 家人之禮，即宜區別。

translations.literal: family ritual should be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Family ritual required distinct forms.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，公主上表，請如長公主之例，並云『某邑公主幾女上表』，郡、縣主亦望依此例稱謂。

translations.literal: We deliberated: princess memorials should follow chief princess precedent, all saying 'such-and-such princess, such number daughter memorializes' — commandery and county princesses also should follow this form."
translations.idiomatic: Princesses were to sign as "Princess of X, Nth Daughter" instead.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 九月，火星犯上將。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Mars transgressed the Upper General.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Mars crossed the Upper General.

sentences.zh: 十月乙亥，中書奏：「汜水縣武牢關是太宗擒王世充、竇建德之地，關城東峰有二聖塑容，在一堂之內。

translations.literal: Tenth month, yihai: the Secretariat memorialized: "Sishui county's Wulao Pass is where Taizong captured Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande; on the pass's east peak are statues of the two sages in one hall.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Secretariat proposed a shrine at Wulao Pass.

sentences.zh: 伏以山河如舊，城壘猶存，威靈皆盛於軒臺，風雲疑還於豐沛。

translations.literal: We submit that mountains and rivers are as of old, ramparts remain — awe and spirit flourish at Xuantai, wind and cloud seem to return to Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: "The landscape still holds Taizong's victory," they wrote.

sentences.zh: 誠宜百代嚴奉，萬邦式瞻。

translations.literal: Truly it should be strictly honored for a hundred generations, beheld by ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: "It deserves eternal veneration."

sentences.zh: 西漢故事，祖宗嘗行幸處，皆令邦國立廟。

translations.literal: Western Han precedent: wherever ancestors once traveled, each state established a temple.
translations.idiomatic: Han precedent placed temples at imperial visit sites.

sentences.zh: 今緣定覺寺例合毀拆。

translations.literal: Now because Dingjue Temple by regulation should be demolished.
translations.idiomatic: Dingjue Temple there faced demolition.

sentences.zh: 望取寺中大殿材木，於東峰以造一殿，四面置宮牆，伏望名為昭武廟，以昭聖祖武功之盛。

translations.literal: We hope to take the great hall's timber on the east peak to build one hall, set palace walls on four sides, and name it Zhaowu Temple to display the holy ancestor's martial glory.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to build Zhaowu Temple from Dingjue's timber on the east peak.

sentences.zh: 委懷孟節度使差判官一人勾當。

translations.literal: Entrust the Huai-Meng military commissioner to assign one supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-Meng was to supervise construction.

sentences.zh: 緣聖像年代已久，望令李石於東都揀好畫手，就增嚴飾。

translations.literal: Because the sacred images are long aged, we hope Li Shi at the eastern capital will select skilled painters to enhance and adorn them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was to send painters to restore the statues.

sentences.zh: 初興功日，望令東都差分司官一員薦告。

translations.literal: On the day work begins, we hope the eastern capital will send a branch-court officer to offer prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang was to send an officer to open the rites.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲辰，敕：「悲田養病坊，緣僧尼還俗，無人主持，恐殘疾無以取給，兩京量給寺田賑濟。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jiachen, edict: "Charity wards for the sick — because monks and nuns returned to lay life there is no one to manage them; we fear the disabled will have no support; the two capitals are to grant temple fields for relief.
translations.idiomatic: A jiachen edict funded charity wards after clerics were laicized.

sentences.zh: 諸州府七頃至十頃，各于本管選耆壽一人勾當，以充粥料。

translations.literal: Circuits and prefectures seven to ten qing each — select one elder in the jurisdiction to manage porridge supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture was to allot fields and an elder for soup kitchens.

translations.literal: Closing quote of edict."
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict."

sentences.zh: 十二月，車駕幸咸陽。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: the carriage visited Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the court visited Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 給事中韋弘質上疏，論中書權重，三司錢穀不合相府兼領。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Hongzhi memorialized that the Secretariat's power was too heavy and the three offices' money and grain should not be jointly held by the council chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hongzhi argued premiers should not control the treasury.

sentences.zh: 宰相奏論之曰：

translations.literal: The chief ministers memorialized in reply:
translations.idiomatic: The premiers rebutted in a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「臣等昨于延英對，恭聞聖旨常欲朝廷尊，臣下肅，此是陛下深究理本也。

translations.literal: "We yesterday faced Yanying and respectfully heard Your Majesty's constant wish that the court be honored and ministers solemn — this is Your Majesty's deep probe of principle's root.
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty wishes a honored court and solemn ministers," they began.

sentences.zh: 臣按《管子》云：『凡國之重器，莫重於令。

translations.literal: We cite Guanzi: "Of a state's heavy vessels none is heavier than the command.
translations.idiomatic: They cited Guanzi on the weight of commands.

sentences.zh: 令重則君尊，君尊則國安。

translations.literal: When commands are heavy the lord is honored; when the lord is honored the state is secure.
translations.idiomatic: "Heavy commands make a honored lord and a secure state."

sentences.zh: 故國安在於尊君，尊君在於行令。

translations.literal: Thus state security lies in honoring the lord; honoring the lord lies in executing commands.
translations.idiomatic: "Security lies in honoring the lord through executing commands."

sentences.zh: 君人之理，本莫要於出令。

translations.literal: The lord's principle — nothing is more essential than issuing commands.
translations.idiomatic: "Nothing is more essential than issuing commands."

sentences.zh: 故曰：虧令者死，益令者死，不行令者死，不從令者死。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: one who damages commands dies, one who adds to commands dies, one who does not execute commands dies, one who does not follow commands dies."
translations.idiomatic: "Who damages, adds, or ignores commands dies."

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『令行於上，而下論可不可，是上失其威，下繫於人也。

translations.literal: Also: "When commands issue above and below debate whether they can or cannot, the superior loses awe and the inferior is tied to persons."
translations.idiomatic: "Debate below the throne means the superior loses awe."

sentences.zh: 』自大和已來，其風大弊，令出於上，非之於下。

translations.literal: From Dahe onward this wind has greatly decayed — commands issue above and are faulted below.
translations.idiomatic: "Since Dahe commands have been faulted from below."

sentences.zh: 此弊不除，無以理國也。

translations.literal: Unless this decay is removed, there is no way to govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: "This decay must be removed to govern."

sentences.zh: 昨韋弘質所論宰相不合兼領錢穀。

translations.literal: Yesterday Wei Hongzhi discussed that chief ministers should not jointly hold money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: "Hongzhi said premiers must not hold the treasury," they wrote.

sentences.zh: 臣等輒以事體陳聞。

translations.literal: We hastened to state the matter's substance.
translations.idiomatic: They laid out the matter's substance.

sentences.zh: 昔匡衡所以云：『大臣者，國家之股肱，萬姓所瞻仰，明王所慎擇。

translations.literal: In old times Kuang Heng said: "Great ministers are the state's thighs and arms, the myriad people's gaze, what the bright king carefully chooses."
translations.idiomatic: They quoted Kuang Heng on great ministers as the state's limbs.

sentences.zh: 』《傳》曰：『下輕其上，賤人圖柄，則國家搖動，而人不靜。

translations.literal: The Classic of Changes says: "When inferiors slight superiors, base men plot the handle, the state shakes and people are unquiet."
translations.idiomatic: They quoted the Changes on base men grasping power.

sentences.zh: 』弘質受人教導，輒獻封章，是則賤人圖柄矣。

translations.literal: Hongzhi received others' teaching and hastily offered a sealed memorial — this is base men plotting the handle.
translations.idiomatic: "Hongzhi, taught by others, is a base man plotting the handle."

sentences.zh: 蕭望之漢朝名儒重德，為御史大夫，奏云：『今首歲日月少光，罪在臣等，』上以望之意輕丞相，乃下侍中御史詰問。

translations.literal: Xiao Wangzhi in Han was a famed Confucian of heavy virtue; as Censor-in-Chief he memorialized: "This year at year's start sun and moon have little light — the fault lies in your servants" — the Emperor thought Wangzhi's meaning slighted the chief minister and sent attendants and censors to interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: They cited Xiao Wangzhi punished for slighting his chief.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，監察御史陳師合上書云：『人之思慮有限，一人不可兼總數職。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, Supervising Censor Chen Shihe memorialized: "Human thought has limits — one man cannot oversee many offices."
translations.idiomatic: They cited Chen Shihe's limit on one man's offices.

sentences.zh: 』太宗曰：『此人妄有譭謗，欲離間我君臣。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "This man rashly slanders, wishing to divide my lord and ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong called it slander meant to divide lord and ministers.

sentences.zh: 』流師合於嶺外。

translations.literal: Chen Shihe was exiled beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 賈誼云：『人主如堂，群臣如陛，陛高則堂高。

translations.literal: Jia Yi said: "The lord is like the hall, ministers like the steps — when steps are high the hall is high."
translations.idiomatic: They quoted Jia Yi: high steps mean a high hall.

sentences.zh: 』亦由將相重則君尊，其勢然也。

translations.literal: Also when generals and ministers are heavy the lord is honored — such is the tendency.
translations.idiomatic: "Heavy ministers make a honored lord."

sentences.zh: 如宰相奸謀隱匿，則人人皆得上論。

translations.literal: If chief ministers hide treacherous plots, then everyone may debate above.
translations.idiomatic: "Hidden treason can still be exposed from below."

sentences.zh: 至於制置職業，固是人主之柄，非小人所得干議。

translations.literal: As for setting offices and duties, solidly it is the lord's handle — not what petty men may debate.
translations.idiomatic: "Office-making is the lord's handle, not petty men's debate."

sentences.zh: 古者朝廷之上，各守其官，思不出位。

translations.literal: In antiquity at court each kept his office; thought did not stray from post.
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity each kept his office."

sentences.zh: 弘質賤人，豈得以非所宜言上瀆明主，此是輕宰相撓時政也。

translations.literal: Hongzhi is a base man — how can he with unsuitable words ascend to the bright lord, slighting chief ministers and disturbing current policy — this is slighting the chief minister and shaking policy.
translations.idiomatic: "Hongzhi's words slight the council and shake policy."

sentences.zh: 昔東漢處士橫議，遂有黨錮事起，此事深要懲絕。

translations.literal: In Eastern Han recluses debated horizontally and the Partisan Proscription arose — this matter deeply needs punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They warned of Eastern Han-style faction debate.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下詳其奸詐，去其朋徒，則朝廷安靜，制令肅然。

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will examine their treachery and remove their cliques — then the court will be quiet and commands solemn.
translations.idiomatic: "Remove their cliques and the court will be quiet."

sentences.zh: 臣等不勝感憤之至。

translations.literal: We cannot overcome our indignant feeling to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: "We are indignant to the utmost."

sentences.zh: 」弘質坐貶官。

translations.literal: Closing quote of memorial." Hongzhi was punished with demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the memorial. Hongzhi was demoted.

sentences.zh: 又奏曰：「天寶已前，中書除機密遷授之外，其他政事皆與中書舍人同商量。

translations.literal: Again memorialized: "Before Tianbao, apart from confidential appointments the Secretariat discussed other government with Secretariat drafters.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to restore pre-Tianbao consultation with drafters.

sentences.zh: 自艱難已來，務從權便，政頗去於臺閣，事多繋於軍期，決遣萬機，不暇博議。

translations.literal: Since hardship, expedients were followed; government largely left the terrace offices; affairs mostly tied to military deadlines; deciding the myriad tasks left no leisure for broad debate.
translations.idiomatic: "Since hardship, broad debate was lost to military haste."

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，今後除機密公事外，諸候表疏、百僚奏事、錢穀刑獄等事，望令中書舍人六人，依故事先參詳可否，臣等議而奏聞。

translations.literal: We deliberated: hereafter apart from confidential public business, for all awaiting memorials, hundred officials' reports, money, grain, and criminal matters, we hope the six Secretariat drafters will first deliberate feasibility per precedent; we will discuss and report."
translations.idiomatic: Six drafters were to pre-review all but confidential business.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 李德裕在相位日久，朝臣為其所抑者皆怨之。

translations.literal: Li Deyu had long been in the council phase; court officials he suppressed all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Long in power, Deyu had bred resentment among the suppressed.

sentences.zh: 自崔鉉、杜悰罷相後，中貴人上前言德裕太專，上意不悅，而白敏中之徒，教弘質論之，故有此奏。

translations.literal: After Cui Xuan and Du Cong left the council, inner eunuchs spoke before the throne that Deyu was too exclusive; the Emperor's mind was displeased; Bai Minzhong's faction taught Hongzhi to debate — hence this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and Bai Minzhong's faction used Hongzhi to attack Deyu's monopoly.

sentences.zh: 而德裕結怨之深，由此言也。

translations.literal: Yet Deyu's deep enmity arose from these words.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu's deepest enemies arose from this episode.

sentences.zh: 會昌六年六年春正月癸卯朔。

translations.literal: Huichang 6, first month, guimao new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang 6 opened on guimao.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，左散騎常侍致仕馮定卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: On dingsi Left Regular Attendant retired Feng Ding died; posthumously Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi retired Feng Ding died and was posthumously minister of works.

sentences.zh: 己未，南詔、契丹、室韋、渤海、牂柯、昆明等國遣使入朝，對於麟德殿。

translations.literal: On jiwei Nanzhao, Khitan, Shiwei, Bohai, Zangke, Kunming, and other states sent envoys to court, received at Qilin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei frontier embassies were received at Qilin Hall.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎、判度支盧商奏：「諸道兵討伐党項，今差度支郎官一人往所在有糧料州郡，先計度支給。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War, acting Revenue overseer Lu Shang memorialized: "Armies campaigning against the Tangut — now send one Revenue bureau official to circuits with grain, to calculate and issue supplies in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shang ordered advance grain calculations for the Tangut campaign.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 己丑，渤海王子大之萼入朝。

translations.literal: On jichou the Bohai prince Da Zhie entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou a Bohai prince presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 東都太微宮修成玄元皇帝、玄宗、肅宗三聖容，遣右散騎常侍裴章往東都薦獻。

translations.literal: The eastern capital Taiwei Palace completed images of the Primordial Lord, Xuanzong, and Suzong; Right Regular Attendant Pei Zhang was sent to Luoyang to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhang was sent to dedicate Luoyang's new sage images.

sentences.zh: 監察元壽奏前彭州刺史李鈇買本州龍興寺婢為乳母，違法，貶隨州長史。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Yuan Shou memorialized that former Pengzhou prefect Li Fu bought a Longxing Temple slave as wet-nurse — illegal — demoted to Suizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shou banished Li Fu for buying a temple slave as wet-nurse.

sentences.zh: 二月壬申朔。

translations.literal: Second month, renshen new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The second month opened on renshen.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以時雨愆候，詔：「京城天下系囚，除官典犯贓、持仗劫殺、忤逆十惡外，餘罪遞減一等，犯輕罪者並釋放。

translations.literal: On guiyou, because seasonal rain was untimely, edict: "Capital and empire prisoners — except official corruption, armed robbery and murder, and the ten great rebellions — other crimes reduced one grade; light crimes all released.
translations.idiomatic: Untimely rains brought a graded prisoner amnesty.

sentences.zh: 征党項行營兵士，不得濫有殺傷。

translations.literal: Campaigning Tangut soldiers must not wantonly kill and wound."
translations.idiomatic: Tangut troops were forbidden wanton killing."

sentences.zh: 」丁丑，左拾遺王龜以父興元節度使起年高，乞休官侍養，從之。

translations.literal: On dingchou Left Reminder Wang Gui begged leave to nurse his father, former Xingyuan military commissioner Qi, advanced in years — assented.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui left office to nurse his aged father Wang Qi.

sentences.zh: 是夜，月犯畢大星，相去三寸。

translations.literal: That night the moon transgressed the great star of the Net, three cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: That night the moon neared the Net's great star.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以夏州節度使米暨充東北道招討党項使。

translations.literal: On gengchen Xia military commissioner Mi Ji was made northeast campaign commissioner against the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Mi Ji took the northeast Tangut command.

sentences.zh: 壬午，右庶子呂讓進狀：「亡兄溫女，大和七年嫁左衛兵曹蕭敏，生二男。

translations.literal: On renwu Right Heir-apparent Son Lü Rang memorialized: "My late elder brother Wen's daughter in Dahe 7 married Left Guard army-cao Xiao Min and bore two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Rang asked to reunite his niece with her divorced husband.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，敏心疾乖忤，因而離婚。

translations.literal: In Kaicheng 3 Min's heart illness caused estrangement and they divorced.
translations.idiomatic: They had divorced in Kaicheng 3 when Min fell ill.

sentences.zh: 今敏日愈，卻乞與臣侄女配合。

translations.literal: Now Min improves daily and again begs to marry my brother's niece."
translations.idiomatic: Min had recovered and sought remarriage."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，前太子少保劉沔可太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: Former Heir-apparent Junior Protector Liu Mian was made Heir-apparent Grand Protector retired.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian retired as grand protector of the heir.

sentences.zh: 前壽州刺史王鎮貶潞州長史。

translations.literal: Former Shou prefect Wang Zhen was demoted to Lu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen was banished to Lu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁亥夜，月色少光，至一更一點，犯熒惑，相去四寸。

translations.literal: On dinghai night the moon's color was slightly dim; at the first watch it transgressed Mars, four cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai night the moon dimmed and neared Mars.

sentences.zh: 後良久，其光燭地，在軫七度。

translations.literal: After long while its light lit the ground at seven degrees of the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Its light later lit the ground in the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以翰林學士、起居郎孫穀為兵部員外郎充職。

translations.literal: On renchen Hanlin academician, Diarist Sun Gu was made Vice Minister of War on duty.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Sun Gu took war duties at the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 以旱，停上巳曲江賜宴。

translations.literal: Because of drought, the third-day Qujiang banquet grant was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Drought canceled the Shangsi Qujiang feast.

sentences.zh: 敕：「比緣錢重幣輕，生人轉困，今新加鼓鑄，必在流行，通變救時，莫切於此。

translations.literal: Edict: "Recently because money was heavy and coin light, the living grew poorer; now newly added casting must circulate — to transform and save the season nothing is more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered new coin to circulate and old coin phased out.

sentences.zh: 宜申先甲之令，以儆居貨之徒。

translations.literal: The prior jia order should be proclaimed to warn hoarders."
translations.idiomatic: Hoarders were warned under prior orders."

sentences.zh: 京城諸道，宜起來年正月已後，公私行用，並取新錢。

translations.literal: Capital and circuits from first month next year, public and private use should all take new coin; old coin is provisionally stopped three years.
translations.idiomatic: New coin was mandatory from next year's first month.

sentences.zh: 其舊錢權停三數年。

translations.literal: If there is violation, handle like the lead-tin coin precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Violators faced the lead-tin coin penalties.

sentences.zh: 如有違犯，同用鉛錫錢例科斷。

translations.literal: Old coin is all confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Old coin was to be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 其舊錢並沒納。

translations.literal: Closing quote." Again edict: "Circuit coin casting already has sequence; old coin must circulate so silk prices rise slightly.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict required old coin circulation to raise silk prices.

sentences.zh: 」又敕：「諸道鑄錢，已有次第，須令舊錢流布，絹價值稍增。

translations.literal: Civil and military hundred officials' salaries from third month first day — half paid in cash on hand.
translations.idiomatic: From the third month half of salaries would be paid in cash.
