sentences.zh: 文武百僚俸料，起三月一日，並給見錢一半。

translations.literal: First given bolts, valued at current price — all given cash on hand.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth portions were converted to cash at market price.

sentences.zh: 先給疋段，對估時價，皆給見錢。

translations.literal: First given bolts, valued at current price — all given cash on hand.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth portions were converted to cash at market price.

sentences.zh: 」貶舒州刺史蘇滌為連州刺史。

translations.literal: Closing quote." Su Mian, Shuzhou prefect, was demoted to Lianzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict. Su Mian was banished from Shuzhou to Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 滌李宗閔黨，前自給事中為德裕所斥，累年郡守，至是李紳言其無政故也。

translations.literal: Mian was a Li Zongmin partisan; formerly from supervising secretary he was expelled by Deyu; for years a prefect — now Li Shen said he governed without ability.
translations.idiomatic: Su Mian, a Li Zongmin man Deyu had exiled, fell when Li Shen cited misrule.

sentences.zh: 以邠甯節度使高承恭充西南面招討党項使。

translations.literal: Bing-Ning military commissioner Gao Chenggong was made southwest campaign commissioner against the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chenggong took the southwest Tangut command.

sentences.zh: 丙申夜，月掩牛南星，又犯歲星。

translations.literal: On bingchen night the moon covered the south star of the Ox; it also transgressed Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the moon veiled the Ox and Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，新羅使金國連入朝。

translations.literal: On dingyou the Silla envoy Jin Guolian entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou a Silla envoy presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 辛丑夜，東北流星如桃，色赤，其光燭地，尾跡入大角，西流穿紫微垣。

translations.literal: On xinchou night a northeast meteor like a peach, red in color, its light lit the ground, tail trace entering the Great Horn, streaming west through the Purple Forbidden enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou a red meteor blazed west through the Purple Forbidden enclosure.

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅，上不豫，制改御名炎。

translations.literal: Third month, renyin: the Emperor was ill; an edict changed the imperial name to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wuzong fell ill and took the name Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝重方士，頗服食修攝，親受法籙。

translations.literal: The Emperor valued wonder-workers, often took elixirs and cultivation, personally received registers and talismans.
translations.idiomatic: He had dabbled in alchemy and Daoist registers.

sentences.zh: 至是藥躁，喜怒失常，疾既篤，旬日不能言。

translations.literal: By now elixir frenzy — joy and anger abnormal — when illness was deep, ten days he could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Elixir fever left him mute in his final ten days.

sentences.zh: 宰相李德裕等請見，不許。

translations.literal: Chief ministers Li Deyu and others asked audience — not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu and the premiers were refused audience.

sentences.zh: 中外莫知安否，人情危懼。

translations.literal: Inside and outside did not know whether he was safe; popular feeling was fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not know whether he lived; fear spread.

sentences.zh: 是月二十三日，宣遺詔，以皇太叔光王柩前即位。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day of that month the testamentary edict was proclaimed: the imperial grand-uncle Prince of Guang ascended before the bier.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third Prince Guang ascended before the bier by testament.

sentences.zh: 是日崩，時年三十三。

translations.literal: That day he died, age thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong died that day at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 諡曰至道昭肅孝皇帝，廟號武宗，其年八月，葬於端陵，德妃王氏祔焉。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhaosu Xiaohuangdi, temple name Wuzong; eighth month that year buried at Duanling; Virtuous Consort Wang was attached in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Duanling as Wuzong; Consort Wang joined him in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：開成中，王室寖卑，政由閽寺。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: In Kaicheng the royal house daily sank; government lay with gate eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] In Kaicheng the throne waned and eunuchs ruled.

sentences.zh: 及綴衣將變，儲位遽移。

translations.literal: When the heir's robe was about to change, the heir's seat shifted in haste.
translations.idiomatic: When succession loomed, the heir was swapped overnight.

sentences.zh: 昭肅以孤立維城，副茲當璧。

translations.literal: Zhaosu, solitary, buttressed the wall, fitted to receive the jade disk.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong, though isolated, was fitted to receive the mandate.

sentences.zh: 而能雄謀勇斷，振已去之威權；

translations.literal: Yet he could with fierce plan and brave cut restore departed authority;
translations.idiomatic: He restored imperial authority by fierce resolve.

sentences.zh: 運策勵精，拔非常之俊傑。

translations.literal: deploy policy and rouse essence, pull up extraordinary heroes.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted extraordinary men to office.

sentences.zh: 屬天驕失國，潞孽阻兵，不惑盈庭之言，獨納大臣之計。

translations.literal: When Heaven's pride lost its state and Lu's villain blocked armies, he was not deluded by full-court words but alone took great ministers' plans.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored court chatter and trusted his great ministers against Lu.

sentences.zh: 戎車既駕，亂略底寧，紀律再張，聲名復振，足以蹈章武出師之跡，繼元和戡亂之功。

translations.literal: Once war chariots were yoked, rebellion's outline was pacified, discipline was raised again, fame resounded anew — enough to tread Zhangwu's campaign traces and continue Yuanhe's quelling of chaos.
translations.idiomatic: His campaigns pacified Lu and revived Yuanhe-era discipline.

sentences.zh: 然後迂訪道之車，築禮神之館，棲心玄牝，物色幽人，將致俗於大庭，欲希蹤于姑射。

translations.literal: Then he turned to visit the Way's carriage and built halls for ritual spirits, lodged heart in the dark female, sought recluses in the hidden — wishing to bring custom to the Great Court, hoping to trace Gugu in footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: Then he turned to Daoist rites and immortals, chasing the age of Gugu.

sentences.zh: 於是削浮圖之法，懲游隋之民，志欲矯步丹梯，求珠赤水。

translations.literal: Thus he cut the floating-graph law and punished idle roaming people, will wishing to straighten steps on the cinnabar ladder, seek pearls at Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Buddhism and idlers, seeking immortality's ladder.

sentences.zh: 徒見蕭衍、姚興之謬學，不悟秦王、漢武之非求，蓋惑于左道之言，偏斥異方之說。

translations.literal: He only saw Xiao Yan and Yao Xing's mistaken learning, did not realize First Emperor of Qin and Han Wudi's wrong seeking — deluded by left-path words, biased against alien teachings.
translations.idiomatic: He imitated Qin and Han folly and spurned all foreign teaching.

sentences.zh: 況身毒西來之教，向欲千祀，蚩蚩之民，習以成俗，畏其教甚于國法，樂其徒不異登仙。

translations.literal: Moreover the teaching from Gandhara in the west had wished a thousand sacrifices; the simple people, habit become custom, feared its teaching more than state law, delighted in its followers no less than ascending immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism had rooted deeper than law for common folk.

sentences.zh: 如文身祝髮之鄉，久習而莫知其醜；

translations.literal: Like lands of tattooed bodies and tonsured hair — long practiced and unaware of ugliness;
translations.idiomatic: Like tattooed lands, habit hid its harm;

sentences.zh: 以吐火吞刀之戲，乍觀而便以為神。

translations.literal: seeing fire-breathing and knife-swallowing plays, at first glance they took them for spirits.
translations.idiomatic: fire-swallowing shows passed for miracles.

sentences.zh: 安可正以《咸》《韶》，律之以章甫。

translations.literal: How could one correct them with Xian and Shao, regulate them with cap and gown?
translations.idiomatic: Confucian ritual could not regulate what habit sanctified.

sentences.zh: 加以笮融、何充之佞，代不乏人，非荀卿、孟子之賢，誰興正論。

translations.literal: Moreover flatterers like Qirong and He Chong — every age has them; without sages like Xunzi and Mencius, who would raise upright debate?
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers abounded; only sages could have argued back.

sentences.zh: 一朝隳殘金狄，燔棄胡書，結怨於膜拜之流，犯怒於鄙夫之口。

translations.literal: In one morning he smashed golden Buddhas and burned barbarian books, knotting hatred in prostration's stream, provoking wrath in vulgar mouths.
translations.idiomatic: His smash of temples won hatred from monks and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 哲王之舉，不駭物情，前代存而勿論，實為中道。

translations.literal: A wise king's act should not startle popular feeling; former ages kept it and did not discuss — truly the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: A wise king would not have shocked the people so.

sentences.zh: 欲革斯弊，以俟河清，昭肅明照，聽斯弊矣。

translations.literal: Wishing to reform this decay, one must await the river clearing — Zhaosu bright in illumination, heard this decay.
translations.idiomatic: Reform of such decay awaited a clearer age; Wuzong heard too late.

sentences.zh: 宣宗聖武獻文孝皇帝諱忱，憲宗第十三子，母曰孝明皇后鄭氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, Sagely Martial and Literary Filial, taboo Chen, was Xianzong's thirteenth son; his mother was Empress Xiaoming Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong—taboo Chen—was Xianzong's thirteenth son, born of Empress Zheng.

sentences.zh: 六月二十二日，生於大明宮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the sixth month he was born in Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in Daming Palace on the twenty-second of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 三月，封光王，名怡。

translations.literal: Third month: enfeoffed Prince of Guang, name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he became Prince of Guang Yi.

sentences.zh: 三月一日，武宗疾篤，遺詔立為皇太叔，權勾當軍國政事。

translations.literal: Third month first day: Wuzong's illness was grave; testamentary edict installed him as imperial grand-uncle, acting military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the third month Wuzong named him regent grand-uncle.

sentences.zh: 翌日，柩前即帝位，改今名，時年三十七。

translations.literal: Next day he took the throne before the bier, changed to the present name, age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ascended as Xuanzong at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 帝外晦而內朗，嚴重寡言，視聸特異。

translations.literal: Outwardly dull yet inwardly bright, solemn and sparing of words, his gaze was especially strange.
translations.idiomatic: He seemed dull but was inwardly keen, grave and watchful.

sentences.zh: 幼時宮中以為不慧。

translations.literal: In childhood the palace thought him ungifted.
translations.idiomatic: The palace once thought him simple.

sentences.zh: 十餘歲時，遇重疾沈綴，忽有光輝燭身，蹶然而興，正身拱揖，如對臣僚。

translations.literal: Past ten sui, meeting grave illness prostrate, suddenly radiance lit his body; he started up, straightened body and bowed as to ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After a grave illness in youth he rose glowing and bowed like an emperor.

sentences.zh: 乳媼以為心疾。

translations.literal: The wet-nurse thought it heart illness.
translations.idiomatic: His nurse called it madness.

sentences.zh: 穆宗視之，扶其背曰：「此吾家英物，非心憊也。

translations.literal: Muzong looked at him, steadied his back: "This is our house's heroic thing — not heart weariness."
translations.idiomatic: Muzong said, "This is no madness but our house's hero."

sentences.zh: 」賜以玉如意、御馬、金帶。

translations.literal: Granted jade ruyi, imperial horse, gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He received jade ruyi, an imperial horse, and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 常夢乘龍升天，言之於鄭后，乃曰：「此不宜人知者，幸勿復言。

translations.literal: He often dreamed of riding a dragon to heaven; telling Empress Zheng, she said: "This is not fit for others to know — pray do not speak again."
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of ascending on a dragon; Empress Zheng bade him silence it.

sentences.zh: 」歷太和、會昌朝，愈事韜晦，群居游處，未嘗有言。

translations.literal: Through Taihe and Huichang reigns he grew more hidden; in groups at play he never spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Through Taihe and Huichang he kept his wit hidden.

sentences.zh: 文宗、武宗幸十六宅宴集，強誘其言，以為戲劇，謂之「光叔」。

translations.literal: Wenzong and Wuzong, visiting the sixteen mansions for feasts, forced him to speak for sport, calling him "Uncle Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong and Wuzong mocked him as "Uncle Guang" at princely feasts.

sentences.zh: 武宗氣豪，尤不為禮。

translations.literal: Wuzong was bold in spirit and especially discourteous.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong especially scorned him.

sentences.zh: 及監國之日，哀毀滿容，接待群僚，決斷庶務，人方見其隱德焉。

translations.literal: When he oversaw the state, grief filled his face; receiving the hundred officials he decided common affairs — men then saw his hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: As regent he mourned openly and ruled decisively; his virtue showed.

sentences.zh: 四月辛未，釋服，尊母鄭氏曰皇太后。

translations.literal: Fourth month, xinwei: mourning released; mother Zheng was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month mourning ended and Zheng became empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎、翰林學士承旨白敏中守本官、同中書門下平章事；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War, Hanlin academician-in-chief Bai Minzhong kept his posts and became Grand Councillor;
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong joined the council from the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 以特進、守太尉、門下侍郎、同平章事、上柱國、衛國公、食邑二千戶李德裕檢校太尉、同平章事、江陵尹、荊南節度使；

translations.literal: Special Advance, Grand Preceptor, Secretariat Vice Director, Grand Councillor, Pillar of State, Duke of Weiguo with two thousand households Li Deyu was made acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Councillor, Jiangling metropolitan governor, Jingnan military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu was sent to Jingnan and stripped of the capital.

sentences.zh: 以中散大夫、大理卿馬植為金紫光祿大夫、刑部侍郎，充諸道鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: Palace Cadet, Minister of Punishments Ma Zhi was made Gold-Purple Grandee, Vice Minister of Punishments, and circuit salt-and-iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi took punishments and the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 以成德軍節度使王元逵檢校太保，山南西道節度使王起檢校司空，魏博節度使何弘敬、淮南節度使李紳並檢校司空，劍南西川節度使崔鄲檢校尚書右僕射，同中書門下平章事並如故。

translations.literal: Chengde military commissioner Wang Yuankui was made acting Grand Protector; Shannan West military commissioner Wang Qi acting Minister of Works; Weibo military commissioner He Hongjing and Huainan military commissioner Li Shen both acting Minister of Works; Jiannan West military commissioner Cui Xun acting Right Vice Director — all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioners received honorary promotions unchanged in post.

sentences.zh: 東都留守李石奏修奉太廟畢，所司迎奉太微宮神主祔廟訖。

translations.literal: Eastern capital regent Li Shi memorialized that repair of the Imperial Ancestral Temple was complete; the responsible office welcomed Taiwei Palace spirit tablets to attach in the temple — finished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi reported Luoyang's ancestral temple restored and tablets installed.

sentences.zh: 東都太廟者，本武后家廟，神龍中中宗反正，廢武氏廟主，立太祖已下神主付之。

translations.literal: The eastern capital temple was originally Empress Wu's family temple; in Shenlong Zhongzong restored the throne, abolished Wu's tablets, established High Ancestor-down tablets and entrusted them there.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's temple had been Wu Zetian's, then held Tang ancestors after Shenlong.

sentences.zh: 安祿山陷洛陽，以廟為馬廄，棄其神主，而協律郎嚴郢收而藏之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan took Luoyang he used the temple as stables, abandoned the tablets; Harmony Master Yan Ying recovered and hid them.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan stabled horses there; Yan Ying rescued the tablets.

sentences.zh: 史思明再陷洛陽，尋又散失。

translations.literal: Shi Siming again took Luoyang and they scattered again.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming's sack scattered them again.

sentences.zh: 賊平，東京留守盧正己又募得之。

translations.literal: After rebels were pacified, eastern capital regent Lu Zhengji again collected them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhengji recovered them after the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 廟已焚毀，乃寄主于太微宮。

translations.literal: The temple was burned; they lodged tablets at Taiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: With the temple burned, tablets lodged at Taiwei Palace.

sentences.zh: ，留守路嗣恭奏重修太廟，以迎神主。

translations.literal: , Regent Lu Sisi memorialized rebuilding the temple to welcome the tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sisi later sought to rebuild the temple.

sentences.zh: 詔百官參議，紛然不定，禮儀使顏真卿堅請歸祔，不從。

translations.literal: Edict for hundred officials to debate — unsettled; Rituals Commissioner Yan Zhenqing firmly asked return to attachment — not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Debate failed; Yan Zhenqing's plea to reunite tablets was ignored.

sentences.zh: ，留守李石因太微宮正殿圮陊，以廢弘敬寺為太廟，迎神主祔之。

translations.literal: , Regent Li Shi because Taiwei's main hall collapsed used abolished Hongjing Temple as the temple and welcomed tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi housed tablets in a converted Hongjing Temple when Taiwei collapsed.

sentences.zh: 又下百僚議，皆言准故事，無兩都俱置之禮，唯禮部侍郎陳商議云：「周之文、武，有鎬、洛二廟，今兩都異廟可也。

translations.literal: Again sent down to hundred officials — all said follow precedent, no ritual for both capitals; only Vice Minister of Rites Chen Shang said: "Zhou's Wen and Wu had Feng and Luo two temples — today two-capital separate temples is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chen Shang argued for two-capital temples like Zhou.

sentences.zh: 然不宜置主於廟，主宜依禮瘞廟之北墉下。

translations.literal: Yet tablets should not be placed in the temple; tablets should follow ritual buried north of the temple wall."
translations.idiomatic: He said tablets should be buried north of the temple, not enthroned."

sentences.zh: 」事未行而武宗崩。

translations.literal: The matter had not proceeded when Wuzong died.
translations.idiomatic: The matter lapsed when Wuzong died.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，因詔有司迎太微宮寓主，祔廢寺之新廟，而知禮者非之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong on assuming the throne ordered officials to welcome Taiwei's lodged tablets to attach in the abolished temple's new temple — ritualists disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong installed the tablets anyway, to ritualists' dismay.

sentences.zh: 制：「皇長男溫可封鄆王，二男涇可封雅王，第三男滋可封蘄王，第四男沂可封慶王。

translations.literal: Edict: "Eldest son Wen may be enfeoffed Prince of Yan; second son Jing Prince of Ya; third son Zi Prince of Qi; fourth son Yi Prince of Qing."
translations.idiomatic: Four sons were enfeoffed princes of Yan, Ya, Qi, and Qing.

translations.literal: Fifth month: left and right street merit commissioners memorialized: "Per the fifth-day amnesty section this month, the upper capital's two wards keep four temples, eight more to be added outside.
translations.idiomatic: Merit commissioners proposed restoring eight capital temples under the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，左右街功德使奏：「准今月五日赦書節文，上都兩街留四寺，外更添置八所。

translations.literal: Two keep original names Xingtang Temple and Baoshou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Xingtang and Baoshou kept their names.

sentences.zh: 兩所依舊名興唐寺、保壽寺。

translations.literal: Six request old-name changes: Baoying to Zisheng, Qinglong to Huguo, Puti to Baotang, Qingchan to Anguo, Fayun Nunnery to Tang'an, Chongjing Nunnery to Tangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Six temples were renamed under the restoration plan.

sentences.zh: 六所請改舊名，寶應寺改為資聖寺，青龍寺改為護國寺，菩提寺改為保唐寺，清禪寺改為安國寺，法雲尼寺改為唐安寺，崇敬尼寺改為唐昌寺。

translations.literal: Right ward adds eight.
translations.idiomatic: The right ward gained eight sites.

sentences.zh: 右街添置八所。

translations.literal: Ximing Temple changed to Fushou Temple, Zhuangyan to Shengshou — former retained temples.
translations.idiomatic: Ximing became Fushou and Zhuangyan Shengshou among retained temples.

sentences.zh: 西明寺改為福壽寺，莊嚴寺改為聖壽寺，舊留寺。

translations.literal: Two old names: Qianfu to Xingyuan, Huadu to Chongfu, Yongtai to Wanshou, Wenguo to Chongsheng, Jingxing to Longxing, Feng'en to Xingfu.
translations.idiomatic: Qianfu, Huadu, and others were renamed as listed.

sentences.zh: 二所舊名，千福寺改為興元寺，化度寺改為崇福寺，永泰寺改為萬壽寺，溫國寺改為崇聖寺，經行寺改為龍興寺，奉恩寺改為興福寺。

translations.literal: Closing quote." Edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the memorial. The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨依奏。

translations.literal: Twelve Daoists including Liu Xuanjing were executed — because their doctrines deluded Wuzong and slandered Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanjing and eleven other Daoists were executed for swaying Wuzong against Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 誅道士劉玄靖等十二人，以其說惑武宗，排毀釋氏故也。

translations.literal: This month's fifth-day amnesty section: Personnel's three selection boards choose candidates only by seniority — many lack real talent; observation commissioners and prefects may recommend men of strange talent and unusual governance for trial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty allowed prefects to recommend talent beyond seniority lists.

sentences.zh: 今月五日赦書節文，吏部三銓選士，祗憑資考，多匪實才，許觀察使、刺史有奇才異政之士，聞薦試用。

translations.literal: Also when observation commissioners and prefects hand over office, if household registers they deliver increase by a thousand households, they receive exceptional promotion;
translations.idiomatic: Prefects who added a thousand households on handover won fast promotion;

sentences.zh: 又觀察使、刺史交代之時，冊書所交戶口如能增添至千戶，即與超遷；

translations.literal: if flight reaches seven hundred households, for three years after leaving they may not take office.
translations.idiomatic: those who lost seven hundred were barred three years.

sentences.zh: 如逃亡至七百戶，罷後三年內不得任使。

translations.literal: Also exiles at Tiande and Zhenwu — measure loan of grain seed in the circuit so they farm as livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier exiles were lent seed to farm.

sentences.zh: 又徒流人在天德、振武者，管中量借糧種，俾令耕田以為業。

translations.literal: Jiannan East military commissioner, acting Minister of Rites Lu Shang was made Vice Minister of War and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shang joined the council from Jiannan East.

sentences.zh: 以劍南東川節度使、檢校禮部尚書盧商為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Vice Minister of Revenue, circuit salt-and-iron commissioner Ma Zhi was made Grand Councillor in his original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi joined the council in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 六月，以戶部侍郎、充諸道鹽鐵轉運使馬植本官同平章事。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Minister of War Li Rangyi was made Jiannan East military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rangyi took Jiannan East in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 七月，以兵部尚書李讓夷為劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: Tenth month, edict: "Grand Temple shared offerings should pair meritorious subjects.
translations.idiomatic: An edict paired meritorious subjects in Xianzong's temple offerings.

sentences.zh: 十月，敕：「太廟祫享，合以功臣配。

translations.literal: At Xianzong's temple, Pei Du, Du Huangchang, Li Su, Gao Chongwen, and others are to share offerings."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du, Du Huangchang, Li Su, and Gao Chongwen were named.

sentences.zh: 其憲宗廟，以裴度、杜黃裳、李愬、高崇文等配享。

translations.literal: Jingnan military commissioner Li Deyu was made eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu became Luoyang regent.

sentences.zh: 」以荊南節度使李德裕為東都留守。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: the responsible office offered at the Grand Temple; Muzong's chamber text said "imperial elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Temple offering Muzong was styled "imperial elder brother."

sentences.zh: 十一月，有司享太廟，其穆宗室文曰「皇兄」。

translations.literal: Grand Temple academician Min Qingzhi memorialized: "Ritual has honoring honor, not sequencing kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Min Qingzhi protested the kinship wording.

sentences.zh: 太常博士閔慶之奏：「夫禮有尊尊，而不敘親親。

translations.literal: Prayer text saying younger brother is improper; please change to 'successor Emperor'."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that "younger brother" become "successor Emperor."

sentences.zh: 祝文稱弟未當，請改為'嗣皇帝'。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Jingzhao prefecture memorialized: "Capital hundred offices' salary fields' grain measure — please follow Huichang 3 precedent, allow people forever to deliver to the capital themselves; nearby prefectures may not conceal."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao asked salary-field grain delivered freely to the capital per Huichang 3.

sentences.zh: 京兆府奏：「京師百司職田斛鬥，請准會昌三年例，許人永自送納京師，親冀州縣無得欺隱。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi observation commissioner Zhou Chi was made Yicheng military commissioner and Zheng-Hua observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi took Yicheng and Zheng-Hua.

sentences.zh: 以江西觀察使周墀為義成軍節度使、鄭滑觀察等使。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Minister of Punishments, acting Revenue overseer Cui Yuanshi memorialized: "Per the seventh month second-day edict, inferior silk bolts are all forbidden like copper — may not be woven.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanshi moved to ban inferior silk weaving.

sentences.zh: 十二月，刑部尚書、判度支崔元式奏：「准七月二日敕，綾紗絹等次弱疋段，並同禁斷，不得織造。

translations.literal: I wish to join Salt, Revenue, and Personnel in one memorial, first survey the left treasury, list inferior-bolt circuits, then order search and destroy narrow looms.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed joint surveys and destruction of narrow looms.

sentences.zh: 臣欲與鹽鐵戶部三司同條疏，先勘左藏庫，令分析出次弱疋段州府，即牒本道官搜索狹小機杼，令焚毀。

translations.literal: Already delivered inferior bolts — report the count."
translations.idiomatic: Delivered inferior bolts were to be reported."

sentences.zh: 其已納到次弱疋段，具數以聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong assented.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: Dazhong 1, first month, wuxu new moon: the palace parks commissioner memorialized: "When the Emperor fasts for the suburban rite, inner palace garden gates total ninety-four — all to be locked; keys forwarded inside.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu of Dazhong 1 palace gates were locked for the suburban fast.

sentences.zh: 大中元年春正月戊戌朔，宮苑使奏：「皇帝致齋行事，內諸宮苑門共九十四所，並令鎖閉，鑰匙進內。

translations.literal: When the carriage returns, please receive them."
translations.idiomatic: Keys would return when the emperor came back from the rite.

sentences.zh: 候車駕還宮，則請領。

translations.literal: Thus ended the edict; the throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: On wushen the Emperor performed suburban rites; when ritual ended he took Vermilion Phoenix Gate and proclaimed great amnesty, changed the reign title; the edict said:
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Dazhong began with suburban rites and amnesty at Vermilion Phoenix Gate.

sentences.zh: 戊申，皇帝有事于郊廟，禮畢，御丹鳳門，大赦，改元，制條曰：「古者郎官出宰，卿相治郡，所以重親人之官，急為政之本。

translations.literal: "In antiquity palace officials went out to govern prefectures, chief ministers administered commanderies — thus to weight kinship's office and hurry the root of government.
translations.idiomatic: "Ancient officers governed in the provinces," the edict began.

sentences.zh: 自澆風久扇，此道稍消，頡頏清途，便臻顯貴。

translations.literal: Since shallow custom long blew, this path slightly vanished; wrangling the clear path, one reached eminent rank.
translations.idiomatic: "Courtiers now reach rank without governing."

sentences.zh: 治人之術，未嘗經心，欲使究百姓艱危，通天下利病，不可得也。

translations.literal: The art of governing people was never mastered — wishing to exhaust the people's hardship and communicate empire-wide benefit and harm is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: "They never learn the people's hardship."

sentences.zh: 為政之始，思厚儒風，軒墀近臣，蓋備顧問，如其不知人疾苦，何以膺朕眷求？

translations.literal: At government's start, think to thicken Confucian wind; terrace nearness ministers should be prepared advisers — if they do not know people's toil, how bear Our search?
translations.idiomatic: "Near ministers must know popular toil."

sentences.zh: 今後諫議大夫、給事中、中書舍人曾任刺史、縣令，或在任有贓累者，宰臣不得擬議。

translations.literal: Hereafter remonstrance grandees, supervising secretaries, and Secretariat drafters who once were prefects or county magistrates, or while in office had corruption stains — chief ministers may not nominate them.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt former prefects were barred from high nomination.

sentences.zh: 守宰親人，職當撫字，三載考績，著在格言。

translations.literal: Magistrates' kin — office should comfort and inscribe; three years' examination performance is in the maxim.
translations.idiomatic: "Magistrates must serve full terms," the edict continued.

sentences.zh: 貞元年中，屢下明詔，縣令五考，方得改移。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan the bright edict was repeatedly sent: a magistrate must pass five examinations before transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan had required five reviews before transfer.

sentences.zh: 近者因循，都不遵守，諸州或得三考，畿府罕及二年，以此字人，若為成政？

translations.literal: Recently through inertia none obeyed; some circuits got three reviews, capital counties rarely reached two years — with such men governing, how make successful policy?
translations.idiomatic: "Prefects now move too soon to govern well."

sentences.zh: 道塗郡吏有迎送之勞，鄉里庶民無蘇息之望。

translations.literal: Road clerks and circuit officials have escort toil; village people have no rest hope.
translations.idiomatic: "People get no rest from revolving magistrates."

sentences.zh: 自今須滿三十六個月，永為常式。

translations.literal: From now must complete thirty-six months — forever the constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: "Thirty-six months shall be the fixed term."

translations.literal: Closing quote of edict."
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the amnesty edict."

sentences.zh: 二月丁卯，制：「憲宗第十七子惕封彭王，第十八子惴為棣王；

translations.literal: Second month, dingmao, edict: "Xianzong's seventeenth son Ti enfeoffed Prince of Peng; eighteenth son Zhui Prince of Di;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Xianzong's sons Ti and Zhui were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 皇第五子澤為濮王，第六子潤為鄂王。

translations.literal: fifth son Ze Prince of Pu; sixth son Run Prince of E.
translations.idiomatic: Ze and Run became princes of Pu and E.

sentences.zh: 」敕修百福殿。

translations.literal: Closing quote." Edict to repair Baifu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Baifu Hall was ordered repaired.

sentences.zh: 以檢校太尉、東都留守李德裕為太子少保，分司東都；

translations.literal: Acting Grand Preceptor, eastern capital regent Li Deyu was made Heir-apparent Junior Protector, eastern capital branch office;
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu was sidelined to junior protector at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以給事中鄭亞為桂州刺史、御史中丞、桂管防禦觀察等使。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zheng Ya was made Guizhou prefect, Censor-in-Chief, Guiguan defense and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ya was sent to Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 二月丁酉，禮部侍郎魏扶奏：「臣今年所放進士三十三人，其封彥卿、崔琢、鄭延休等三人，實有詞藝，為時所稱，皆以父兄見居重位，不令中選。

translations.literal: Second month, dingyou: Vice Minister of Rites Wei Fu memorialized: "This year's thirty-three passed jinshi include Feng Yanqing, Cui Zhuo, and Zheng Yanxiu — all have literary craft and are praised in the time, yet because fathers and brothers hold heavy posts they were not allowed to pass."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fu withheld three gifted candidates whose kin held high office.

sentences.zh: 」詔令翰林學士承旨、戶部侍郎韋琮重考覆，敕曰：「彥卿等所試文字，並合度程，可放及第。

translations.literal: Edict ordered Hanlin academician-in-chief, Vice Minister of Revenue Wei Cong to re-examine; edict: "Yanqing and others' trial texts all meet standard — may pass and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cong's re-exam restored Feng Yanqing and the other two.

sentences.zh: 有司考試，祗在至公，如涉請托，自有朝典。

translations.literal: Responsible examination rests in utmost fairness; if patronage is involved, there is the court code.
translations.idiomatic: "Patronage has its own penalties," the edict said.

sentences.zh: 今後但依常例放榜，不別有奏聞。

translations.literal: Hereafter release lists by usual rule — no separate memorial."
translations.idiomatic: "Release lists by usual rule without special pleas."

sentences.zh: 」帝雅好儒士，留心貢舉。

translations.literal: The Emperor elegantly loved Confucian scholars and attended to the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong favored scholars and watched the examinations closely.

sentences.zh: 有時微行人間，采聽輿論，以觀選士之得失。

translations.literal: Sometimes he secretly walked among the people, gathering popular debate to observe selection's gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes walked incognito to hear opinion on the exams.

sentences.zh: 每山池曲宴，學士詩什屬和，公卿出鎮，亦賦詩餞行。

translations.literal: Whenever mountain-pool curved feasts, academician poems responded in turn; when dukes and ministers went out to command, he also composed poems to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: He joined poets at feast and sent off ministers with verse.

sentences.zh: 凡對臣僚，肅然拱揖，鮮有輕易之言。

translations.literal: Facing ministers he was solemn in bow; rarely light words.
translations.idiomatic: He faced ministers with solemn bows and few light words.

sentences.zh: 大臣或獻章疏，即燒香盥手而覽之。

translations.literal: When great ministers presented memorials he burned incense and washed hands before reading.
translations.idiomatic: He read memorials with incense and washed hands.

sentences.zh: 當時以大中之政有貞觀之風焉。

translations.literal: At the time Dazhong's government was said to have Zhenguan's wind.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries likened Dazhong government to Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 又敕：「自今進士放榜後，杏園任依舊宴集，有司不得禁制。

translations.literal: Again edict: "From now when jinshi lists are posted, Apricot Garden may feast as of old; responsible offices may not forbid."
translations.idiomatic: Apricot Garden feasts after the list were restored.

sentences.zh: 」武宗好巡遊，故曲江亭禁人宴聚故也。

translations.literal: Closing quote." Wuzong loved tours — hence Qujiang Pavilion had forbidden people's feasts.
translations.idiomatic: The ban had begun under tour-loving Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，敕：「會昌季年，並省寺宇。

translations.literal: Intercalary third month, edict: "In Huichang's last years temples were merged and cut.
translations.idiomatic: An intercalary-third-month edict began restoring temples.

sentences.zh: 雖雲異方之教，無損致理之源。

translations.literal: Though called alien teaching, it did not harm governance's source;
translations.idiomatic: "Alien teaching did not harm the state's root,"

sentences.zh: 中國之人，久行其道，厘革過當，事體未弘。

translations.literal: Huaxia people long practiced its path — the reform was excessive, the matter not yet broad.
translations.idiomatic: "but the cut was excessive and the policy too narrow."

sentences.zh: 其靈山勝境、天下州府，應會昌五年四月所廢寺宇，有宿舊名僧，復能修創，一任住持，所司不得禁止。

translations.literal: Spirit mountains and famous sites, empire-wide prefectures — Huichang 5 fourth-month abolished temples with old-name monks who can again repair — let them reside, offices may not forbid.
translations.idiomatic: Famed temples with restoring monks were reopened.

translations.literal: Closing quote of edict."
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the temple edict."

sentences.zh: 四月，積慶太后蕭氏崩，諡曰貞獻，文宗母也。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Accumulated Celebration Empress Dowager Xiao died; posthumous title Zhenxian — Wenzong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's mother, Empress Dowager Xiao, died as Zhenxian.

sentences.zh: 六月，以義成軍節度使周墀為兵部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Yicheng military commissioner Zhou Chi was made Vice Minister of War, acting Revenue overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi took Revenue in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 冊黠戛斯王子為為英武誠明可汗，命鴻臚卿李業入蕃冊拜。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed the Qarluq prince as Yingwu Chenming Qaghan; ordered Court of Imperial Entertainments Minister Li Ye into the steppe to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: A Qarluq prince was invested qaghan by Li Ye.

sentences.zh: 以金紫光祿大夫、守太子少保分司東都、上柱國、奇章郡開國公、食邑二千戶牛僧孺守太子太師，銀青光祿大夫、行太子賓客、上柱國、隴西郡開國公、食邑二千戶李彥佐為太子太保。

translations.literal: Gold-Purple Grandee, Heir-apparent Junior Protector retired eastern capital branch, Pillar of State, Duke of Qizhang with two thousand households Niu Sengru was made Heir-apparent Grand Preceptor; Silver-Green Grandee, acting Heir-apparent Guest of Honor, Pillar of State, Duke of Longxi with two thousand households Li Yanyou was made Heir-apparent Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru and Li Yanyou were honored at Luoyang as grand preceptor and protector.

sentences.zh: 並依前分司。

translations.literal: Both as before in branch office.
translations.idiomatic: Both remained in eastern-branch posts.

sentences.zh: 以左諫議大夫庾簡休為虢州刺史，以正議大夫、行尚書考功郎中、知制誥、上柱國崔璵為中書舍人，以中散大夫、前湖州刺史、彭陽縣開國男、食邑三百戶令狐綯行尚書考功郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Grandee Yu Jianxiu was made Guo prefect; Regular Grandee, acting Ministry of Personnel merit director, edict drafter, Pillar of State Cui Yun was made Secretariat drafter; Palace Cadet, former Huzhou prefect, Baron of Pengyang with three hundred households Linghu Tao was made acting Personnel merit director and edict drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jianxiu, Cui Yun, and Linghu Tao received capital posts.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，制以正議大夫、尚書戶部侍郎、知制誥、翰林學士承旨、柱國、賜紫金魚袋韋琮以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month: Regular Grandee, Vice Minister of Revenue, edict drafter, Hanlin academician-in-chief, Pillar of State, granted purple-gold fish Wei Cong was made Grand Councillor in his present posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cong joined the council in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 以太子少保分司東都、衛國公李德裕為人所訟，貶潮州司馬員外置同正員。

translations.literal: Heir-apparent Junior Protector retired eastern capital branch Duke of Weiguo Li Deyu was sued by others, demoted to Chaozhou acting staff member same-rank regular.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu was banished to Chaozhou after lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 八月，工部尚書、中書侍郎、平章事盧商出為鄂嶽觀察使，。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Minister of Works, Secretariat Vice Director, Grand Councillor Lu Shang went out as E-Yue observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shang left the council for E-Yue in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 神策軍奏修百福殿成，名其殿曰雍和殿，樓曰親親樓，凡廊舍屋宇七百間，以會諸王子孫。

translations.literal: The Divine Strategy army reported repair of Baifu Hall complete — named the hall Yonghe, tower Qinqin, seven hundred corridor rooms in all, to assemble princes' sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Strategy army finished Yonghe Hall for princely kin.

sentences.zh: 九月，前永甯縣尉吳汝納詣闕稱冤，言：「弟湘任揚州江都縣尉，被節度使李紳誣奏湘贓罪，宰相李德裕曲情祔紳，斷臣弟湘致死。

translations.literal: Ninth month: former Yongning county sheriff Wu Runa came to the gate claiming injustice, saying: "My younger brother Xiang was Yangzhou Jiangdu county sheriff; military commissioner Li Shen falsely memorialized Xiang's corruption; chief minister Li Deyu bent favor to Shen and judged my brother Xiang to death."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Runa accused Li Shen and Li Deyu of murdering his brother Wu Xiang.

sentences.zh: 」詔下御史臺鞫按。

translations.literal: Closing quote." Edict sent down to the Censorate to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended his plea. The Censorate was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 大中二年二年春正月壬戌，宰臣率文武百僚上徽號曰聖敬文思和武光孝皇帝，御宣政殿受冊訖，宣德音。

translations.literal: Dazhong 2, first month, renxu: chief ministers led civil and military hundred officials offering honorific Sagely Reverent Literary Reflective Harmonious Martial Bright Filial Emperor; received the seal at Xuanzheng Hall, proclaimed virtuous sound.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu of Dazhong 2 the court offered a new honorific at Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 神策軍修左銀臺門樓、屋宇及南面城牆，至睿武樓。

translations.literal: The Divine Strategy army repaired the left Silver Terrace gate tower, rooms, and southern wall to Ruiwu Tower.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Strategy army repaired the Silver Terrace gate to Ruiwu Tower.

sentences.zh: 二月，制劍南西川節度、光祿大夫、檢校吏部尚書、同平章事、成都尹、上柱國、隴西郡開國公、食邑二千戶李回責授湖南觀察使，桂州刺史、御史中丞、桂管防禦觀察使鄭亞貶循州刺史，前淮南觀察判官魏鉶貶吉州司戶，陸渾縣令元壽貶韶州司戶，殿中侍御史蔡京貶澧州司馬。

translations.literal: Second month, edict: Jiannan West military commissioner, Glory Grandee, acting Minister of Personnel, Grand Councillor, Chengdu metropolitan governor, Pillar of State, Duke of Longxi with two thousand households Li Hui was demoted to Hunan observation commissioner; Guizhou prefect, Censor-in-Chief, Guiguan commissioner Zheng Ya demoted to Xun prefect; former Huainan observation judge Wei Chang demoted to Ji prefect staff; Lu Hun county magistrate Yuan Shou demoted to Shao prefect staff; Palace Censor Cai Jing demoted to Li acting staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui, Zheng Ya, and allies in the Wu Xiang case were demoted in the second month.

sentences.zh: 御史台奏：

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate reported on the Wu Xiang case:

sentences.zh: 據三司推勘吳湘獄，謹具逐人罪狀如後：揚州都虞候盧行立、劉群，於一月十四日，于阿顏家吃酒，與阿顏母阿焦同坐，群自擬收阿顏為妻，妄稱監軍使處分，要阿顏進奉，不得嫁人，兼擅令人監守。

translations.literal: According to the three offices' investigation of Wu Xiang's case, we respectfully list each man's crimes: Yangzhou chief commandant Lu Xingli and Liu Qun on the fourteenth of the first month drank at A Yan's house with A Jiao; Qun himself wished to take A Yan as wife, falsely claiming the army supervisor's order that A Yan be presented and not marry, also arbitrarily set guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate detailed Lu Xingli and Liu Qun's seizure of a courtesan.

sentences.zh: 其阿焦遂與江都縣尉吳湘密約，嫁阿顏與湘。

translations.literal: A Jiao then secretly agreed with Jiangdu sheriff Wu Xiang to marry A Yan to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiao arranged her marriage to Wu Xiang.

sentences.zh: 劉群與押軍牙官李克勳即時遮欄不得，乃令江都百姓論湘取受，節度使李紳追湘下獄，計贓處死。

translations.literal: Liu Qun and escort military officer Li Kexion immediately blocked it; then ordered Jiangdu commoners to accuse Xiang of bribes; military commissioner Li Shen pursued Xiang to prison, calculated corruption, executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qun blocked the marriage and Li Shen executed Xiang for bribery.

sentences.zh: 具獄奏聞。

translations.literal: Full case memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The full case had been reported.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑其冤，差御史崔元藻往揚州按問，據湘雖有取受，罪不至死。

translations.literal: The court doubted injustice and sent Censor Cui Yuanyao to Yangzhou to inquire; according to Xiang though there was taking, crime did not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanyao found the crime did not warrant death.

sentences.zh: 李德裕党附李紳，乃貶元藻嶺南，取淮南元申文案，斷湘處死。

translations.literal: Li Deyu clique-attached to Li Shen, then demoted Yuanyao to Lingnan, took Huainan original judge Wei Chang's documents, judged Xiang to death.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu exiled Yuanyao and used Wei Chang's papers to kill Xiang.

sentences.zh: 今據三司使追崔元藻及淮南元推判官魏鉶並關連人款狀，淮南都虞候劉群、元推判官魏鉶、典孫貞高利錢倚黃嵩、江都縣典沈頒陳宰、節度押牙白沙鎮遏使傅義、左都虞候盧行立、天長縣令張弘思、曲張洙清陳回、右廂子巡李行璠、典臣金弘舉、送吳湘妻女至澧州取受錢物人潘宰、前揚府錄事參軍李公佐、元推官元壽吳珙翁恭、太子少保分司李德裕、西川節度使李回、桂管觀察使鄭亞等，伏候敕旨。

translations.literal: Now according to the three commissioners' pursuit of Cui Yuanyao and Huainan original judges Wei Chang and connected persons' confessions — Huainan chief commandant Liu Qun, original judge Wei Chang, clerk Sun Zhen lending at high interest relying on Huang Song, Jiangdu clerks Shen Yan and Chen Zai, military escort Fu Yi, left commandant Lu Xingli, Tianchang magistrate Zhang Hongsi, Qu Zhangzhu and Chen Hui, right wing patrol Li Xingfan, clerk Jin Hongju, men who delivered Wu Xiang's wife and daughter to Li prefecture for bribes Pan Zai, former Yang prefecture recorder Li Gongzuo, original judges Yuan Shou, Wu Gong, Weng Gong, retired eastern-branch Junior Protector Li Deyu, Jiannan West commissioner Li Hui, Guiguan commissioner Zheng Ya, and others — await imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: A long list of officials in the Xiang case awaited judgment.

sentences.zh: 其月，敕：

translations.literal: That month, edict:
translations.idiomatic: That month the throne ruled:

sentences.zh: 三月己酉，兵部侍郎、判度支周墀本官平章事。

translations.literal: Third month, jiyou: Vice Minister of War, acting Revenue overseer Zhou Chi was made Grand Councillor in original posts.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Zhou Chi joined the council.

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書、鹽鐵轉運使馬植本官同平章事。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites, salt-and-transport commissioner Ma Zhi was made Grand Councillor in original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi also joined the council.

sentences.zh: 日本國王子入朝貢方物。

translations.literal: The Japanese prince entered court presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: A Japanese prince presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 王子善棋，帝令侍詔顧師言與之對手。

translations.literal: The prince was skilled at chess; the Emperor ordered Attendant-Assembled Gu Shiyan to play him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shiyan was ordered to play the prince at chess.

sentences.zh: 五月己未，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jiwei: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei of the fifth month the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 六月己丑，太皇太后郭氏崩，諡懿安，憲宗妃，穆宗之母也。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jichou: Grand Empress Dowager Guo died; posthumous title Yi'an — Xianzong's consort, Muzong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Grand Empress Dowager Guo died as Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎，兼御史大夫、判度支崔龜從奏：「應諸司場院官請卻官本錢後，或有欺隱欠負，征理須足，不得苟從恩蕩，以求放免。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, acting Revenue overseer Cui Guicong memorialized: "All circuit field-office officials — after returning office capital, if there is concealment and arrears, collection must be full, may not seek release through favor —
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guicong tightened collection of field-office arrears.

sentences.zh: 今後凡隱盜欠負，請如官典犯贓例處分。

translations.literal: hereafter any concealed theft and arrears — please handle like official corruption precedent.
translations.idiomatic: "Hidden arrears shall be punished like corruption," he said.

sentences.zh: 縱逢恩赦，不在免限。

translations.literal: Even if favor amnesty comes, not within exemption limit.
translations.idiomatic: "Even amnesties shall not wipe such debts."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Closing quote." Assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the memorial. The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 七月戊午，以前山南西道節度使高元裕為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Seventh month, wuwu: former Shannan West military commissioner Gao Yuanyu was made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Gao Yuanyu took Personnel.

sentences.zh: 八月戊子，朝散大夫、中書舍人、充翰林學士、上柱國、平陰縣開國男、食實封三百戶賜紫金魚袋畢諴為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuzi: Palace Companion, Secretariat Drafter, Hanlin academician, Pillar of State, Baron of Pingyin with three hundred household fief and purple-gold fish Bi Kan was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Bi Kan became Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 九月，敕：「比有無良之人，於街市投匿名文書，及于箭上或旗幡上縱為奸言，以亂國法。

translations.literal: Ninth month, an edict: "Of late wicked men have cast anonymous documents in the markets, or on arrows or banners spread slander to disturb state law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banned anonymous slander in markets, on arrows, and on banners.

sentences.zh: 此後所由切加捉搦，如獲此色，便仰焚瘞，不得上聞。

translations.literal: Henceforth authorities must seize such cases strictly; when obtained, burn and bury them at once — do not report upward."
translations.idiomatic: Seized materials were to be burned without report to the throne.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 十一月，兵部侍郎、判戶部事魏扶奏：「天下州府錢物、斛斗、文簿，並委錄事參軍專判，仍與長史通判，至交代時具數申奏。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Vice Minister of War and acting revenue commissioner Wei Fu memorialized: "Money, grain, and registers of all prefectures should be entrusted to the registrar for sole judgment, still jointly checked with the chief administrator; at handover list numbers and memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fu ordered prefectural registers to be kept by registrars with joint review at handover.

sentences.zh: 如無懸欠，量與減選注擬。

translations.literal: If no outstanding shortage, reduce selection points proportionally."
translations.idiomatic: Clean accounts could earn reduced rotation points.

sentences.zh: 」敕：「路隨等所修《憲宗實錄》舊本，卻仰施行。

translations.literal: " An edict: "The old text of the Veritable Record of Xianzong edited by Lu Sui and others — restore and implement.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Lu Sui's Xianzong Veritable Record and recalled Huichang revisions.

sentences.zh: 其會昌新修者，仰並進納。

translations.literal: The Huichang newly revised version — all are to be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang revisions had to be surrendered.

sentences.zh: 如有鈔錄得，敕到並納史館，不得輒留，委州府嚴加搜捕。

translations.literal: If copies are found, on receipt of the edict submit them to the History Office; none may be kept — commission prefectures to search strictly."
translations.idiomatic: Copy-holders had to surrender texts to the History Office under search.

sentences.zh: 」以戶部侍郎、判度支崔龜從本官同平章事。

translations.literal: " Vice Minister of Revenue and acting finance commissioner Cui Guicong was Grand Councillor at his present rank.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guicong joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 銀青光錄大夫、門下侍郎，兼禮部尚書、同平章事韋琮為太子詹事，分司東都。

translations.literal: Silver-glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Rites, Grand Councillor Wei Cong was made Heir-apparent Mentor and assigned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cong went to Luoyang as heir-apparent mentor.

sentences.zh: 大中三年三年春正月丙寅，涇原節度使康季榮奏，吐蕃宰相論恐熱以秦、原、安樂三州及石門等七關之兵民歸國。

translations.literal: Dazhong 3, spring, first month, bingyin: Jingyuan military commissioner Kang Jirong memorialized that the Tibetan minister Lun Kongre brought the troops and people of Qin, Yuan, Anle, and the seven passes including Shimen to submit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 3's first month Kang Jirong reported Tibetans returning Qin, Yuan, and seven passes.

sentences.zh: 詔太僕卿陸耽往喻旨，仍令靈武節度使硃叔明、邠甯節度使張君緒，各出本道兵馬應接其來。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Master of the Stud Lu Dan to convey the imperial will; still order Lingwu commissioner Zhu Shuming and Binning commissioner Zhang Junxu each to dispatch troops of their circuits to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dan was sent to welcome the returnees while Zhu Shuming and Zhang Junxu provided escort troops.

sentences.zh: 乙太常卿封敖檢校兵部尚書，為興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies Feng Ao was made acting Minister of War, Xingyuan prefect, and Shannan West military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ao took Xingyuan and Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 三月乙卯，敕待詔官宜令與刑法官、諫官次對。

translations.literal: Third month, yimao: edict — awaiting-audience officials should take turns remonstrating after penal-law officials and remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao awaiting-audience officials were ordered into the remonstrance rotation.

sentences.zh: 銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、同平章事、監修國史、上柱國、汝南縣開國子、食邑五百戶周墀檢校刑部尚書、梓州刺史，充劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: Silver-glitter Grand Master, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, dynastic historian, Pillar of State, Viscount of Runan with five hundred households Zhou Chi was made acting Vice Minister of Punishments, Zizhou prefect, and Sword South East Chuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi was sent to Sword South East Chuan.

sentences.zh: 四月，以正議大夫、守中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿大學士、賜紫金魚袋馬植為太子賓客，分司東都；

translations.literal: Fourth month: Regular Grand Master, acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, Hall of Assembled Worthies academician with purple-gold fish Ma Zhi was made heir-apparent Guest of Honor at the eastern capital;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhi became heir-apparent guest at Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 以正議大夫、守御史大夫、上柱國、博陵縣開國子、食邑五百戶、賜紫金袋崔鉉可中書侍郎、平章事；

translations.literal: Regular Grand Master, acting Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, Viscount of Boling with five hundred households and purple-gold fish Cui Xuan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan joined the council;

sentences.zh: 正議大夫、行兵部侍郎、判戶部事、上柱國、钜鹿縣開國男、食邑五百戶、賜紫金魚袋魏扶可本官、平章事。

translations.literal: Regular Grand Master, acting Vice Minister of War and revenue commissioner, Pillar of State, Baron of Julu with five hundred households and purple-gold fish Wei Fu was Grand Councillor at his present rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fu also joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 五月，幽州節度使、檢校司徒、平章事張仲武卒，三軍以其子直方知留後事。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Youzhou military commissioner, acting Minister of Works, Grand Councillor Zhang Zhongwu died; the three armies made his son Zhifang know regent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu died; his son Zhifang became Youzhou regent.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，五色雲見於京師。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guiwei: five-colored clouds appeared in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Five-colored clouds appeared over the capital on guiwei.

sentences.zh: 敕：先經流貶罪人，不幸歿於貶所，有情非惡逆，任經刑部陳牒，許令歸葬，絕遠之處，仍量事官給棺櫝。

translations.literal: Edict: those previously exiled who died in exile — if the case was not wicked rebellion, they may petition the Ministry of Punishments and be permitted burial; in very distant places still grant coffins according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles not guilty of treason might be repatriated for burial.

sentences.zh: 康季榮奏收原州、石門驛藏木峽制勝六磐石峽等六關訖。

translations.literal: Kang Jirong memorialized recovery of Yuan prefecture and the six passes Shimen, Yizang, Muxia, Zhisheng, Liupan, and Shixia completed.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Jirong reported six frontier passes recovered.

sentences.zh: 邠甯張君緒奏，今月十三日暇復蕭關。

translations.literal: Binning's Zhang Junxu memorialized that on the thirteenth of this month Xia Pass was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Junxu reported Xia Pass recovered.

sentences.zh: 御史台奏，義成軍節度使韋讓于懷真坊侵街造屋九間，已令毀拆訖。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized: Yicheng military commissioner Wei Rang built nine houses encroaching on the street at Huaizhen Ward — already ordered demolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rang's illegal houses at Huaizhen were torn down.

sentences.zh: 敕于蕭關置武州，改長樂為威州。

translations.literal: Edict: establish Wu prefecture at Xia Pass; change Changle to Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu prefecture was founded at Xia Pass; Changle became Wei.

sentences.zh: 七月，三州七關軍人百姓，皆河、隴遺黎，數千人見於闕下。

translations.literal: Seventh month: troops and people of the three prefectures and seven passes — all remnant folk of He and Long — several thousand appeared below the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Hexi refugees presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 上御延喜門撫慰，令其解辮，賜之冠帶，共賜絹十五萬疋。

translations.literal: The Emperor went to Yanxi Gate to comfort them, ordered them to undo their braids, granted caps and belts, and altogether gave one hundred fifty thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong welcomed them at Yanxi Gate, gave Chinese dress, and granted one hundred fifty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 八月，鳳翔節度使李玭奏收復秦州，制曰：

translations.literal: Eighth month: Fengxiang military commissioner Li Pin memorialized recovery of Qin prefecture; rescript:
translations.idiomatic: Li Pin reported Qin recovered; a rescript followed.

sentences.zh: 九月辛亥，西川節度使杜忭奏收復維州。

translations.literal: Ninth month, xinhai: West Chuan military commissioner Du Xian memorialized recovery of Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Du Xian reported Wei prefecture recovered.

sentences.zh: 制曰：

translations.literal: Rescript:
translations.idiomatic: A rescript followed.

sentences.zh: 以起居郎庾道蔚、禮部員外郎李文儒並充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yu Daowei and Rites Bureau outer-section member Li Wenru were both made Hanlin academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Daowei and Li Wenru entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 十月辛巳，京師地震，河西、天德、靈夏尤甚，戍卒壓死者數千人。

translations.literal: Tenth month, xinsi: the capital earthquake — Hexi, Tiande, and Ling-Xia especially severe; garrison soldiers crushed to death numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: A capital earthquake killed thousands in northwest garrisons.

sentences.zh: 十一月，東川節度使鄭涯、鳳翔節度使李玭奏修文川谷路，自靈泉至白雲置十一驛，下詔褒美。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: East Chuan commissioner Zheng Ya and Fengxiang commissioner Li Pin memorialized repair of the Wenchuan Valley road — eleven post stations from Lingquan to Baiyun — an edict praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ya and Li Pin won praise for eleven new post stations on the Wenchuan road.

sentences.zh: 經年為雨所壞，又令封敖修斜谷舊路。

translations.literal: After a year rain destroyed it; Feng Ao was again ordered to repair the old Xiegu road.
translations.idiomatic: Rain wrecked the new road; Feng Ao rebuilt Xiegu.

sentences.zh: 以刑部侍郎韋有翼為御史中丞，以職方員外郎鄭處誨兼御史知雜。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishments Wei Youyi was made Censor-in-Chief; Bureau of Appointments outer-section member Zheng Chuhui was concurrent chief investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Youyi became censor-in-chief; Zheng Chuhui took investigating duties.

sentences.zh: 幽州軍亂，逐其留後張直方，軍人推其衙將周綝為留後。

translations.literal: Youzhou army mutinied, expelled regent Zhang Zhifang; soldiers made yamen officer Zhou Lin regent.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou mutinied and made Zhou Lin regent over Zhang Zhifang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，追諡順宗曰至德大聖大安孝皇帝，憲宗曰昭文章武大聖孝皇帝。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: posthumous titles — Shunzong as Great Sage of Perfect Virtue, Great Peace, and Filial Piety; Xianzong as Luminous Literary, Martial, Great Sage, and Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong and Xianzong received enlarged posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 初以河、湟收復，百僚請加徽號，帝曰：「河、湟收復，繼成先志，朕欲追尊祖宗，以昭功烈。

translations.literal: Earlier, because He and Huang were recovered, the hundred offices asked to add honorific titles; the Emperor said: "He and Huang recovered continue the former plan — We wish to exalt ancestors to display merit."
translations.idiomatic: When Hexi returned the court sought a reign title; Xuanzong preferred honoring ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」白敏中等對曰：「非臣愚昧所能及。

translations.literal: " Bai Minzhong and others replied: "This is beyond your servant's dull wit."
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong demurred.

sentences.zh: 」至是，上御宣政殿行事，及冊出，俯樓目送，流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor performed the rites at Xuanzheng Hall; when the document came out he leaned from the tower watching it depart, weeping and sobbing.
translations.idiomatic: At the enshrinement rite Xuanzong wept from Xuanzheng Tower.

sentences.zh: 崖州司戶參軍李德裕卒於貶所。

translations.literal: Yazhou registrar Li Deyu died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu died in exile at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 大中四年四年春正月，以追尊二聖，御正殿，大赦天下：「徒流比在天德者，以十年為限，既遇鴻恩，例減三載。

translations.literal: Dazhong 4, spring, first month: because of exalting the two sages, the Emperor held court in the main hall and proclaimed a great amnesty: "Exiles comparable to Tiande — ten years as the limit; now meeting great grace, reduce three years in general.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong 4 opened with a great amnesty cutting Tiande exiles' terms.

sentences.zh: 但使迴圈添換，邊不闕人，次第放歸，人無怨苦。

translations.literal: Only rotate replacements so the border lacks no men; release in sequence without popular bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: Border rotations were to spare manpower and bitterness.

sentences.zh: 其秦、原、威、武諸州、諸關，先准格徒流人，亦量與立限，止於七年，如要住者，亦聽。

translations.literal: For Qin, Yuan, Wei, Wu prefectures and passes — prior standard exiles — also set limits up to seven years; if they wish to remain, permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi exiles could serve seven-year terms or stay.

sentences.zh: 諸州府縣官如請工假，一月巳下，權差諸廳判官；

translations.literal: When prefectural officials request craft leave under one month, temporarily assign various bureau acting judges;
translations.idiomatic: Short craft leave could be covered by acting judges;

sentences.zh: 一月已上，即准勾當例，其課料等據數每貫刻二百文，與見判案官添給。

translations.literal: over one month follow the usual acting rule; deduct two hundred cash per string of salary for allowance and add to the acting case officer.
translations.idiomatic: Longer leave deducted salary strings for acting officers.

sentences.zh: 有故意殺人者，雖已傷未死、已死更生，意欲殺傷，偶然得免，並同已殺人條處分。

translations.literal: Intentional homicide — though wounded not dead, or dead then revived, intent to injure yet chance escape — all treated under the completed homicide article.
translations.idiomatic: Attempted murder with lethal intent was punished as completed homicide.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，皇女萬壽公主出降右拾遺鄭顥，以顥為銀青光祿大夫、行起居郎、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Second month: Princess Wanshou married Right Reminder Zheng Hao; Hao was made Silver-glitter Grand Master, acting Palace Attendant, and Commandant-consort.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Wanshou married Zheng Hao, now commandant-consort.

sentences.zh: 三月己卯，刑部奏：「監臨主守，應將官物私自貸使並貸借人，及以己物中納官司者，並專知別當主掌所由有犯贓，並同犯入己贓，不在原赦之限。

translations.literal: Third month, jimao: Punishments memorialized: "Supervisors who privately lend state goods or borrow in others' names, or substitute private goods for state intake — specialist clerks and foremen guilty of graft are the same as embezzlement, outside general amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: On jimao lending state goods for profit was excluded from amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: Assented.

sentences.zh: 以幽州節度副大使檢校工部尚書張直方為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Youzhou vice commissioner and acting Minister of Works Zhang Zhifang was made Left Gold Crow guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifang was recalled to the Left Gold Crow guard.

sentences.zh: 四月，敕：「法司用刑，或持巧詐，分律兩端，遂成其罪。

translations.literal: Fourth month, edict: "When law offices apply punishment, some hold crafty fraud, split statutes at two ends, and thus complete guilt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade legal pettifoggery.

sentences.zh: 既奸吏得計，則黎庶何安？

translations.literal: Once wicked clerks gain their scheme, how can the common folk be secure?
translations.idiomatic: The edict warned that trickery harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 自今後應書罪定刑，宜直指其事，不得舞文，妄有援引。

translations.literal: Henceforth when writing guilt and fixing punishment, point straight at the matter — no florid citations or false references."
translations.idiomatic: Judgments had to name the concrete offense.

sentences.zh: 」又刑部奏：「淮今年正月一日敕節文，據三月二十六日敕，竊盜贓至一貫文處死，宜委所司重詳定條目奏聞。

translations.literal: " Punishments again memorialized: "Per this year's first-month edict section and the twenty-sixth-day third-month edict — theft reaching one string cash is death — commission offices to review articles and memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: Punishments asked to revisit the one-string theft rule.

sentences.zh: 臣等檢校，並請准三月二十四日敕，竊盜贓滿三疋已上決殺，如贓數不充，量請科放。

translations.literal: Your servants checked and request following the twenty-fourth-day third-month edict: theft of three bolts or more — execution; if value insufficient, apply proportional release."
translations.idiomatic: They proposed death only for theft of three bolts or more.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: Assented.

sentences.zh: 七月丙子，大理卿劉蒙奏：「古者懸法示人，欲使人從善遠罪，至於不犯，以致刑措。

translations.literal: Seventh month, bingzi: Court of Judicial Review director Liu Meng memorialized: "Antiquity hung the law to show people, wishing them follow goodness and shun crime until none offend and punishments rest unused."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Meng urged engraved law codes for clerks.

sentences.zh: 准十月二十六日刑部侍郎高釴條疏，准勘節目一十一件，下諸州府粉壁書於錄事參軍食堂，每申奏罪人，須依前件節目。

translations.literal: "Per Vice Minister of Punishments Gao Xi's twenty-sixth-day tenth-month articles — eleven verified items — sent to prefectures to paint on registrar mess halls; each memorialized offender must follow those items."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xi's eleven articles were to be posted in mess halls.

sentences.zh: 歲月滋久，文字湮淪，州縣推案，多違漏節目。

translations.literal: Years lengthen, writing sinks away; prefectures in trials often miss items.
translations.idiomatic: Posted laws had faded from use.

sentences.zh: 今後請下諸道，令刻石置於會食之所，使官吏起坐觀省，記憶條目，庶令案牘周詳。

translations.literal: Hereafter send to all circuits orders to carve stone at assembly places so officials rising and sitting may view and remember — hoping dossiers will be thorough."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Meng ordered the articles carved on stone at assembly halls.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: Assented.

sentences.zh: 八月，刑部侍郎、御史中丞魏掞奏：「諸道州府百姓詣台訴事，多差御史推劾，臣恐煩勞州縣，先請差度支、戶部、鹽鐵院官帶憲銜者推劾。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Vice Minister of Punishments and Censor-in-Chief Wei Zhan memorialized: "When commoners of circuits sue at the tower, censors are often sent to investigate — your servant fears troubling prefectures; first request finance, revenue, and salt commissioners bearing censor titles investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhan wanted finance and salt commissioners to hear common suits.

sentences.zh: 又各得三司使申稱，院官人數不多，例專掌院務，課績不辦。

translations.literal: Each Three-Office commissioner stated office staff are few, usually devoted to office business — performance duties unmet.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners said their staffs were already overloaded.

sentences.zh: 今諸道觀察使幕中判官，少不下五六人，請於其中帶憲銜者委令推劾。

translations.literal: Now observation commissioners' staffs have no fewer than five or six judges — request those bearing censor titles be entrusted to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed using observation judges with censor titles instead.

sentences.zh: 如累推有勞，能雪冤滯，御史台闕官，便令奏用。

translations.literal: If through repeated investigation they clear wrongs, when the Censorate lacks officers memorialize them for appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Successful investigators could be promoted into the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: Assented.

sentences.zh: 九月，以朝請大夫、檢校禮部尚書、孟州刺史、河陽三城節度使李拭為太原尹、北都留守、河東節度等使。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Regular Grand Master, acting Minister of Rites, Mengzhou prefect, Heyang Three Cities military commissioner Li Shi was made Taiyuan prefect, northern capital regent, and Hedong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi took Taiyuan and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 幽州節度周綝卒，軍人立其牙將張允伸為留後。

translations.literal: Youzhou commissioner Zhou Lin died; soldiers made yamen officer Zhang Yunshen regent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lin died; Zhang Yunshen became Youzhou regent.

sentences.zh: 十月，中書侍郎、平章事魏扶罷知政事。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor Wei Fu ceased knowing administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fu left the council.

sentences.zh: 十一月己亥，敕：「收復成、維、扶等三州，建立已定，條令制置，一切合同。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jihai, edict: "Recovery of Cheng, Wei, and Fu prefectures — establishment fixed, regulations and arrangements all uniform."
translations.idiomatic: An edict unified rules for recovered Cheng, Wei, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 其已配到流人，宜淮秦、原、威、武等州流例，七年放還。

translations.literal: Exiles already assigned there should follow Qin, Yuan, Wei, and Wu exile precedent — release after seven years."
translations.idiomatic: Exiles in the new prefectures could return after seven years.

sentences.zh: 」以戶部侍郎、判本司事令狐綯為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: " Vice Minister of Revenue and acting head of the ministry Linghu Tao was made Vice Minister of War and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tao joined the council.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以華州刺史周敬復為光祿大夫、檢校左散騎常侍，兼洪州刺史、江南西道團練觀察使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Huazhou prefect Zhou Jingfu was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrent Hongzhou prefect and Jiangxi West circuit training-and-observation commissioner, granted gold-purple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jingfu took Jiangxi West with gold-purple.

sentences.zh: 大中五年五年春正月甲戌，制皇第七子洽封懷王，第八子汭為昭王，第九子汶為康王。

translations.literal: Dazhong 5, spring, first month, jiaxu: invested the seventh son Zhi as Prince of Huai, eighth son Rui as Prince of Zhao, ninth son Wen as Prince of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Three princes were enfeoffed on jiaxu.

sentences.zh: 敕兩京天下州府，起大中五年正月一日已後，三年內不得殺牛。

translations.literal: Edict both capitals and all prefectures: from Dazhong 5 first month for three years cattle may not be slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: A three-year cattle-slaughter ban began in Dazhong 5.

sentences.zh: 如郊廟享祀合用者，即以諸畜代。

translations.literal: Where suburban and temple sacrifice requires it, substitute other livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were to use other animals.

sentences.zh: 二月，戶部侍郎裴休充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: Second month: Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Xiu was made salt and transport commissioner for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu took the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 四月癸卯，刑部侍郎劉瑑奏：據今年四月十三日已前，凡二百二十四年，雜制敕計六百四十六門，二千一百六十五條，議輕重，名曰《大中刑法統類》，欲行用之。

translations.literal: Fourth month, guimao: Vice Minister of Punishments Liu Zuan memorialized: before this year's fourth-month thirteenth, two hundred twenty-four years, miscellaneous edicts six hundred forty-six categories, two thousand one hundred sixty-five articles — weighing severity, titled Comprehensive Categories of Dazhong Penal Law — desired to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zuan submitted the Comprehensive Categories of Dazhong Penal Law.

sentences.zh: 五月，以太原尹、河東節度使李拭為鳳翔節度使；

translations.literal: Fifth month: Taiyuan prefect and Hedong commissioner Li Shi was made Fengxiang commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi went to Fengxiang;

sentences.zh: 李業檢校戶部尚書、太原尹、北都留守，充河東節度使；

translations.literal: Li Ye was acting Minister of Revenue, Taiyuan prefect, northern capital regent, and Hedong commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye took Hedong;

sentences.zh: 守司空、門下侍郎、太原郡開國伯、食邑一千戶白敏中檢校司徒、同平章事邠州刺史，充邠寧節度觀察、東面招討党項等使；

translations.literal: acting Minister of Works, Vice Director, Baron of Taiyuan with one thousand households Bai Minzhong was acting Minister of Education, Grand Councillor, Binzhou prefect, Binning observation commissioner, and eastern Tangut campaign commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong took Binning and the Tangut front;

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎、判戶部事魏謩本官同平章事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue and acting revenue head Wei Mo was Grand Councillor at his present rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mo joined the council.

sentences.zh: 七月，宰相監修國史崔龜從續柳芳《唐曆》二十二卷上之。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Grand Councillor and dynastic historian Cui Guicong continued Liu Fang's Tang Calendar in twenty-two scrolls and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guicong presented twenty-two scrolls continuing the Tang Calendar.

sentences.zh: 八月，敕：「公主邑司擅行文牒，恐多影庇，有率條章。

translations.literal: Eighth month, edict: "Princess estate offices issuing documents on their own — fear much sheltering, violating regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Princess estates were forbidden to issue documents to prefectures.

sentences.zh: 今後公主除緣征封外，不得令邑司行文書牒府縣，如緣公事，令邑司申宗正寺，與酌事體施行。

translations.literal: Hereafter except for enfeoffment rites princesses may not have estate offices send documents to prefectures; for public affairs have the estate office report to the Court of the Imperial Clan and act after weighing the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Estate business had to route through the Imperial Clan court.

sentences.zh: 」沙州刺史張義潮遣兄義澤以瓜、沙、伊、肅等十一州戶口來獻，自河、隴陷蕃百餘年，至是悉復隴右故地。

translations.literal: " Shazhou prefect Zhang Yichao sent elder brother Yize to present household registers of eleven prefectures including Guazhou, Shazhou, Yizhou, and Suzhou — since He-Long fell to Tibet a hundred-plus years, now all Longyou old territory was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yichao presented eleven Hexi prefectures back under Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 以義潮為瓜沙伊等州節度使。

translations.literal: Yichao was made commissioner of Guasha and allied prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yichao became Hexi commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九月，敕：「條疏刺史交代，須一一交割公事與知州官，方得離任。

translations.literal: Ninth month, edict: "Spell out prefect handover — each public matter must be delivered to the knowing prefect official before leaving office."
translations.idiomatic: Prefects had to hand over every file before departure.

sentences.zh: 准會昌元年敕，刺史只禁科率官吏抑配人戶，至於使州公廨及雜利潤，天下州府皆有規制，不敢違越。

translations.literal: "Per Huichang 1 edict, prefects only forbid extorting clerks and pressing households; as for using prefectural offices and miscellaneous profits, all circuits have rules and dare not exceed.
translations.idiomatic: Huichang rules already barred extortion of clerks and households.

sentences.zh: 緣未有明敕處分，多被無良人吏致使恐嚇，或致言訟。

translations.literal: Because there was no clear edict, many wicked clerks intimidated or brought lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Without a clear edict clerks had bullied outgoing prefects.

sentences.zh: 起今後應刺史下擔什物，及除替後資送錢物，但不率斂官吏，科配百姓，一任各守州縣舊例色目支給。

translations.literal: From now on when prefects carry goods or after replacement send money — so long as they do not extort clerks or apportion to commoners — let each circuit keep old categories of payment.
translations.idiomatic: Outgoing gifts were allowed if the people were not squeezed.

sentences.zh: 如無公廨，不在資送之限。

translations.literal: If there is no public office, it is outside the send-off limit.
translations.idiomatic: Poor prefectures need not send parting gifts.

sentences.zh: 若輒有率配，以入己贓論。

translations.literal: If there is arbitrary apportionment, treat as embezzlement."
translations.idiomatic: Forced levies counted as graft.

sentences.zh: 」以正議大夫、兵部侍郎、諸道鹽鐵轉運使、上柱國、河東縣開國子裴休守禮部尚書，進階金紫；

translations.literal: " Regular Grand Master, Vice Minister of War, salt-and-transport commissioner, Pillar of State, Viscount of Hedong Pei Xiu was acting Minister of Rites, advanced to gold-purple;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu took Rites with gold-purple;

sentences.zh: 以前宣歙觀察使、太中大夫、檢校左散騎常侍裴諗權知兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: former Xuan-She observation commissioner, Grand Master of the Palace, acting Left Cavalier Pei Shen was acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shen acted as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十月己亥，京兆尹韋博奏：「京畿富戶為諸軍影占，苟免府縣色役，或有追訴，軍府紛然。

translations.literal: Tenth month, jihai: Jingzhao prefect Wei Bo memorialized: "Capital-region rich households are shadow-enrolled by armies to evade prefectural corvée; when sued, military offices clamor."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo protested army shadow-enrollment of rich households.

sentences.zh: 請准十二月敕，諸軍使不得強奪百姓入軍。

translations.literal: Request following the twelfth-month edict — army commissioners may not forcibly enroll commoners into the army."
translations.idiomatic: Armies were barred from forcibly enrolling civilians.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: Assented.

sentences.zh: 十一月，中書侍郎，兼吏部尚書、平章崔龜從檢校尚書估僕射、汴州刺史，充宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Personnel, Grand Councillor Cui Guicong was acting Minister of Works, Bianzhou prefect, and Xuanwu army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guicong took Bianzhou and Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 沙州置歸義軍，以張義潮為節度使。

translations.literal: Shazhou established the Return-to-Allegiance Army; Zhang Yichao was commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Return-to-Allegiance Army was founded at Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事姚康獻《帝王政纂》十卷；

translations.literal: Heir-apparent Mentor Yao Kang presented Imperial Governance Compendium in ten scrolls;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Kang presented ten scrolls of Imperial Governance.

sentences.zh: 又撰《統史》三百卷，上自開闢，下盡隋朝，帝王美政、詔令、制置、銅鹽錢穀損益、用兵利害，下至僧道是非，無不備載，編年為之。

translations.literal: also compiled Comprehensive History in three hundred scrolls from opening of the age through Sui — imperial good government, edicts, institutions, bronze, salt, coin, grain gains and losses, military advantage and harm, down to Buddhist and Daoist right and wrong — nothing omitted, arranged by year.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a three-hundred-scroll Comprehensive History.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒馮審奏：「文宣王廟，始太宗立之，睿宗書額，武后竊政之日，改篆題『大周』二字，請削之。

translations.literal: Director of the Directorate of Education Feng Shen memorialized: "The Temple of the Literary King — Taizong first built it, Ruizong wrote the plaque; when Wu Zetian usurped she changed the seal script to the two characters Great Zhou — request they be cut away."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shen asked to remove Wu Zetian's "Great Zhou" plaque.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: Assented.

sentences.zh: 十二月，盜斫景陵神門戟，京兆尹韋博罰兩月俸，貶宗正卿李文舉睦州刺史，陵令吳閱岳州司馬，奉先令裴讓隋州司馬。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: thieves chopped the spirit-gate halberds of Jing Mausoleum — Jingzhao prefect Wei Bo fined two months' salary; demoted Director of the Imperial Clan Li Wensun to Mizhou prefect; mausoleum magistrate Wu Yue to Yuezhou registrar; Fengxian magistrate Pei Rang to Suizhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Mausoleum halberds were stolen; several officials were punished.

sentences.zh: 是歲，湖南大饑。

translations.literal: That year Hunan suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan starved that year.

sentences.zh: 大中六年六年春正月戊辰，以隴州防禦使薛逵為秦州刺史、天雄軍使，兼秦、成兩州經略使。

translations.literal: Dazhong 6, spring, first month, wuchen: Longzhou defense commissioner Xue Kui was made Qinzhou prefect, Tianxiong army commander, and Qin-Cheng frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Kui took Qin and the frontier command.

sentences.zh: 二月，右衛大將軍鄭光以賜田請免租稅。

translations.literal: Second month: Right Guard great general Zheng Guang asked tax exemption for granted fields.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guang sought tax exemption on imperial grant land.

sentences.zh: 宰相魏謩奏曰：「鄭光以國舅之親，賜田可也，免稅無以勸蒸民。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Wei Mo memorialized: "Zheng Guang as the emperor's maternal uncle may receive fields, but tax exemption cannot encourage the common folk."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mo refused tax exemption for the imperial uncle.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「一依人戶例供稅。

translations.literal: " Edict: "Follow the common household rule for tax supply."
translations.idiomatic: An edict taxed the grant like ordinary land.

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 三月，隴州刺史薛逵奏修築定成關工畢。

translations.literal: Third month: Longzhou prefect Xue Kui memorialized completion of Dingcheng Pass construction.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Kui finished Dingcheng Pass.

sentences.zh: 四月丁酉，敕：「常平義倉斛斗，每年檢勘，實水旱災處，錄事參軍先勘人戶多少，支給先貧下戶，富戶不在支給之限。

translations.literal: Fourth month, dingyou, edict: "Ever-Normal and charity granary grain — inspect yearly; where flood or drought truly strike, the registrar first surveys household numbers and issues to poor households first; rich households are outside issuance."
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal grain was to reach poor households first in disasters.

sentences.zh: 」以禮部尚書、諸道鹽鐵轉運等使裴休可本官同平章事。

translations.literal: " Minister of Rites and salt-and-transport commissioner Pei Xiu was Grand Councillor at his present rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu joined the council.

sentences.zh: 五月，敕：「天下軍府有兵馬處，宜選會兵法能弓馬等人充教練使，每年合教習時，常令教習。

translations.literal: Fifth month, edict: "Where military prefectures have troops, select men skilled in military law and archery as training commissioners; in annual drill seasons keep drilling and then report to the Ministry of War."
translations.idiomatic: Training commissioners were ordered for all garrisoned prefectures.

sentences.zh: 仍于其時申兵部。

translations.literal: The edict closed with the closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」御史台奏：「諸色刑獄有關連朝官者，尚書省四品已上、諸司三品已上官，宜先奏取進止。

translations.literal: " The Censorate memorialized: "Criminal cases touching court officials — for Ministry of State officials of fourth rank and above and other offices of third rank and above, first memorialize for imperial decision."
